text: Hillingham? Or home? It's all the same to my horse. He won't go past the churchyard after dark. Not for money.

speaker: player
text: Why does he refuse?

speaker: Cabman
text: He sweats, sir, and sidles. The cart-horses are the same. I think there's something in the place that animals know.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: A white figure drifts between the tombs, tall, with something in her arms. She stops. She comes on again, her face turned from us.

speaker: player
text: Hold still. Let her come nearer.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Wait. Wait. A little more...

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: She is within ten paces. The Professor slides the lantern open, and the light falls on a lovely face, sweet and pure, and blood on her chin and on her white gown. It is Lucy.

speaker: player
text: Hold your ground, and open the lantern fully.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Lucy! In the name of God, stand!

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: She flings the child on the ground, snarls like a cat, and glides past us to the tomb. The Professor puts the crucifix between her and the vault, and she is gone in a second... through the lock-plate.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: The child is alive, breathing heavily; the bruise on its throat is no more than a prick. We must take it where the police will find it. We cannot answer questions.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: The child sleeps, curled into my coat. The wound is the twin of the others.

speaker: player
text: Carry it away to the lane.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: The lamp, the bench, the policeman's beat. A child laid here will be found in ten minutes.

speaker: player
text: Lay the child on the bench, ring the policeman's bell and slip behind the hedge.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: We wait, hearts hammering, behind the hedge. The constable's lantern swings. 'Hullo! What's this?' He gathers it up. 'Well, there's one safe.' We go.

speaker: Narrator
text: The next afternoon

speaker: Constable
text: Found a child, gentlemen, on the bench. Breathing, thank God. I'll take it to the station. Did you see anyone?

speaker: player
text: Nothing, constable. A good night to you.

speaker: player
text: We came across the Heath on a doctor's errand.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Look at her, John. Not corpse, not alive. See how red the lips are, how the flesh is fuller than when she died.

speaker: player
text: Look at her lips.

speaker: player
text: Look at her teeth.

speaker: player
text: Look at the coffin lead.

speaker: player
text: Professor, we must bring Arthur before tonight.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: Redder than in life, and a fresh fleck of blood at the corner: not hers, the Professor says. It has come from some child.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: The canine teeth are sharper than they were. I lift her lip. No living woman's mouth is made so.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: There is no sign of the lead being touched since it was sealed; she is in and out of it as she chooses. Mist or moonbeam, I do not know. But she goes, and she returns before dawn.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Quite so. She must be put to rest, and he must see it done. Arthur will not like it. But he must be brought, or he will hate us for ever. Come, to Hillingham.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: John. Professor. You come again, and say nothing, and look at me like physicians at a bed. Lucy is dead. What more is there to say?

speaker: player
text: Arthur, trust the Professor. He has asked for nothing for himself.

speaker: player
text: We believe she is not at rest. She walks.

speaker: player
text: Come with us at midnight, and see for yourself.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: I trust you, John. But this... for God's sake, say what you want.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: She... walks? You will drive me mad, Seward. If you were any other man, I would knock you down.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Lord Godalming, I ask a great thing: I ask your hand to do a thing which will break your heart, and in time mend it. If you refuse, I shall not blame you. But if you consent, you will be the one who frees her.

speaker: player
text: Arthur, it is the kindest service you can do her.

speaker: player
text: Arthur, if you refuse, I shall do it myself.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: Very well. I have loved her, and I will not leave her in the hands of strangers. I will come.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Count me in. I've shot grizzlies, but I never shot a thing I couldn't see. I'll hold the guns, and Art holds the stake.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Doc, I'll tell you plain: I've seen a lot in the wild, and nothing strikes me as hard as a man who loved a girl and is told to go and see her in her coffin.

speaker: player
text: He will bear it, Quincey. He has you.

speaker: player
text: Do you believe the Professor?

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: He's got a Texan's word. I'll be at his back, and if a lady comes at him, I'll hold him, not shoot.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: That Dutchman knows more than any three doctors. If he says dead folk walk, I'll give him a rifle and a long night.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Here is what is needed. A little of the Host from Amsterdam, which I have by Indulgence from the Pope. The Host and the putty make a seal that no spirit passes.

speaker: player
text: Take the Host.

speaker: player
text: Professor, please knead the Host into the putty for me.

speaker: player
text: Professor, I have the ash wood but I cannot work it. Will you sharpen the stake?

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Good. Take also the missal. You will need the prayers. And bring the garlic: a mouth full of it, when the time comes.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Watch my hands. A little here, a little there, until the putty is like wax. Behold: a seal against the Un-Dead.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Give me the knife. So, a good point; we char the end to harden it. Here: a stake that will not splinter.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: She comes down the path between the yews, a child in her arms, red lips parted. The moon bathes her golden hair. 'Arthur,' she murmurs. 'Come to me. My arms are hungry for you.'

speaker: player
text: Hold Arthur back by the arm.

speaker: player
text: Raise the crucifix.

speaker: player
text: Stand your ground and say nothing.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: Lucy! My God, Lucy... Her voice... Seward, she is calling me...

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Stand back, all! The cross! In the name of God, I command you!

speaker: Van Helsing
text: She has been driven back, and she cannot return to her coffin while the Host is on the door. She is wild with hunger and must go in before dawn. Shall we let her pass?

speaker: player
text: Remove the strips and let her go to her coffin.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: The strips come away. She flows through the gap like smoke, and we hear a faint sigh within the vault. Now we wait out the day, John. Tonight we finish this.

speaker: Narrator
text: 30 September. The next evening.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Friends, we do now the work which God demands. Attend, for the order matters, and I will not repeat it in the vault. What is the first step with the Un-Dead?

speaker: player
text: Garlic in the mouth first, then the stake.

speaker: player
text: Behead first; the heart can wait.

speaker: player
text: The stake through the heart, the prayers, then the head, then the garlic in the mouth, and last the coffin sealed.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: No, friend. The stake first: it frees her soul. The head and the garlic follow. Think again.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Exactly so. The stake, driven by the hand that loved her; the prayers; the head; the garlic; the seal of lead. Arthur, you will stand here. Quincey, at the door. John, the knives. We wait for her to rise; she will be restless at the sunset.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Let us pray for the dead, as the Church has ordered. 'Out of the depths I have called to Thee, Lord...' Amen.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: It is the oldest ritual I know, and the least understood. When the Professor closes the book, the body is quiet, and the tomb seems to breathe out.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: Seward, Professor... she looked at me. At the last she smiled at me, as she used to. It was Lucy. And she is at peace.

speaker: player
text: She is at peace, Arthur. You did what only love could do.

speaker: player
text: We mourn her, but she mourns no longer.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: I thank God that He gave me the strength. And I thank you for letting me keep the last of her. From now, if there is anything I can do against the creature that did this, I am in.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Friends, the work of tonight is done, but we are at the first of many. Someone made Lucy what she was, and that one is in England, in London. He is strong, and old, and patient. Will you stand with me, John, Arthur, Quincey? Will you hunt the creature that did this?

speaker: player
text: To the last, Professor.

speaker: player
text: I will stand with you. Where do we begin?

speaker: Van Helsing
text: In your asylum, John, where there is a library and a madman who has known the master. I leave tonight for Amsterdam to find what I need. When I return, we hold council of war.

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT V: THE COUNCIL OF WAR

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Dr. Seward. I would rather be of no use at all than of the use I am. But I will give you everything I have.

speaker: player
text: Mr. Harker, may I have your journal? Mrs. Harker will copy it.

speaker: player
text: How is Mrs. Harker?

speaker: player
text: The Carfax papers, Mr. Harker?

speaker: player
text: What do you make of this house?

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Here. Every shorthand page, from the Golden Krone to the castle chapel. Mina will read it, and I cannot. Not yet. Take it, Doctor, and let her put it in type.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: She is braver than I. She wants to be of use, always. I fear she will insist on being of too much.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: It is a good house, Doctor. But the wall at the end of your garden... I have seen that sort of wall before.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Mr. Hawkins left them to me. The deeds to Carfax, a bunch of heavy keys, and a letter I once carried to a Count. Here are the keys, and a letter of authority over Lord Godalming's seal. The carriers, the agents: they will talk to you, if you show them this.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Doctor Seward, may I ask a great favour? I have a typewriter, and I have a head for order. Let me copy everything in the case. Jonathan's journal, your phonograph diary, my Whitby papers, the Professor's notes.

speaker: player
text: Mrs. Harker, I shall be glad of your help.

speaker: player
text: Where should I begin?

speaker: player
text: What will you do with them?

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Thank you. Here are my own papers: my Whitby diary and the cuttings from the Dailygraph. The rest I shall ask for as I need them. Bring them to the room off the library, and I will type each one. Then we shall see what they say together.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Four things I need: Jonathan's journal, which he keeps; your phonograph cylinders, Doctor, which I think you keep locked; the Professor's memorandum; and my Whitby papers, which you have. And if Mr. Renfield keeps notes, I should like to see them too. The typewriter is in the little room west of the library.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: A story told in six voices is a story nobody has heard. Typed in order, it may speak.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Friend John! The mountain has come to Mahomet. The Harkers are here, and the work begins. Madam Mina has the eye of a lawyer and the heart of a nurse.

speaker: player
text: Professor, Mrs. Harker asks for your memorandum.

speaker: player
text: What do you think of the case?

speaker: player
text: Is the Host safe in your bag?

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Ah, yes! My memorandum. It tells of Miss Lucy, and of what I think, and of what I do not yet dare to think. Give it to her, and tell her to be gentle with my English.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: There is a man, or a thing, in London. He has fifty boxes of earth, and we cannot kill him until we know where all of them lie. When Madam Mina has finished her typewriting, we shall be wiser. And then we hold the council.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Seven wafers, from my own priest in Amsterdam. Not a toy, not a charm. A thing to be used with care, and in faith. Do not waste a crumb.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: The whole story, in threads and pins. Each paper I have typed is pinned in its place, and I try to make them agree. What shall I ask the papers?

speaker: player
text: Where does the Count lie in London?

speaker: player
text: How did he come from Transylvania?

speaker: player
text: Why does Renfield know him?

speaker: player
text: What can be done against him?

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Jonathan wrote that fifty boxes were brought from the castle chapel. The Doctor's cylinders say that Renfield screams loudest from the window that looks over the wall. And Mr. Hawkins sold the Count a house on the other side of that wall. He rests at Carfax, among his boxes, in the old chapel.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: The Demeter put into Whitby in the storm with a dead crew and a great dog that leapt ashore. Jonathan's boxes were aboard her, fifty of them. The dog was the Count. Then the boxes went to London by rail, consigned to Billington of Whitby and forwarded by the carriers.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Doctor Seward noted that Renfield grows violent when the night is clear, and eats the flies and sparrows with an increasing greed, 'to take their life into his own'. Each turn corresponds to the Count's visits. He is the Count's pawn, and may be the Count's door.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: He needs his native earth to rest. He cannot enter a house unasked. He fears the crucifix, garlic, the Host. If every box of earth is made unfit for him, he will have nowhere to lie by day. That is what we must do: find every box, and sanctify every one.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Whitby is where Lucy first met him, but he does not rest there. There is no box in that churchyard. Look again at Jonathan's pages.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: A madman, Doctor Seward calls him. But no madman keeps a record that matches the Count's movements. Look again at the cylinders.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Yes. It is all one story, and now I can say it plainly: the Count lies at Carfax, in the fifty boxes, and the fifty boxes must be found and sanctified. I will take it to the Professor.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: I have given the Professor the typescript. He wishes us all to meet at the long table. I think it is a council, Doctor, and I think I am afraid that I shall be asked to leave it.

speaker: player
text: You have earned a seat, Mrs. Harker.

speaker: player
text: Is there anything that troubles you?

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Thank you. I do not mean to be a burden. But if I am in the dark, I fear I shall be a greater one.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: A dream, only. A great white mist about the window. I woke, and the garlic wreath on the sill had curled, as though it, too, felt something. Pray set it at my window, Doctor, if you can find a reason.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Friends! Madam Mina has done what no man of us could do. She has made the story one. Now I must tell you what I know, which is what none of you wish to hear. Sit, and listen, and do not laugh.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Ask, and I will answer. You may ask in any order. When you know enough, we shall settle the matter of Madam Mina.

speaker: player
text: What is it that we hunt?

speaker: player
text: How can he be harmed?

speaker: player
text: Why does he need the boxes of earth?

speaker: player
text: Can he enter this house?

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: The Nosferatu does not die like other things. He has the strength of twenty men; he can command the wolf, the rat, the owl, the bat, the moth; he can come on moonlight as mist, as dust. He casts no shadow and no reflection. And he feeds on blood, and those who feed him become his.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: In the daylight he is powerless. He cannot cross running water save at ebb or flow of the tide. The crucifix, the garlic, the wild rose, the Sacred Host: all these he must obey. And the stake through the heart and the sword to the head will give his body peace.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: He is bound to his native earth. He must rest in it by day, or he withers. That is why he brought fifty boxes from Transylvania. If we can make each unfit for him, in sanctified ground he cannot lie. We find the boxes. We hallow the earth. It is a work of days, but it is a work we can do.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: He may not enter unless he is invited. That is why he needs a door. That is why a man like Renfield is dangerous. A lunatic does not know what an invitation is, and the Count will give him a reason to say yes.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina has read every paper we have. She has the best brain in the house. She is also the woman whose friend he took, and the woman whose husband he tormented. I think she has a right. But she is delicate. What do you say?

speaker: player
text: Agreed. We keep no secrets from her.

speaker: player
text: Think of the danger to her.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: I have thought of it. But a woman kept in the dark by love is a woman in greater danger than a woman who knows. Think again.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Then we are six, and God help us. Tomorrow, to Carfax, the chapel, the boxes. Mr. Harker has the keys. Take the Host, take the crucifix, take the lamps. Let Lord Godalming's dogs go before us. And let us all swear, here, on this table, to put an end to this thing.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Friend John. We stand on the edge of a long road. Ask me what you will.

speaker: player
text: What do we do now, Professor?

speaker: player
text: How should the Host be used?

speaker: player
text: A ward for Mrs. Harker's room?

speaker: player
text: I am out of the Host, Professor.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: First Carfax, the chapel. There lie twenty-nine boxes, or so I judge. Each must be sanctified with a crumb of the Host. Go with the keys from Harker. Beware the rats: the Count is a master of them. Then, when we have counted what we found, we shall know how many are elsewhere. Then the carriers, the ledgers, the agents.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: A crumb upon the earth in each box, with the true intent of the heart. There are five stacks in the chapel; I count one wafer for each. Do not waste it on one box when a stack will do. And remember, we have use for it elsewhere.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Yes. The garlic wreath at the window, the crucifix on the sill. They are not proof against him, but they will tell us if he has come. Do it quietly. Madam Mina must not think we mistrust her sleep.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Then take another. There is one more in the pyx. Be careful with it: they are not easily come by.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: Seward. I have my terriers in the yard, a good rope, and a very bad conscience. I wish to end this thing, for Lucy's sake.

speaker: player
text: Lord Godalming, might I have a length of rope?

speaker: player
text: How are you bearing up, Art?

speaker: player
text: What of your dogs?

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: Take it. Good Sussex hemp. It has hauled many a fox from its earth.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: I think of her every day, and then I think of what she became, and I do not know which thought is worse. Mina is a fine woman. I shall protect her.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: Three terriers, hard as nails. If the Count's rats come, they will meet something that bites back.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Doc. I have a Winchester in my room and a bowie knife under my coat. Say the word, and I'll shoot at anything that moves after dark.

speaker: player
text: Quincey, I am told you carry the purse.

speaker: player
text: What do you make of the Professor?

speaker: player
text: What do you make of this whole business?

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Sure thing. Three sovereigns. Pay for a clerk's silence, a carter's thirst, and keep a spare. In this town gold talks louder than a judge.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: He's the first man I met who looks at a ghost the way my father looked at a bear. Calm. Practical. I'd follow him anywhere.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: I've seen more of the world than most. Never believed in witches. Now I believe in everything.

speaker: Renfield
text: Doctor! Dr. Seward! I must speak with you. Not of the flies, nor the spiders, but of myself. Of what is coming.

speaker: player
text: What is troubling you, Renfield?

speaker: player
text: Tell me again about the Master.

speaker: Renfield
text: Let me go, Doctor! Let me go home. I am not safe here. He is near, nearer than ever, and he will want something. I cannot refuse him and live. I cannot obey him and be saved.

speaker: player
text: Tell me what you fear. I will listen.

speaker: player
text: I cannot release you. Quiet, or I will call the attendants.

speaker: Renfield
text: Then I am lost! Then I am his! No! NO!

speaker: Renfield
text: Thank you, Doctor. I am sorry. He promised me lives, thousands of them, if I would be his. He has come before, in the mist. He will come again. If he asks me in, I... I do not know what I shall do. Keep him from my window. Keep him from hers.

speaker: Renfield
text: He is no master of mine. He is a tyrant, a tempter. He showed me a swarm of rats. He said they would be mine, and I should have an endless supply of lives. All I had to do was say 'Come in.' I said nothing. Doctor, I said nothing.

speaker: player
text: Swear that you will not invite him.

speaker: player
text: If he comes, will you call out?

speaker: Renfield
text: I swear it, Doctor. On the flies. On my own life, which is not much of a stake. But I am afraid I am a weak vessel.

speaker: Renfield
text: I will scream till the roof comes down. But I fear the roof is not the thing he needs. He needs a door, and I am one.

speaker: Renfield
text: Keep it off me, Doctor! Not for me. For her window. Garlic the lady's window and there is not a cloud that can cross it. But he may find another way.

speaker: Renfield
text: Doctor... Doctor, my back... I cannot... lips...

speaker: player
text: Who did this, Renfield?

speaker: Renfield
text: That is better. Thank you, Doctor. I must tell you quickly. While I can.

speaker: Renfield
text: He came through the mist. I had not asked him in, but he came. And I knew what he meant to do, and I begged him to spare her. He laughed. Then he took me up and broke me against the floor like a child's toy. Doctor, he is going to the lady. Now. This minute.

speaker: player
text: Where? Which room?

speaker: Renfield
text: The room... of the Harkers. Go! GO! Tell her... tell her I was not wholly his...

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: He is dead. Poor Renfield. He tried to be a man at the end. I will see to it that he is buried with the dignity he never had in life.

speaker: Simmons
text: Evenin', Doctor. He's been quiet today. Quiet's worse. He writes in that book of his, columns of numbers, day and night.

speaker: player
text: What numbers?

speaker: player
text: Has anyone visited him?

speaker: Simmons
text: Flies, sir. Spiders. Sparrows. He ticks each one off. Says they're the 'lives', and he's collecting a hundred for the one big life.

speaker: Simmons
text: Not as I've seen, sir. But the window... I have heard a sound on it more than once. Like a bat at the glass.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: The tall clock stands at ten. The house is quiet, and quiet in this house is rarely rest.

speaker: player
text: What have I yet to do?

speaker: player
text: Not yet.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: Mina's records, the council, Carfax, the carriers, the trace to Piccadilly, and a word with Renfield. When all are done, we can rest for a night, and perhaps be wiser.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: I locked the library, doused the lamps, and went to the wards. I do not know why. Something in the house had changed.

speaker: Narrator
text:
Night of 3 October. Purfleet.

A scream in the dark. A pool of blood. The Count has come.

speaker: Old gardener
text: Evenin', sir. That wall's older than the house. Folks say Carfax was a monastery, once, and the chapel's older still. Nobody goes in. Nobody comes out.

speaker: player
text: Has anyone been over the wall lately?

speaker: player
text: The chapel door. Is there a key?

speaker: player
text: I need oil, wood and cloth for torches.

speaker: Old gardener
text: I've seen lights, sir, at night. And I've seen a great dog sitting on the wall, with eyes like coals. I don't go that end any more.

speaker: Old gardener
text: The old caretaker, God rest him, was afeard of thieves. Hid the chapel key somewhere in the grounds where a dog could not dig and a child could not climb. Under a stone, or in a well, or maybe in a gatepost. Look about, sir.

speaker: Old gardener
text: Oil's in the barrel by the shed. Ash-wood stacked by the stove. And Mrs. Billing's washing, I daresay, has a spare strip or two.

speaker: Cabman
text: Cab, sir? Town in the hour. Anywhere you like, sir, and no questions, save the fare.

speaker: player
text: Have you carried a foreign gentleman lately?

speaker: player
text: Not just yet.

speaker: Cabman
text: Aye, a tall thin gent, ancient, with a white moustache and a fine black coat. Carried a box under his arm like a child's coffin. Paid me in gold, he did, and never so much as blinked. Bit of a cold fish. The horse near bolted.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: I sold him this place. Or helped to. I drew up the deed and sealed the packet that put the Count in the very house he dreamed of. Now I come as his enemy.

speaker: player
text: Mr. Harker, the chapel key?

speaker: player
text: Shall we go in?

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: The deeds mention that the old caretaker hid it in the park, near a stone feature of some kind: a post, a cross, a well. I have looked at the house; I should not like to go further without the chapel key in hand.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Not before we have the key. And the Professor says rats may be abroad. Hold your lamps high, Doctor.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Here it is, friend John. Here is where he sleeps. The Count's house of dead earth. If we do this right, he will have no bed in England tonight.

speaker: player
text: What of the rats?

speaker: player
text: How shall we cleanse the boxes?

speaker: player
text: I am out of the Host, Professor.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: The Count commands them. They will come when we move toward the earth. Hold your lamps, hold your ground, and keep the dogs close. They are only rats, friend John. Rats are afraid of men with lamps and resolve.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Five stacks, by my count. Six boxes in four of them, five in the last: twenty-nine in all. A crumb of the Host upon each stack, with the intent of the heart. It is enough. It will not be pleasant, and it will not be quick, but it is the work we came for.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: There is one more in the pyx. Take it, and God forgive me if I have miscounted.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: The count is easy, if we are patient. I have kept the tally from the castle in my head: fifty boxes, I counted them sleeping and wakeful, and I will never be wrong.

speaker: player
text: How many do we see here?

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Five stacks. By the chalk on the wall, twenty-nine boxes. But there were fifty in the castle chapel, and fifty on the Demeter. So twenty-one are elsewhere.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Twenty-nine boxes, and all are clean. The Count can no more lie here. But where are the other twenty-one? He has scattered them across London, I am sure of it. The carriers, Doctor. There is a ledger somewhere in London that remembers every box.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: A trail is a chain: one link leads to the next. Carriers, then the man who carried, then the man who sold the house. Where shall we begin?

speaker: player
text: Where do I start?

speaker: player
text: What have we learned?

speaker: player
text: What am I missing?

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Carter, Paterson & Co. They are the carriers, and the Hawkins letter will open the office door even if it will not open the ledger. Then, whoever carried the boxes. And lastly the house-agents. A man who buys a house in cash leaves a name somewhere.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: That depends what we have done. Smollet's ledger shows six boxes to Mile End and six to Bermondsey. Bloxam knows where the nine went, I suspect. And the house-agents must know whose house it is.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Keys, mostly. And patience. The Count paid cash for everything. A man who pays cash is a man who hates a written record, and I have never known one to leave none.

speaker: Street boy
text: Penny for a poor lad, sir? I know every court and alley between here and the river.

speaker: player
text: Do you know a white-moustached old gentleman?

speaker: Street boy
text: Coo, sir. 'Sam Bloxam, Korkrans, 4, Poters Cort, Bartel Street, Walworth.' Who writes like that? It don't make sense. What's it supposed to say?

speaker: player
text: Poter's Cort, off Bartel Street.

speaker: player
text: Potter's Court, off Bartel Street, Walworth: Corcoran's, number four.

speaker: player
text: Sam Bloxam is a made-up name.

speaker: Street boy
text: Never heard of no Poter. Try again, guv.

speaker: Street boy
text: Sam Bloxam's real enough. Drinks at the 'Are and 'Ounds. It's the writing that's daft.

speaker: Street boy
text: That's it! Potter's Court, Corcoran's, down the alley by the barrel, sir. Sam Bloxam lodges there. Good luck, and a penny would not go amiss.

speaker: Street boy
text: A gent with a white moustache and a hat pulled low? Walked up to the big stone house with the bow window in Piccadilly, he did. Carried a box up the steps himself. One hand. Gave me a shiver.

speaker: Mr. Smollet
text: Business hours, sir. State your errand. I can't show our book to every gentleman who walks in off the street.

speaker: player
text: I am inquiring after fifty boxes of earth, consigned to Carfax.

speaker: player
text: About that ledger entry...

speaker: Mr. Smollet
text: Boxes of earth, is it? Aye, we carried the like. But it's a confidential book, sir. I'd need good reason.

speaker: Mr. Smollet
text: A letter's a handsome thing, sir. But a letter's not a ledger. My memory has been poor of late. A bit of grease might clear it.

speaker: Mr. Smollet
text: Constable? On what charge? Hauling boxes? Be off with you, sir, or I'll fetch him myself.

speaker: Mr. Smollet
text: Ah, well. Sovereign talks, sir. Here: I'll copy the entry for you. Six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town. Six more to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey. And the nine that went to a gentleman in Piccadilly, that's Sam Bloxam's work. Here's his direction. My own spelling is a little on the poor side, mind.

speaker: Mr. Smollet
text: I have told you all I know, sir. And I'd thank you not to mention my name outside.

speaker: Thomas Snelling
text: Zzz... Eh? Who? Boxes? Aye, boxes. Dirty. Heavy. Smelt like a churchyard. The old gent that bought 'em lifted one hisself. One-handed. I'm tellin' ye, sir, I'm a sober man.

speaker: player
text: Where did he take them?

speaker: Thomas Snelling
text: Chicksand Street, Mile End... and a place in Bermondsey... and that big stone house in Piccadilly. Ask Sam Bloxam. He had the cart. Zzz...

speaker: Sam Bloxam
text: Who wants Sam Bloxam? If it's about that Hackney debt...

speaker: player
text: Tell me about the nine boxes.

speaker: player
text: The house in Piccadilly...

speaker: Sam Bloxam
text: Nine boxes? Don't know what you mean, guv. Memory's gone a bit foggy. Might come back with a bit of coin.

speaker: Sam Bloxam
text: Well, now. Nine boxes of earth, heavy as sin. An old gent with a white moustache, strong as a horse, took us to a stone house with a bow window and high steps. Near a big white church, beyond the Junior Constitutional Club. A torn 'To Let' board. I forget the number, guv, but a groom in the mews will know it. Number 347, I'd say, but don't swear to it.

speaker: Sam Bloxam
text: I've told you all. Go careful. That old gent was no ordinary old gent.

speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
text: Good day, sir. How may we serve you?

speaker: player
text: I am enquiring after 347 Piccadilly.

speaker: player
text: About the Piccadilly keys...

speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
text: I am afraid our clients' affairs are strictly confidential, sir.

speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
text: Sir! This is a respectable house. Please put that away.

speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
text: I must ask you to leave, sir, or I shall call Mr. Candy.

speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
text: Lord Godalming? Of Ring? Oh, I beg your pardon, sir. The buyer was a Count de Ville, who paid in cash and wished the house kept quiet. A foreigner, very old, very strong. I would not have liked to cross him. Here are the keys, sir. And I would say, sir: if you do mean to enter, take company.

speaker: Mr. Candy's clerk
text: You have the keys, sir. I hope you find what you seek.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: Jonathan lies on his back, face flushed, breathing heavily like one in a drugged sleep. I shake him. Nothing.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: In the moonlight through the yellow blind: a tall, thin man in black, his face waxen, his eyes red. His left hand grips both of Mina's wrists. His right holds her head against his open breast, where a bleeding wound drips. Her mouth is at it. On the bed, Jonathan lies in a stupor.

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: The wreath lies trampled on the floor. It did not keep him out. Only an invitation could, and he had that already.

speaker: Count Dracula
text: Fools. Do you think you can strike me? I who have commanded armies when your fathers were babes?

speaker: Count Dracula
text: You think yourselves so wise, all of you. Your girls are mine, and through them you, and others, shall be mine. The sheep are in my hands. Yet before I go, I shall have her again; and again.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: The Count drops the girl and turns on us. He is a hawk, a stoat, a wolf. Van Helsing steps forward with an envelope. 'Back!'

speaker: Dr. Seward
text: He cowers. Further and further we advance with crucifixes lifted. A bar of moonlight crosses his face and he grows grey, then thin, then a pale mist under the door. We hear the whining of the wind. He is gone.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Unclean! Unclean! Even the Almighty shuns my polluted flesh! I must bear this shame upon my forehead until the Judgment Day!

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina. This is the Sacred Host. Forgive me.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Doctor Seward. I am awake, and I am whole, and I am afraid to look in a glass.

speaker: player
text: How do you feel, Mrs. Harker?

speaker: player
text: May I see the mark?

speaker: player
text: Is there anything I can do?

speaker: Mina Harker
text: I feel him. Like a cold wind with a taste. When the sun rises or sets I seem able to follow him a little way, wherever he is. The Professor says it may be our only road to him. I pray God it is not also his to me.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: I would rather you did not. It is the size of a florin, red as a coal. Jonathan weeps when he looks at it. The Professor says it will fade when the Count dies, and not before.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Finish the boxes. Every one you destroy is a day gained. And promise me that you will not keep me in the dark, whatever the Professor thinks best.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Friend John, he has tasted her, and she him. That is a link we cannot cut. But it may serve us. He is not omnipotent. He fears us, you have seen it.

speaker: player
text: What now, Professor?

speaker: player
text: We need more of the Host.

speaker: player
text: I am out of the Host, Professor.

speaker: player
text: How is Madam Mina?

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Piccadilly, with the keys that Harker got from the agents. Nine boxes, or eight, if he has taken one. Then, if the Count's keys come into our hands, the houses in Mile End and Bermondsey. We shall find him leaving, or arriving. Either way, we strike.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: I wrote to Amsterdam as soon as I arrived. This morning my priest sent four more. Piccadilly will need two, Mile End one, Bermondsey one. Take them, friend John.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Then take another. There is one more in the pyx.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: She is stronger than she knows. She asked me to keep nothing from her, and I shall obey, God help me. But she must rest, friend John. She must rest.

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: Eight boxes, Professor says. The ninth the Count has taken, or perhaps he sleeps in it. We sanctify the two stacks, and we wait. If he comes, he must come through us.

speaker: player
text: How do you feel, Jonathan?

speaker: Jonathan Harker
text: I have not slept since the night he took her. I do not mean to sleep until he is dead.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Two stacks, friend. A crumb on each. Then we wait at the door. He comes here to see to his property, and we shall be waiting.

speaker: player
text: I am out of the Host.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Good. He will think twice at the threshold. Perhaps once is enough for us.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Take another. We cannot be short of it.

speaker: Count Dracula
text: So. The sheep have found the wolf's lair. You are clever, you English, with your keys and your agents. But you came too late, and you leave too soon.

speaker: Count Dracula
text: Do you think a bauble stops me? I have lived when your fathers' fathers were dust. Stand aside!

speaker: Count Dracula
text: Ha! Hold him, men! I'll not fight in a doorway.

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: The Count's key opened the Mile End lock like butter. Six boxes, in a coal-cellar. I thought I should feel triumphant. I only feel tired.

speaker: player
text: A crumb on the stack, then?

speaker: Arthur Holmwood
text: One wafer, one stack. Do it with the right heart, the Professor says. I shall try to think of Lucy.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Last of the lot, Doc. Last house, last stack. Then there's only the one with the Count.

speaker: player
text: How many boxes remain?

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Twenty-nine at Carfax, eight at Piccadilly, six at Mile End, six here: forty-nine. One left. The Count's got it somewhere, and himself in it.

speaker: Quincey Morris
text: Forty-nine down, one to go. The sun is setting. Let's get back to Purfleet; Mrs. Harker will be waiting.

speaker: Narrator
text:
Evening of 4 October. Purfleet.

Forty-nine boxes cleansed. One remains.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina, you said the link may serve us. Let us try it. At sunrise and at sunset the Count is at his weakest and his closest. Will you let me?

speaker: player
text: What does she mean, Professor?

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Darkness. Everything is dark... lapping water... a creaking of wood... a rope drawn taut... above me, feet. Cold. So cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sunrise, 5 October. Purfleet.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: A bell, dull and distant. Hawsers. Men calling, and a cry from the deck. 'We are going, we are going.' He is awake, Professor. He knows I am listening. He is so very near, and so very far.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sunset, 5 October. Purfleet.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Think, friend. Water lapping. Wood creaking. A rope pulled taut. Feet above. A bell. 'We are going.' What is the Count's box? Where is he?

speaker: player
text: He lies in the Bermondsey cellar still.

speaker: player
text: He is aboard a ship. We must learn her name: wire Lloyd's.

speaker: player
text: The Czarina Catherine, bound for Varna.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: No. Bermondsey has no lapping water, and the box there is clean. Think of the sounds again.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Good. Lord Godalming has the ear of Lloyd's. A telegram will come. When it does, tell me.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Yes. The telegram says the Czarina Catherine cleared the Thames this morning for Varna. Water, wood, rope, the bell: a ship, and one eastbound. He is running home with his last box. Lord God, what a woman you are, Madam Mina.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: The Professor wants me to try the link. I am afraid, but I would rather be afraid and useful than safe and idle.

speaker: player
text: You are braver than any of us, Mrs. Harker.

speaker: player
text: What does it feel like?

speaker: Mina Harker
text: I do not feel brave. But it helps to be told.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: Like standing at the edge of a dark river, with the other bank hidden. I can hear it, but I cannot see.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: The Czarina Catherine: a slow ship to Varna. We go by rail to Paris, thence the Orient Express to Varna, and wait on the quay for the ship to come in. We shall be there before her.

speaker: player
text: Who goes?

speaker: player
text: And Madam Mina?

speaker: player
text: I am out of the Host, Professor.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Lord Godalming, Mr. Morris, Dr. Seward, Mr. Harker, and myself. Five good men, and a ship's passage of rope, wood, and faith.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: She is not to come. Not this time. She has done more than any of us, and the Count has her link. If she is near him, he has her. If she is far, she is free. We shall tell her this at the last, for her own peace.

speaker: player
text: She will not agree to be left out.

speaker: player
text: It is a hard thing, but for her safety.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: She has taken one wound for us. I will not let her take another. We say nothing of the plan, friend John. Nothing.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Good. Then it is settled. I will make out the passage. Let each man gather what he needs.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Crucifix, stake, hammer, Host. Without these we go to our graves. Do you have them all?

speaker: player
text: Crucifix, Host, stake, hammer: all here.

speaker: player
text: Not yet.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Then we are ready. Go and speak with Madam Mina. She is waiting. And friend John, be kind.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Take another. We must not be short of it where we go.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: They have decided. I overheard the Professor with Lord Godalming. They mean to go without me. It is for my safety, they say, and I have not the heart to refuse. And I do not mean to stay behind.

speaker: player
text: Let them go. I shall wait, and watch the link.

speaker: player
text: Not yet. Let me think.

speaker: Professor Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina, I beg you. It is for your sake. The Count has the claim on your blood. We go to cut it. Stay safe here.

speaker: Mina Harker
text: They stand in the hall with their kits, the five of them: Jonathan, Arthur, Quincey, Dr. Seward, and the Professor in his shabby coat. I kiss Jonathan. I press the Professor's hand. They go. I watch the cab out of sight, and feel the line in my blood quiver, as though the Count himself were looking back.

speaker: Narrator
text:
5 October, evening.

The party leaves Charing Cross for Paris, the Orient Express, and Varna, to wait for the Czarina Catherine. Mina remains behind.

speaker: Harbour master
text: Another Englishman, and another question about the Czarina Catherine. She is not in my book, sir, and no berth is kept for her.

speaker: player
text: When was she last heard of?

speaker: player
text: What ships go astray between the Straits and Varna?

speaker: player
text: Thank you. [Leave]

speaker: Harbour master
text: The Dardanelles, the fourth of October, by the telegraph. A slow brig, Roumanian flag, owners in Galatz. Eleven days is long, even for a slow brig.

speaker: Harbour master
text: Ships from the Straits make Varna by the cape, or, if the weather is foul and the captain a Roumanian, they run north for the Danube mouth and Galatz. Nobody tells a Roumanian where to go. If I wanted a ship that would not arrive, I should look at the Danube.

speaker: Greek sailor
text: You look for the Czarina? Ach, I would not wish to find her. A fog stood off Kaliakra three nights back, and it moved against the wind.

speaker: player
text: What do you mean, against the wind?

speaker: player
text: Have a drop of brandy.

speaker: Greek sailor
text: I mean a fog does not sail upstream, sir. This one did. My mate saw a ship go into it, and it closed behind her like a door. We made the sign and rowed for shore.

speaker: Greek sailor
text: God bless you. A man who offers brandy is a man who knows a bad sea. I tell you, sir: keep a wreath of garlic at the hatch and a candle in the cabin.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina, the sun is near the horizon; this is the hour. Friend John has the watch, Jonathan the pencil. Are you willing?

speaker: player
text: I am ready, Professor.

speaker: player
text: What do the trances tell us, Professor?

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Look into my hand. Sleep, Madam Mina. Where are you?

speaker: player
text: What do you hear, Madam Mina?

speaker: Mina
text: I hear water. It is lapping, and rushing, and lapping again. Cool and dark.

speaker: player
text: What else do you hear?

speaker: Mina
text: Wood creaks. Rope strains. There are feet above me, going to and fro, and a bell. Everything is straining as if it wished to be free.

speaker: player
text: Do you feel anything beneath you?

speaker: Mina
text: I am rising and falling. We are moving. The ship is moving, and I am not in her. I am somewhere dry and still, and I feel the motion of her as one feels a heart beat in another's chest.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Enough, enough. Wake, Madam Mina. [Her eyes open. She remembers nothing, and I write everything down.]

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Consider it as the lawyer, the doctor, the metaphysician, all three. Water laps and rushes. A ship creaks and moves. Where is she, friend, and what must we do?

speaker: player
text: She is in the harbour. We should wait on the quay.

speaker: player
text: She is out on the open sea and will reach Varna any day now.

speaker: player
text: He knows we are at Varna. He will not come where we wait; she may make for the Danube and Galatz, and we must watch the wires.

speaker: player
text: I cannot say. [Leave]

speaker: Van Helsing
text: No. In port a ship does not move. Madam Mina feels motion, hears rushing water. And the harbour master has no berth marked for her. Think again.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Perhaps, perhaps. But Lloyd's had her at the Straits eleven days ago. A ship of that kind would be here already. Something else holds her. Read the Lloyd's report again and ask the harbour master where a ship may go besides Varna.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Ah, friend John, that is thinking. He learned through her trance that we are here, and then he cut that thread. Any port but this will do him. We watch every wire, and when the news comes we move.

speaker: Narrator
text: We waited. The days of October dragged by, a trance at every sunrise and sunset, and every day a telegram from Lloyd's: 'Czarina Catherine, not reported.' At last, on the twenty-eighth...

speaker: Mina
text: I am quite well. Do not look at me so. I have rested and eaten and I am sorry to be a burden.

speaker: player
text: You asked us for a promise, Mina.

speaker: player
text: Mina, you know the railways. How do we reach Galatz?

speaker: Mina
text: I did, and I ask it again, with the sun high and my head clear. If I turn, Arthur, John, all of you: let me not live as that thing. Kill me. Jonathan shall read the Burial Service.

speaker: player
text: I swear it, Mina.

speaker: player
text: I... cannot say it.

speaker: Mina
text: You must, dear friend, and soon. It is the one favour I ask. I will ask it every day of this journey until you say it.

speaker: Mina
text: Thank you. Now I am no longer afraid; or no more than I can bear. God keep you all.

speaker: Mina
text: You forget that I am the train fiend. I always keep the Bradshaw. At what hour does the one train for Galatz leave, do you think?

speaker: player
text: In the afternoon, I suppose.

speaker: player
text: Let me consult the Bradshaw. [Open it]

speaker: player
text: I do not know. [Leave]

speaker: Mina
text: No, dear friend. Look it up before you guess. It is on the table.

speaker: Mina
text: Half-past six in the morning, there is only one train. It arrives in the afternoon. Tell the Professor, and tell Jonathan to sleep.

speaker: Jonathan
text: I have been at this knife an hour. It was good in Ghoorka hands; it is not good in mine. A dull blade is an insult to what it must do.

speaker: player
text: What does it have to do, Jonathan?

speaker: player
text: Is there a whetstone about?

speaker: Jonathan
text: Cut through the throat of a man who is not a man, and do it clean. I shall be nearest. I mean to be the one.

speaker: Jonathan
text: A fine stone would do wonders. There are chandlers on the quay. If you find one, put it in my hand. I cannot rest until this thing is right.

speaker: Quincey
text: Well, Doc. We're a long way from the Staked Plains, and the buffalo here wears horns and trousers. Anything on your mind?

speaker: player
text: You swore first, Quincey. Why?

speaker: player
text: Have you cartridges to spare?

speaker: Quincey
text: Because a Texan don't ask a lady twice. Because I loved Lucy, and have lost her, and here's a woman I'd lose my right arm for. Sit down, Doc; this country gets under the skin.

speaker: Quincey
text: Always. Here, take a handful. The Winchester wants feeding, and so do you.

speaker: Arthur
text: Lloyd's wires every morning: 'Czarina Catherine, not reported.' It makes me want to take a boat and meet her in the Bosphorus. Is there anything you need from me?

speaker: player
text: What of the ship's owners? We cannot open the box without their consent.

speaker: player
text: Is there money for a long chase?

speaker: Arthur
text: The shippers' agent is at Lloyd's. Courteous, closed, a hard man to move. He'll not consent to open a case on the strength of a good face. You'll want a reason, not a truth. And, I suspect, a compensation.

speaker: Arthur
text: Whatever it takes. I have the purse. I'll not spare a sovereign for my own comfort, but anything that gets us to him faster, I'll buy.

speaker: Porter
text: Good day, sir. No post, sir. I only wait in case.

speaker: player
text: Any telegram for Lord Godalming?

speaker: Porter
text: Yes, sir! Just this minute, from Lloyd's. 'Czarina Catherine reported entering Galatz at one o'clock to-day.'

speaker: Lloyd's clerk
text: Lord Godalming. The usual, sir? 'No news.' I am sorry. It is the same for every ship in the Black Sea. You may consult the register if you wish.

speaker: player
text: What is the last entry for the Czarina Catherine?

speaker: Lloyd's clerk
text: Passing the Dardanelles, the fourth of October. Roumanian-flagged brig, hull and rigging sound. Since then, nothing; not a signal, not a sighting. If the sea had her we should have a report of wreckage by now.

speaker: Shippers' agent
text: Lord Godalming, is it? You have asked after a consignment aboard the Czarina Catherine. What, precisely, would you have of me?

speaker: player
text: Open the box. It contains a dead man that is not dead.

speaker: player
text: A friend of mine has had a thing stolen, and I think it is in that ship.

speaker: player
text: Allow me to show my appreciation for the owners' trouble.

speaker: player
text: The owners will surely forgive some delay for the sake of a friend. Here is something for their trouble.

speaker: Shippers' agent
text: You will forgive me if I have the door held open. I have heard many reasons for opening cargo. That was the first to make me afraid for your health.

speaker: Shippers' agent
text: Stolen? That is a serious matter. If the thing is yours, a friend's, I should be glad to see it restored. But the owners will want assurance, and some consideration for delay. Return when you can promise both.

speaker: Shippers' agent
text: You mistake me, my lord. I do not take money for nothing. Give me a reason and then we shall discuss recompense.

speaker: Shippers' agent
text: Ah. Now we understand each other. I will give you a paper to the Captain and another to our man at Galatz. They will open the box in your presence, and any claim the owners have will be settled between gentlemen.

speaker: Harbour master
text: The Czarina Catherine? In last night on the tide without a pilot. Moored in the fog, and not a soul on deck till dawn. I have never seen a ship come up the Danube so still. What is your interest, gentlemen?

speaker: player
text: Did anything leave the ship?

speaker: player
text: Who handles her cargo?

speaker: Harbour master
text: A long box, by the first light. Men from Hildesheim's lighter took it ashore. And a very tall thin man in a big coat watched from the wharf-head; I thought he was a foreigner. When I looked again he was gone.

speaker: Harbour master
text: Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, the agents. Their clerk is on the quay by the crates. But the Captain, Donelson, he has the papers. A Scot, and a rough one. You would do well to carry a letter from his owners.

speaker: Clerk
text: Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, gentlemen. What can I do for you? The Captain is aboard; I cannot say more than he allows.

speaker: player
text: I have the Captain's bill of lading. Who is the consignee?

speaker: player
text: What can you tell me about the cargo?

speaker: Clerk
text: A bill, signed. Yes, I see; Hildesheim, Burgen-strasse 16. He is cautious, sir, and fond of coin. Take this note from my masters; he will see the name of Mackenzie & Steinkoff and perhaps be less difficult.

speaker: Clerk
text: A single long box, sir, consigned from Varna. Fifty pounds' worth of earth, they said. I thought it a joke. Hildesheim paid the carriage with an English note and signed for it in his own hand.

speaker: Captain Donelson
text: Ye'll be the gentlemen from Varna. I have the shippers' letter. Aye, I can see it. Well, ye may ask what ye like, but dinna expect me to tell ye a pretty story.

speaker: player
text: Tell me about the voyage, Captain.

speaker: player
text: Show me the bill of lading.

speaker: Captain Donelson
text: From the day we cleared the Bosphorus the fog came on, and it stayed. Nine days, nae a breath of wind, but we made a sea-mile an hour more than any ship I've seen. The men would na touch the wheel; I stood it myself.

speaker: player
text: What of the box?

speaker: Captain Donelson
text: A long box brought aboard at Varna, by an old man in a great coat. The men crossed themselves at the sight of him. When we sailed they asked to throw it overboard, and I laid a handspike to the loudest. If the Deil did have any luggage aboord the ship, I'm thinkin' it was nane ither than that same!

speaker: Captain Donelson
text: Here it is. Hildesheim's the name, Burgen-strasse 16. And ye'll find a Slovak called Skinsky has the box now. Go canny, gentlemen. That old man was no man.

speaker: Sailor
text: [He makes the sign of the horns, and mutters in Roumanian.] Strigoi. We carried a strigoi. I would not have sailed if I had known.

speaker: player
text: What did you see on the voyage?

speaker: Sailor
text: A man who was not there. A tall pale man at the rail at night. We found a mate gone one morning, with a neck like a torn flower. The Captain said he fell. I know what fell.

speaker: Deckhand
text: I scrub, sir, I scrub. It does not take out the smell. Not blood: earth. Earth from a grave. You smell it in the hold.

speaker: player
text: Where did the man go when you docked?

speaker: Deckhand
text: He went into the box, sir. I was at the rail at dawn and I swear he went in like water in the sand. Then the lid shut. Then Hildesheim's men came.

speaker: Hildesheim
text: You are English gentlemen. I like English gentlemen; they are always in a hurry, and a hurry is a thing that has a price. What is it that you want?

speaker: player
text: I come from Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, with their letter.

speaker: player
text: The box taken ashore this morning. Where is it?

speaker: player
text: A Slovak called Skinsky has the box. Can you confirm it, in writing?

speaker: Hildesheim
text: Ah. They are good clients. That makes it easier, although not free. What information do you want?

speaker: Hildesheim
text: I had it of a gentleman who signed 'de Ville.' A letter, a fee, and delivery. If I tell, the gentleman is no longer a client. And for a man in my line, a client lost is a thing to be paid for.

speaker: Hildesheim
text: Skinsky is a Slovak, his men take cargo up the river by boat. I gave him the box. For a signature and thumbprint I would put it in writing, but the paper costs.

speaker: player
text: Pay him from the purse.

speaker: player
text: I have no money. [Leave]

speaker: Hildesheim
text: Excellent. Here is my receipt, with the Slovak's mark. You will find him at the churchyard if he lives. I would not trouble to look in the taverns. Good day, sir. It was a pleasure doing business.

speaker: Priest
text: A poor Slovak, Petrof Skinsky. They found him at dawn at the churchyard wall. The people say wolves, but we have no wolves in the town. God have mercy on his soul.

speaker: player
text: The wound is too clean for a wolf, Father.

speaker: player
text: Did he have anything on him?

speaker: player
text: May I see the coat, Father?

speaker: Priest
text: You have seen it, then, and you are not afraid to say it. A wolf tears. This was cut, as if by a single great tooth. I have said nothing to the police. They would think me mad. I laid the dead man's coat on the wall; no one has asked for it.

speaker: Priest
text: Only a coat. His widow came for it, but she has not the heart to wear it. I laid it by the wall until someone should ask.

speaker: Priest
text: Take it, my son. Something is sewn in the lining. A slip of paper. A boat, and Slovaks, and the river by night. I cannot read what it means. You may. God go with you.

speaker: Neighbour
text: He was a good man, Petrof, though he drank. He took money from a foreigner and a big box on a boat. Then in the night he came home white and he said: 'Do not open the door.' In the morning he was in the lane.

speaker: player
text: What did the foreigner look like?

speaker: player
text: Where did the boat go?

speaker: Neighbour
text: Tall. Thin. A long white moustache. A voice like honey. He lifted the great box alone, and Petrof, who could carry a barrel, could not help but stare.

speaker: Neighbour
text: Up the river, by night, with Slovaks at the oars. Petrof said they would not stop till the mountains.

speaker: Mina
text: Jonathan sleeps and the others rest, so I am putting all of it in order. Hildesheim, Skinsky, the Captain's tale; the facts want only a clear head. Help me think it through.

speaker: player
text: Begin the memorandum.

speaker: player
text: Read it back to me.

speaker: player
text: We have not yet gathered everything. [Leave]

speaker: Mina
text: He cannot go by sea again; the ship is here, and watched. How would he carry his box from Galatz to the Borgo Pass? By road?

speaker: player
text: By road, in a cart.

speaker: player
text: By rail.

speaker: player
text: By water.

speaker: Mina
text: A cart takes days, and the horses will not abide him; I remember Jonathan's driver. And the receipt names a boat, Skinsky's slip says 'by night'. No, not the road.

speaker: Mina
text: Every station is a risk: clerks, officials, customs. The Count must be seen. The slip says a boat. It is not rail.

speaker: Mina
text: By water. Skinsky's slip, Hildesheim's receipt, the neighbour's account: all speak of a boat, a Slovak crew, and the river by night. It remains: which river?

speaker: player
text: The Pruth, to the north.

speaker: player
text: The Sereth, then a tributary to the mountains.

speaker: Mina
text: The Pruth leads away from the Pass. No, the Sereth has the Bistritza, and the Bistritza runs from the Borgo Pass itself, by Jonathan's journal. It must be that.

speaker: Mina
text: Yes. Up the Sereth, then into the Bistritza, near Fundu. It is the only river that ends at the Count's door. I shall pencil the route on a map.

speaker: Mina
text: The memorandum: Galatz, the Sereth, the Bistritza, the Borgo Pass. The map is on the table. Now Professor Van Helsing must hear it.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Friends, Madam Mina has given us the road. I think we must divide. A launch on the water, riders on the bank, and Madam Mina and myself by rail and carriage to the Pass. Let us make arrangements.

speaker: player
text: Who goes where?

speaker: player
text: Jonathan will not agree to his wife's going.

speaker: player
text: We are ready. Let us set out.

speaker: player
text: Not yet. [Leave]

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Lord Godalming and Jonathan take the steam launch up the Sereth. Dr. Seward and Mr. Morris ride the bank. We go by the 6.30 and the carriage. At the Pass we meet. Each must have what he needs: the dealer in the hall has the launch, the horses, the flag, the lamp.

speaker: Mina
text: Jonathan, I am safest with the Professor. The Count's will no longer holds me, and it is I who can lead the Professor through the castle. You know it. Trust me.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Then go, God keep you. Madam Mina will write. And, friends: remember that it is the sun that is our friend. He is helpless between sunrise and sunset. Let us not miss it.

speaker: Narrator
text: 30 October, night. The party divides. Lord Godalming and Jonathan board the steam launch 'Mina' and head upstream into the dark. Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris ride the bank. Van Helsing and Mina take the morning train.

speaker: Dealer
text: Lord Godalming has told me you require a steam launch and good horses within three hours. It is possible. For a consideration.

speaker: player
text: Buy the launch, a lamp and a flag.

speaker: player
text: Is there a map or chart I might have?

speaker: Dealer
text: A small steam launch with a boiler of English make, and an electric lamp such as the English navy uses. And here is a Roumanian flag. Fly it at Fundu and the village will think you officials. She is called, I believe, the Mina.

speaker: Dealer
text: The lady at the table has a map. She is the only one who has drawn the river as it is, not as the Roumanian government pretends.

speaker: Jonathan
text: I will not take my eyes off the water. We must overtake him before the mountains. Every boat on this river is a suspect.

speaker: player
text: You are worried for Mina.

speaker: player
text: Do you feel steady?

speaker: Jonathan
text: She is with the Professor, and the Professor is a good man. And she has asked me to go. But I would give ten years to be in that carriage with her.

speaker: Jonathan
text: When I am working, yes. When I think of that castle, no. I escaped it once. I swore I would never see it again. Now I am running to it. Strange, is it not?

speaker: Slovak boatman
text: [He fell to his knees in the light of the lamp, and prayed.] Do not harm us, gentlemen. We have done nothing. We are poor men.

speaker: player
text: Have you seen a boat with a great box and Szgany at the oars?

speaker: player
text: Stand up, man. Where is your boat bound?

speaker: Slovak boatman
text: Yes, gracious sir! Before dusk, a boat with eight men at the oars, a great box in the middle, and in the stern a tall dark man in a cloak. He did not look at us but I felt his eyes. They turned in at the river mouth on the left, up the Bistritza. They did not stop.

speaker: Slovak boatman
text: Downriver to Galatz with timber, sir. We saw lights and heard a shot and we hid. Please do not tell the Count's men we spoke.

speaker: Raftsman
text: [He crossed himself twice.] If you hunt what I think you hunt, you have courage. I have seen the lights of his boat at the fork, with wolves howling on the bank. They did not harm him.

speaker: player
text: Which fork?

speaker: Raftsman
text: Where the Bistritza comes into the Sereth, past Fundu. A man who knew the river would go there. And a man with wolves for guards would not need to ask.

speaker: Farmer
text: She struck the rock, your boat. I saw it from the field. Sit by the fire. You will need a night and a plank to mend that seam, and horses for the road.

speaker: player
text: Can you spare two horses and a saddle?

speaker: player
text: How bad is the river ahead?

speaker: Farmer
text: For this gold, six. Take the grey and the bay. The road follows the river. Go with God, and do not stop when the wolves howl.

speaker: Narrator
text: 2-3 November. The launch is mended, but the river will carry us no further. Lord Godalming buys horses; he and Jonathan will ride for the mountains. And on the bank, Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris have been in the saddle three days.

speaker: Farmer
text: Rapids for three versts. A rock in each, and the water black. A launch with a sound keel may pass. A launch with a broken one may not.

speaker: Jonathan
text: A plank sprung; no more. We need a splint, rope to bind it and canvas to stop the water. We must be on the river by nightfall.

speaker: Arthur
text: If we cannot mend her we shall ride. But the river is faster, and I'll not give up the Mina while she floats. A spar for the splint, a rope, some canvas; I know what to do.

speaker: Innkeeper
text: Gentlemen, you are not from here. News is a thing I sell. Bread and brandy first, and then we talk.

speaker: player
text: What news from the river?

speaker: player
text: Have you a sledge?

speaker: Innkeeper
text: Last night a launch passed, with an English lamp. And the day before, a boat with Szgany, a box, and wolves following on the bank. Both turned up the Bistritza.

speaker: Innkeeper
text: A sledge? There will be snow by dark. Take mine. Two horses, a bearskin and sleigh-bells I won't take back. For gold.

speaker: Quincey
text: Doc, I've followed a trail in sleet for three days and I never felt so tired or so awake. Mina is ahead, God willing. What's the good word?

speaker: player
text: We must hurry. The sun sets at five.

speaker: player
text: I fear for Arthur and Jonathan on the river.

speaker: Quincey
text: Then we hurry, and Mina does what she has to. I told her once that I'd see the thing through, and I will. Tell the horses.

speaker: Quincey
text: The launch has a lamp and a flag; Arthur's no fool. Let's keep our heads and we'll all meet at the Pass.

speaker: Landlady
text: [She makes the sign of the horns at my forehead, then flushes and pats my hand.] Forgive an old fool, little lady. Here, a bite for the road. Garlic in the soup, and garlic at the door.

speaker: player
text: Why the garlic?

speaker: player
text: Is the road to the Pass safe?

speaker: Landlady
text: Because of what lives up there, lady. In the old castle. You are young, and your husband's journal is no answer. Wear it. Carry it.

speaker: Landlady
text: The road to the Pass is safe by day. By night it belongs to wolves, and to him who calls them. Be across the Pass before dark, or camp in a ring.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina, we must have a carriage, horses, and furs. The road above Veresti is rough and the nights are cold. I have gold; let me use it.

speaker: player
text: Buy the carriage and horses.

speaker: player
text: What do you fear most on this road?

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Done, and well done. Four horses, a stout carriage, and a driver who will take us to the last village and not a yard further. Now furs and provisions, and your letter to Jonathan.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Not the wolves, Madam Mina, nor even the Un-Dead. I fear that you will be tired, and the Count will find the thread he has lost in you. We must be careful of your sleep.

speaker: Peasant woman
text: [She crosses herself and thrusts garlic into my hand.] Go home, lady. Not past the cross. Dracula's wolves do not eat; they only wait.

speaker: player
text: Which road leads to the castle?

speaker: player
text: Thank you for the garlic.

speaker: Peasant woman
text: None you want. The wide road goes to the valley; the narrow road to the shepherd's hut; the old by-road goes to the Pass, and from there to the devil's house. Your man's book knows it better than I.

speaker: Peasant woman
text: Wear it at your throat, and when you sleep, keep your hands crossed. God keep you.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Madam Mina, we come to three roads. I know that you have read Jonathan's journal many times. Which of these is the one he took?

speaker: player
text: The wide cart-road, to the left.

speaker: player
text: The narrow track, to the right.

speaker: player
text: Let me consult Jonathan's typescript.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: That one goes down into the valley, Madam Mina. Jonathan's coach went up. Read again.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: That goes to a shepherd's hut. Jonathan did not meet a shepherd. Think of the cross and the bend.

speaker: Mina
text: Here: 'the road went up, then down, then up again under tall pines, past a cross at the bend.' It is the old by-road, the grass-grown one beyond the shrine. I know it. Have not my Jonathan travelled it, and wrote of his travel?

speaker: Van Helsing
text: Then it is that road. Madam Mina, I must ask you to stay close and to take sleep when you can. Something is changing in you, and I do not want it to take you unawares. First, the wolves; they are waiting.

speaker: Mina
text: Professor, I feel the snow under me but I do not feel the cold. I only feel that I am drawn to that castle, as a bird to a snake. I am so tired.

speaker: player
text: Step into the ring, Mina.

speaker: player
text: The night is coming. Let us wait.

speaker: player
text: What do you feel, Mina?

speaker: Mina
text: I am in. I did not think I could be so glad of a few handfuls of dust. Keep the fire high, Professor. Keep it high.

speaker: Mina
text: Then we wait. Whatever comes, I shall not leave this circle; I give you my word, and I give it with all the strength I have left.

speaker: Narrator
text: The sun went down behind the mountain. The cold deepened. The horses began to scream, and from the mist beyond the firelight came a whisper of women's laughter...

speaker: Mina
text: I feel him in the distance, as one feels a draught under a door. He is not far, and he is not alone. Do not leave me, Professor.

speaker: The sisters
text: Come, sister. Come to us. Come! Come! Why will you not come? We are so cold and the snow is so soft. He sent us, as he sends all his lovelies. Come!

speaker: The sisters
text: Brave sister! You are not afraid of us? We are not afraid of you. Give us your hand, only your hand, through the line. One kiss. One only.

speaker: The sisters
text: The Master, our dear Master. He is close. He is racing the sun. Come, and be one with us, and he will be so glad.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: [He raised the Host between her hand and the line.] Madam Mina! You cannot. The circle will hold, but not if you will it open. Look at me, look at the Host.

speaker: Mina
text: [I draw my hand back. The sisters laugh, and wolves begin to howl all around the ring. They cannot enter; but they will try until dawn.]

speaker: Van Helsing
text: [She is lovely beyond description. She seems to breathe, and the colour of her lips is the colour of life. A thing in me longs to kneel and kiss her, and I know what that is: not love, but a trap.]

speaker: player
text: Look away. Use the crucifix.

speaker: player
text: Think of Mina, waiting in the circle.

speaker: player
text: Bend to her lips.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: [I hold the crucifix before my eyes. The spell shrinks. She is a thing, not a woman; a beautiful corpse that has fed on the living.]

speaker: Van Helsing
text: [Somewhere across the snow, Mina cries out my name, and I know the cry is real, or I have imagined it. It cuts the charm like a knife. My hand steadies, my eyes clear.]

speaker: Van Helsing
text: [I am a hair's breadth from her lips when something in my mind screams: 'You are drowning!' I wrench myself back, shaking, drenched in sweat. I must not look so long.]

speaker: Mina
text: Professor, the castle is behind us, the three are at peace, and I am myself again, or nearly. But I feel the Count draw near, as the tide draws in. Can you see anything?

speaker: player
text: Stay in the ring. I shall look from the rock.

speaker: player
text: They come. We shall see the end of it, Madam Mina.

speaker: Mina
text: Yes. I shall be quiet. But be careful not to fall; the sun is almost down, and I would not have you late.

speaker: Van Helsing
text: [The glass shakes in my hand.] They are racing for the sunset. We may be too late. God's will be done!

speaker: Narrator
text: 6 November, an hour before sunset. Four men ride on the plain: Jonathan, Lord Godalming, Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris. Before them, a wagon flogged by Szgany whips, and the dying sun.

speaker: Arthur
text: Jonathan, we have them. I will take the right flank with Seward and rifles at the ready. We pick the first man who raises a knife.

speaker: player
text: Hold the right, Arthur. Cover the escort with the rifle.

speaker: player
text: Steady, man.

speaker: Arthur
text: Right flank, rifle on the escort. For Lucy, and for Mina. Go.

speaker: Arthur
text: I am steady. I have never been steadier. God forgive me if I miss.

speaker: Seward
text: Jonathan, I take the left, wide of the wagon, to keep their horsemen from circling. If I fire at the wolves, they are the lesser danger.

speaker: player
text: Hold the left, Jack. Break the circle if you must.

speaker: player
text: How much ammunition do you have?

speaker: Seward
text: Left flank, understood. I shall fire over their heads if I can, and between their eyes if I cannot.

speaker: Seward
text: Plenty, and a prayer for each cartridge. We do not need many.

speaker: Quincey
text: Jonathan, we two go for the box. You get the throat, I'll get the heart. If either's down, the other does the job. Shake on it.

speaker: player
text: We go together, Quincey. The kukri first, the bowie after.

speaker: player
text: Is your side hurting you?

speaker: Quincey
text: That's a deal, Jonathan. For Lucy, and for the little lady up there. Let's go.

speaker: Quincey
text: Only a scratch. Don't fuss, Jonathan.

speaker: Szgany captain
text: [He looks at us, at the sun, and back at the box.] Gentlemen, the road is closed. This is a poor man's load and a poor man's journey. I am paid by the day.

speaker: player
text: Stand aside. We have no quarrel with you.

speaker: player
text: Who is the master you serve?

speaker: Szgany captain
text: [He spits.] A man who pays in gold and watches me with eyes I do not like. I do not stand aside, English. He made us swear. He will make us die before he lets his box be touched.

speaker: Szgany captain
text: I do not know his name. The Count of the castle, they say. If you come between the Count and his house, you will not see another day.

speaker: Quincey
text: I am only too happy to have been of any service. Don't cry, little lady. It was a fair fight.

speaker: player
text: Quincey, you are hurt.

speaker: Quincey
text: [He took my hand in his feeble one, and smiled.] Oh, God! It was worth for this to die! Look! look!

speaker: Mina
text: [The sun was now right down upon the mountain top, and the red gleams fell upon my face so that it was bathed in rosy light. The men sank on their knees; a deep and earnest 'Amen' broke from all.]

speaker: Quincey
text: Now God be thanked that all has not been in vain! See! The snow is not more stainless than her forehead! The curse has passed away!

speaker: Mina
text: [And to our bitter grief, with a smile and in silence, he died, a gallant gentleman. I touched my forehead: there was no mark.]

speaker: Jonathan
text: He was braver than any of us, Mina. He was our friend. And I never said so.

speaker: player
text: He knew, Jonathan.

speaker: Jonathan
text: Let us carry him down together. Wherever we go, whatever we call our children, he will be remembered.

speaker: Mina
text: He is a lovely boy, Jonathan. He has Quincey's name and, I think, Quincey's laugh. The scar is gone, and so is the fear. Come and read what you have written.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: Arthur. Is that the light, or is it the evening?

speaker: player
text: Evening, sir. Dr. Lenox says you must rest.

speaker: player
text: Your spectacles, sir. I found them under the Bible.

speaker: player
text: The cordial, sir. Dr. Lenox's evening dose.

speaker: player
text: There is a telegram from Hillingham, sir.

speaker: player
text: There is a telegram from Hillingham, sir.

speaker: player
text: Tell me about the Ring, sir.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: Rest? I have rested for forty years in that chair downstairs, and look what it has done to my eyes. Talk to me.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: Ah. Now there is a thing. A man cannot be a Lord without his spectacles; the tenants would see right through him.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: Foul stuff. Lenox swears by it. Well, I shall be brave for you.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: I cannot read it, Arthur, with the whole room swimming. Come back when I can see.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: '...do not stay away for fear of us.' Then go, boy. Go to her. A Holmwood who waits for a death before he lives has not understood the family business.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: There is a ring in my desk. Your mother's. And a letter to Mrs. Westenra, in case her heart needs persuading. The key is somewhere in the hall; I hid it from myself years ago and I have been ashamed ever since.

speaker: Lord Godalming
text: The Ring is the house, the land, and four hundred people who think it will outlast them. It is a burden, Arthur. I hope you will carry it better than I.

speaker: Dr. Lenox
text: The Lord rallies when he has company, Mr. Holmwood. Anything that interests him is medicine. But no excitement.

speaker: player
text: What is wrong with him?

speaker: player
text: Is there any hope?

speaker: Dr. Lenox
text: The heart, and the strain of carrying too much. Worry is the real disease. He has been worrying for years. About what, I have never been told.

speaker: Dr. Lenox
text: Weeks, perhaps. He wants to see you settled. I would see to it, if I were you. The green bottle in my cabinet will steady him for conversation.

speaker: Bates
text: Master Arthur. The household is at your disposal, sir, as it always was at his.

speaker: player
text: Have you seen my father's desk-key?

speaker: player
text: Who is Crowle of Crowle & Aske?

speaker: Bates
text: His lordship hid it himself, sir, in the hall, and told no one where. He said once it was safest in company with something that had never been opened: books, old Sir Hugh, or the chest.

speaker: Bates
text: The Lord's banker, sir. He came often in the winter. The Lord asked me never to announce him. I thought it discreet.

speaker: Tom
