text: Mr. Swales's bench, black with sea-wet and tobacco.

speaker: Narrator
text: Unlit by day. It has a lovely view and no flame.

speaker: Narrator
text: The steep way down to the harbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grass path, and the broken Abbey beyond.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'West Cliff and the Crescent.' Under it, in pencil: 'Mind the steps.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A very old man, weather-beaten like a sea-wall, leaning on a stick and clearly enjoying a young lady's company.

speaker: Narrator
text: He lies on the seat, his neck broken, his face frozen in fear and horror. The coastguard says he fell. I do not think he fell.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout lady in a bonnet, a guide-book in one hand and a parasol in the other, pleased with everything.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tarred door under a tarred lintel. A padlock that has seen more of the sea than of oil.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cliff drops straight into the harbour here, black and dripping.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gulls nest on every ledge.

speaker: Narrator
text: The same wet black rock, down to the waterline.

text: Hundreds of years of feet have worn the steps hollow. The iron rail is cold and wet.

speaker: Narrator
text: Twine, tar, tallow and lamp-glass, and a bunch of garlic hung up by the sailors for luck.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sailors hang garlic to keep off fever and the evil eye.

speaker: Narrator
text: The chandler waves me on: 'Take it, miss, it's no use to me. Lucy'd not like the smell.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Salt and scales and the afternoon's catch.

speaker: Narrator
text: Empty and smelling it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lighthouse lanthorn keeps better time than the town clocks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tate Hill Pier gathers sand and gravel at its foot. A ship driven here would stick fast.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tarred planks and a pair of oars. The coastguard's, by the number on her bow.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cork floats, coils of net and a dead gull somebody swept in.

speaker: Narrator
text: A schooner of Varna, aground on the sand with her sails in tatters. A cordon of ropes keeps the crowd back.

speaker: Narrator
text: A broad woman with arms like rope. She has sold twine to three generations of drowned men.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mending a net with fingers like knots of tarred rope. His eyes never leave the sky.

speaker: Narrator
text: Helmeted, stout, and fully aware of the importance of his rope.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tidy, worried solicitor with a pencil behind his ear and fifty boxes he did not order on his conscience.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great grey brute, cowering under the pier. It sprang from the ship and none can say whose it is.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back out to the harbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black stove with a kettle that never quite boils.

speaker: Narrator
text: Blankets that smell of tobacco and wet dog. No dog.

speaker: Narrator
text: A good steel splicing knife with a horn handle, left on the desk.

speaker: Narrator
text: A knife is no weapon against what is coming, but it cuts rope and ash wood and I take it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The coastguard's chair, worn to his shape.

speaker: Narrator
text: Marline-spikes, a sail-needle, a short iron crowbar for stubborn lids.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the crowbar. A lid that will not open will open to this.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout storm lantern, wick trimmed.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the storm lantern. A hold is a dark place.

speaker: Narrator
text: Paraffin, topped up that morning.

speaker: Narrator
text: I fill a flask from the keg.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rain water, cold and clean.

speaker: Narrator
text: I fill a little flask with clean water.

speaker: Narrator
text: A square, patient man whose eyes are always on the weather even indoors.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the White Lady shows herself at sunset, in the legend, in the same pose as a woman at a high window. The glass is gone, and the light is lovely.

speaker: Narrator
text: Half an arch against the sky. The other half is the sea's now.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cut off at the knee by seven centuries.

speaker: Narrator
text: The slab of some forgotten abbot. A single line of Latin is left: 'Dominus custodiat introitum tuum.' May the Lord guard thy coming in.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pale wild roses growing out of the broken stones. The sexton says they bloom here in defiance of the wind.

speaker: Narrator
text: I pick one sprig, careful of the thorns. Wild rose is a good flower for a grave.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bough of ash, broken in some gale, clean and straight.

speaker: Narrator
text: I break off a straight piece. Ash is good, hard wood.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hollow stone full of rain, collected for nobody.

speaker: Narrator
text: I fill my flask. Rain-water from the Abbey is as pure as any.

speaker: Narrator
text: No name left. Lucy says its owner dislikes visitors.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way back up to the churchyard.

speaker: Narrator
text: An elderly man with a spade, who talks to the stones as if they were shy parishioners.

speaker: Narrator
text: The new searchlight on the summit of the East Cliff, untried until tonight. It sweeps the sea like a white finger.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wet, empty and humming in the wind.

speaker: Narrator
text: Swinging so wildly it throws two shadows at once.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shouting orders into the wind that the wind sends back unfinished.

speaker: Narrator
text: Soaked and delighted. He has predicted this and is not displeased to be right.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fishwife in a shawl, knuckles white on the railing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A boatman, praying aloud and quite without shame.

speaker: Narrator
text: A landlady in a nightcap and her husband's coat.

speaker: Narrator
text: The mast is intact, but its canvas has been ripped into long grey ribbons.

speaker: Narrator
text: The helm. Cords bind the spokes. Whoever stood here meant to keep this course whatever came for him.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mildewed sailcloth and rope-ends. The lock has been burst.

speaker: Narrator
text: Clean canvas, torn from the spare sail. Good for bandages or wicks.

speaker: Narrator
text: A handspike of ash, for keeping men in order, which the mate swore would suffice. The crew thought otherwise.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the handspike. A straight length of ash is worth more than its wooden weight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Smashed. The glass lies outward as though something inside wanted out.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pitch. The deck-house door is bolted with it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the pier.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way below. A padlock holds it, rusty and obstinate.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lashed to the helm, his hands bound over a crucifix and a string of beads, his head fallen forward. Two days dead, they say, and no man in the crowd would touch him.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back up to the deck and the grey light.

speaker: Narrator
text: A straw tick, a Russian Bible and a crucifix-sized empty nail. Under the tick, damp pages.

speaker: Narrator
text: Under the straw tick, a damp roll of paper in a seaman's hand: the second leaf of the log.

speaker: Narrator
text: Charts of the Black Sea and the Channel, with a course pencilled to Gibraltar and a cross where nothing should have been.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rolled inside the chart, a third leaf of the log, smeared with something rust-coloured.

speaker: Narrator
text: Oilskins, a pipe and a ledger. The lid has been forced.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wrapped in oilskin at the bottom: the first leaf of the log, headed Varna.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great box, sealed with nails. Stencilled: 'Clay. For Mr. S. F. Billington, 7 The Crescent, Whitby.' It stinks of old earth, and something else.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lid is off. Earth, black and dry, fills it. In the earth, a hollow the shape of a man's back.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pinned under the lid, the consignment note in two languages: fifty boxes of earth, for Billington, by Hawkins's agents.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sealed. The nails are bent outward. It has been opened and closed again from the inside.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hammer, chisel, a screwdriver. The mate used it only once.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy hammer. If I ever need to drive in a stake...

speaker: Narrator
text: Canvas bag stuffed with old sailcloth and twine.

speaker: Narrator
text: A clean length of canvas from the sail-bag.

speaker: Narrator
text: Out of oil. The wick is black.

speaker: Narrator
text: A four-poster with Lucy's nightgown thrown across the foot.

speaker: Narrator
text: The sash is open to the sea air; Lucy likes it so.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dresses, hats and a very large muff.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chair with a shawl thrown over its back.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thick white shawl, the warmest we own.

speaker: Narrator
text: I lay the shawl ready by my pillow. If the worst came, she should not be cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: Brushes, a silver mirror and Lucy's whole hair-ribbon collection.

speaker: Narrator
text: A flask of brandy that Mrs. Westenra says is only for emergencies.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the flask. Emergencies, as Mrs. Westenra says.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door to the landing, with a good lock and, as yet, no key.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door is still locked from the inside. How did she get out?

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy sleeps with one hand under her cheek and the sea-wind stirring her hair.

speaker: Narrator
text: Stone steps up toward St. Mary's, vanishing into fog.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door I came out of.

speaker: Narrator
text: Small bare footprints in the wet, going up and to the left. Lucy has gone without her slippers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Caught on a rusted spike, a scrap of white cambric the colour of Lucy's nightgown.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dull orange in the thick air.

speaker: Narrator
text: Another, equally helpless.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tired night watchman with a lantern and a bad chest.

speaker: Narrator
text: An urchin of eleven, sitting up long past any bedtime, in a coat that was a man's.

speaker: Narrator
text: The seat where we sit by day. By night it is a different place altogether.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black against the moon, with one lit window. The clock has stopped.

speaker: Narrator
text: The arch stands out with the moon behind it, and something pale seems to hang in the broken window.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way I came.

speaker: Narrator
text: She sits upright on the seat, perfectly still, her head thrown back and her lips parted. Her nightgown is wet to the knee.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall, thin, black shape bending over her. In the moonlight, something white, and two small points of red like eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Case-books, a blotter, a green-shaded lamp. A drawer that has seen better locks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Edison's wax-cylinder phonograph. My diary speaks aloud now, and sometimes disagrees with me.

speaker: Narrator
text: My chair. The leather is worn to the shape of long nights.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small table under the window, piled with ledgers.

speaker: Narrator
text: The asylum case-ledger. Dosages, weights, observations.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where I sort what I have found, before I let myself conclude anything.

speaker: Narrator
text: My working notes on Renfield. I will set down what I have gathered, and decide.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lombroso, Esquirol, Maudsley, Bucknill and Tuke. A row of sensible men who did not meet Renfield.

speaker: Narrator
text: A banked fire, a mantel clock, a photograph of Lucy I should not have kept so near.

speaker: Narrator
text: An old campaign chest of instruments I rarely need.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hippocrates, chipped on the nose. He has heard everything I have said into the phonograph, and has not judged.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three candles, for the nights the gas gives out.

speaker: Narrator
text: Laudanum, labelled, locked up in spirit if not in fact. I keep it on the sill so I will not forget the danger.

speaker: Narrator
text: The passage to the ward and the dispensary.

speaker: Narrator
text: My assistant, brisk and tired, with a stethoscope round his neck and a rumpled Irish smile.

speaker: Narrator
text: My study, where the phonograph waits.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy oak door with a barred grille at the height of a face. Something moves behind it, and counts.

speaker: Narrator
text: The garden door, with a little daylight under it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The poison cabinet: chloral, morphia, laudanum, and my one decent brandy. It is locked, and I am the guard.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hennessey weighs the patients here. A strip of chalk reads: 'R. - 9 st. 4 lb. (down 11 lb.)'. He eats nothing at table.

speaker: Narrator
text: Scales, a graduated glass and a brass measure. Here I weigh out what sends men to sleep.

speaker: Narrator
text: Clean rainwater from the roof, with a tin dipper. Good enough for a draught.

speaker: Narrator
text: Clean sheets for the beds. The lid does not sit quite flat.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench no one sits on for long.

speaker: Narrator
text: An oil lamp, trimmed and lit, with a wire guard.

speaker: Narrator
text: Some patients ask for it and some are quieter without it. We keep it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A square, patient attendant in a white coat, with keys at his belt and his hat in his hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cell door, with a grille on the corridor side only.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iron bars, painted so often they are fat with paint. Through them, Carfax's chimneys show black against the sky.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cot, a blanket, a neatly folded sheet. Some cleaner madness is being hidden here.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lumpy. It has been slit and sewn up again with fishing-twine.

speaker: Narrator
text: Inside, wrapped in a handkerchief: a dozen lumps of sugar, hoarded from his tea.

speaker: Narrator
text: A deal table scrubbed white. On it the evidence of an industry.

speaker: Narrator
text: Forty bluebottles in a jam-jar, bumbling against the muslin.

speaker: Narrator
text: I lift the jar. Forty flies, and every one of them counted.

speaker: Narrator
text: A school exercise book filled with rows of figures and little crosses.

speaker: Narrator
text: Flies; spiders; sparrows. Each total is added with a flourish. I take the notebook.

speaker: Narrator
text: A shallow deal box with a sliding lid. Something dry rustles inside.

speaker: Narrator
text: A box of fat spiders, each in its own cardboard cell like a lodger. I take it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sparrow hops on the flagstones, quite unafraid of a man who has been feeding it spiders.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bolted-down stool.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bucket. The least interesting thing in the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: He crouches by the wall, muttering numbers, his eyes fixed on a point just behind my head. He is thin as a rake and awake as a lamp.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield, sitting quietly on the cot with his hands between his knees. He looks like a clerk, which he once was.

speaker: Narrator
text: The ward door, painted the grey of institutions.

speaker: Narrator
text: Carfax: the old house next door, shut up, tumbledown, sold lately to a foreigner by Mr Hawkins's firm. It is nearer than I should like.

speaker: Narrator
text: The gardener's shed. A row of hooks, a smell of earth and creosote.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pocock's toolbox, with the lid propped by a trowel.

speaker: Narrator
text: A good claw hammer. I take it, and leave the nails.

speaker: Narrator
text: One slat of the boundary fence swings on a single nail. Through the gap, long grass, a worn track leading to the garden of Carfax.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench in the sun, facing the high wall. Convalescent patients sit here when they are well enough to be bored.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sparrows on the gravel, plump as aldermen. One of them hops closer, as if it had been fed by a gentleman.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hansom with a tired grey horse. The driver wants to know which road.

speaker: Narrator
text: A four-wheeler hired for the afternoon. 'The Zoo, sir? Regent's Park, an hour or so.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A gas lamp on an iron standard.

speaker: Narrator
text: The head gardener, with hands like roots and a face that has seen weather and patients alike.

speaker: Narrator
text: A boy in a pillbox cap, red from running, with a buff envelope held out in front of him like a tray.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Zoological Gardens. Carnivora: left. Pachyderms: right. Visitors are requested not to tease the animals.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Two bars of the wolves' cage are bent outward, like grass in a flood. A wolf did not do this alone.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain table outside Mr Bilder's cottage. Tea, a mug, and a folded newspaper.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'An Escaped Wolf'. The paper is already soft from the keeper's thumb.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr Bilder says I may have the cutting. 'Better you than the Missus, who reads it aloud.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench with a view of the wolves and no wolves in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Straw for the cages.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gas lamp not yet lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: My cab, waiting for the return to the asylum.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout keeper in a flat cap, smelling of straw and wintergreen. He has the manner of a man much interviewed.

speaker: Narrator
text: The keeper's wife on her step, with her arms folded and her opinions plain.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great grey wolf paces his cage, back and forth, back and forth, with his eyes on the north.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain door, and beyond it the sound of someone setting out candles.

speaker: Narrator
text: A made-up cot, white as a bandage.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sleeping patient, an old man with a rosary round his wrist.

speaker: Narrator
text: The corner bed. A blanket is drawn up to the chin of the thinnest, whitest man I have ever loved.

speaker: Narrator
text: Empty. The sister has put a sprig of box on the pillow.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small desk with a lamp, a ledger and a rosary. The ledger records every patient's fever to the quarter-degree.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stick of red sealing wax and a taper beside it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the wax. Sister Agatha nods; it is for a good cause.

speaker: Narrator
text: The letter that brought me here, left under the lamp.

speaker: Narrator
text: I fold Sister Agatha's letter into my bag. I shall want it, one day, to show him how it was.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sister's sewing-basket: thread, thimbles, scraps of black ribbon for shrouds.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take a length of black ribbon from the basket.

speaker: Narrator
text: A clean little table near the window, ink, paper, and room enough for a decision.

speaker: Narrator
text: A man's threadbare coat is over the chair-back, with a waistcoat folded beneath it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A few coins, a ticket, and something small and round that has gone green with sweat.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain gold ring, wrapped in a handkerchief. He bought it before the Castle. I take it.

speaker: Narrator
text: My travelling trunk, still strapped. I have brought one good dress, in case.

speaker: Narrator
text: A crucifix over the sister's desk. The ward is quiet beneath it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three candles for the night nurse.

speaker: Narrator
text: A basin of cool water and a folded cloth.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall, quiet Sister of St Joseph, with a calm face, an English that is better than mine is German, and a hand like a bird's.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan, in a hospital shirt, his hair gone white. He is sitting up, which is more than the doctors promised.

speaker: Narrator
text: A young Hungarian sister folding sheets with great severity.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the ward and the corner bed.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain altar-table with a white cloth, two candles, and a missal open to the marriage service.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small silver crucifix. It is Hungarian and old and the face on it is kind.

speaker: Narrator
text: Candles for a wedding in the afternoon.

speaker: Narrator
text: Candles for a wedding in the afternoon.

text: A worn pew.

speaker: Narrator
text: A worn pew.

text: A worn pew.

speaker: Narrator
text: A worn pew.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone stoup of holy water.

speaker: Narrator
text: An English-speaking priest in a worn white surplice, with ink on his thumb. He has agreed to this at two hours' notice.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan, steadied between two orderlies' chairs. He has combed what is left of his hair.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sister Agatha, who has agreed to be the witness for the sake of two strangers and a miracle.

speaker: Narrator
text: The stairs up to Lucy's room. A faint smell of lavender, and of something older.

speaker: Narrator
text: The garden door, ajar, with the hum of evening bees behind it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall clock that ticks like a pulse. It says a quarter to seven, and the post-office closes at eight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs Westenra's writing desk: crested paper, pen and ink, a bundle of Lucy's old Whitby postcards.

speaker: Narrator
text: A packet of post-office telegram forms, each with a printed line: 'Sender's name below, address above'.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take a form. I should compose the message with care; every word is a halfpenny and an hour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A table for papers and magazines. A railway timetable lies open.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bradshaw's Railway Guide, open to the Continental pages.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs Westenra's sideboard: sherry, port, and one decent bottle of brandy for emergencies.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the brandy. I rather suspect I shall need it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small table by the wall.

speaker: Narrator
text: The port decanter, half empty. It does not smell like port.

speaker: Narrator
text: The housekeeper's key-board, labelled in copperplate. 'Miss L.'s room' hangs by itself.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the key to Lucy's room. It may be the only ward that cannot be argued with.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fire kept alight in all weathers. The room is warm and the house is cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: An easy chair by the fire. One could wait for morning in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A deal box with Dutch stamps, full of garlic flowers. The scent is enormous.

speaker: Narrator
text: Umbrellas, a cane or two, and an iron bar someone has stood among them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A branch of candles.

speaker: Narrator
text: A kitchen chair, brought in for the insensible maid.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bust of someone's grandfather, looking disapproving.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's mother: small, silvered, gentle, with a cardiac flush she thinks no one notices and a heart the doctors will not name.

speaker: Narrator
text: A young maid with a duster in her pocket and a way of looking over her shoulder at the stairs.

speaker: Narrator
text: One of the maids, slumped and breathing like an engine, as if she would never wake.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur, a big fair man who looks as if he had been struck. He holds his hat in both hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey Morris, mud to the knees and a wide hat, standing as if he had ridden in. His voice is the softest thing about him.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white bed with a blue counterpane. The pillow is a perfect, slightly sunken oval.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chair set where a watcher would sit. A rug, a cushion, a book unopened.

speaker: Narrator
text: A girl's dressing-table: brushes, a hand-glass, a faded Whitby postcard.

speaker: Narrator
text: A mirror in which a pale girl, if she stood there, would still look like herself.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dresses of a summer that ended in Whitby.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her mother's dressing-case, dropped in the night. Powder, hairpins, and a little bottle of sal volatile.

speaker: Narrator
text: Smelling salts. They will not wake a drugged girl who is truly gone, but they may wake a servant who is only dosed.

speaker: Narrator
text: A water jug, a glass, a candle, and a medicine bottle three-quarters empty.

speaker: Narrator
text: Garlic flowers scattered between the bed and the window, as though dropped by someone walking away.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her white slippers, beside the window-seat. The soles are wet with dew.

speaker: Narrator
text: The east window is gone: a ragged hole, glass across the carpet, the curtains snapping in the night air.

speaker: Narrator
text: We have covered her with a sheet, and with the last decency we had. Her hand has slipped out from under it, and Van Helsing has put it back.

text: The door to the landing. A bolt on the inside, a lock outside.

speaker: Narrator
text: A deep window-seat under the east window. In the evenings she sits here and counts the stars. The sash is painted so it will not open. Except that it has opened.

text: A small grate, swept and empty. A chimney is a door, if one is thin enough.

text: Lucy, propped on pillows: a white-lipped, still beautiful girl with blue-veined eyelids and a pulse like a bird's.

text: A slatted work-bench strewn with pots, twine and bulbs.

text: A lantern hung on the wall by the door.

text: A weathered stone, a skull and an hour-glass.

text: 'Thomas Holloway, of this parish.'

text: A small stone cross with a wreath of dead lilies.

text: A cross leaning at ten degrees to the world.

text: A wet bench. No one is sitting on it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lantern, for the late burials.

text: Wreaths of white lilies and white roses. Arthur's is the largest, and the Professor's is the only one that smells of anything.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor, bare-headed in the rain, with his hat in his hands and a bag at his feet.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur, motionless as a post. Quincey has an arm round his shoulders.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey, his hat pulled down against the rain and, I think, against my eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: The sexton, a leathery man, leaning on a spade and waiting, with the immense patience of his trade.

text: The door of the inn on the crown of the Heath.

text: The narrow path that runs north over the Heath toward the church of Kingstead.

text: A thin lad with a satchel of papers and a loud voice.

text: A woman in a grey shawl, one eye always on the children, the other on a policeman.

text: Two small children playing at being the 'bloofer lady' and the baby she takes away.

text: A tall constable with a notebook, leaning against a rail and tired of questions.

text: A neatly made cot. Its small occupant went home this morning.

text: A small child lies here, white as the sheet, a bandage at the throat.

text: A table with the ward register open upon it.

text: A brass lamp turned low for the night nurse.

text: A chair for the mother who has not come.

text: The way back to the Heath.

text: A small girl propped on pillows, watching me with solemn eyes.

text: A sister in starched cap, carrying linen as if it were a standard.

text: The door to the hall, and the cab that will carry us back to the Heath.

text: The cab for Hillingham, where Lucy's papers still lie.

text: The cab for the railway station and Mrs Harker's hotel.

text: The Professor stands with his hands to the blaze, watching me as one watches a patient who refuses a draught.

text: My desk: the diary on the phonograph cylinders, a half-written case note, and a cold cup of tea.

text: Worn to the shape of an anxious man.

text: My bench. I learned to cut keys as a student to help a locked-up uncle; the asylum has since put the skill to many uses.

text: A drawer of key blanks, odd wards, and a rusty file.

text: An old biscuit tin of keys that belong to nothing I own.

text: The blotter, full of ink and half-formed doubts.

text: The Professor's bag: it clinks in a way that has nothing to do with surgery.

text: My own case of post-mortem knives. He asked for it at Hillingham, and I did not ask why.

text: The asylum's tool chest: saws, a mallet, a hammer for the loose boards.

text: I took the heavy hammer. It will drive a stake or a nail equally.

text: Mina's typewriter stands here, its ribbon worn grey and faint. A folded shawl lies next to it.

text: The machine is ready, the paper rolled in. Mina's shorthand diary would go well on it.

text: Thread, a thimble, a half-darned stocking, and a spare typewriter ribbon in blue paper.

text: A spare ribbon, still in its paper. Mina would not mind.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sofa where Jonathan sits when he is not walking up and down.

text: Mina has marked the Exeter trains in pencil. 'Quick 3.34, change at Reading.'

text: A small coal fire, politely lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain hotel chair.

speaker: Narrator
text: An oil lamp, wick trimmed.

speaker: Narrator
text: The hotel corridor, and the cab back to Purfleet.

text: Mina, pale and composed, has the look of a woman who has lately been very frightened and has decided to be useful.

text: Jonathan's hair is white at the temples. He looks twenty years older than the photograph on Mina's table.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way to the front door and the cab for Purfleet.

text: A cab waits for the road to Kingstead.

text: The bed where Lucy lay, now stripped, with a tarnished outline of lilies still on the pillow.

speaker: Narrator
text: Four tall candles, burnt to stubs. Nobody has dared to remove them.

text: The box that came from Haarlem, addressed by the Professor: a mass of wild garlic flowers, heavy as sin.

text: I took a handful of the white flowers. The smell makes my eyes run.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sprigs of garlic stuck into a vase beside the window.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took the sprigs.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bunch tied with ribbon to the window latch.

speaker: Narrator
text: I untied the bunch.

text: A pretty desk with papers in neat stacks: Mrs Westenra's accounts, Lucy's letters, bills from the undertaker.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thick Turkey rug, one corner turned up as if someone stepped on it in haste.

text: Novels, a Book of Common Prayer, the Peerage. Nothing that would help us.

text: A basket of ash kindling beside the cold grate, from the garden pruning.

text: I took a good length of ash kindling. A carpenter could make something of it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bone-handled paper knife, keen enough to trim a quill or a vein.

speaker: Narrator
text: I pocketed the paper knife.

text: The undertaker left a pattern coffin in the hall. Lead lining, oak outer, brass handles.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor's case. Inside lies the tin that came from Amsterdam.

speaker: Narrator
text: A young maid with red eyes who dusts the same shelf again and again.

text: The family solicitor, in a black coat and an air of professional sorrow, with his hat held like a shield.

text: Arthur sits with his face in his hands. He has not shaved in three days.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey leans on the mantel, slowly rolling a cigarette he does not light.

speaker: Narrator
text: The inn door, with a bell that rings once when it opens.

text: A long table with a cold joint, bread and a stone jug of ale. The Professor is already carving.

text: A fire where a whole sheep could be roasted. It throws shadows like the wings of bats.

text: A cask of the landlord's best. A coil of good hemp rope hangs behind it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Behind the barrel hangs a coil of good hemp rope. I take it.

text: A rack of pewter pots, a ledger and a jar of loose change.

text: A pewter cup holding a few coins.

text: The landlord nods: a silver coin is mine to borrow.

text: A good oil lantern with a slide that opens and closes the light.

text: The landlord sells me the lamp for a florin.

speaker: Narrator
text: A box of lucifer matches and a handful of candle-ends.

text: I pocketed the matches.

text: A stone jug of spring water.

speaker: Narrator
text: I filled a flask.

text: A carter nursing a mug of ale and a grievance.

text: Back to the Heath and Jack Straw's.

text: The lane toward the lych-gate of Kingstead.

text: A lamp that gives light to itself and little else.

text: The patrol's lamp on the corner; the policeman stands under it on his round.

text: I took a ball of the glazier's putty. It has many uses.

text: I took the soldering iron.

text: I took the solder.

text: The Hollis family tomb: weather-stained, mean-looking in the failing sun.

text: The lane back toward the Heath.

text: A sleepy cabman with a muffler over his chin.

text: A juniper marking the church path.

text: Another juniper on the path.

text: A pointed stone, lichen-eaten.

text: A stone cross leaning toward the path.

text: A tomb with iron railing, white against the dark.

text: The creaking door. It lets in a little of the night.

text: A web the size of a dinner-plate, a fat spider in the middle of it.

text: She lies back in the coffin, eyes open and staring, the red fading from her lips. She cannot move.

speaker: Narrator
text: Candles enough to read by, if not to hope by.

text: Rows of lunacy and physiology. I once thought they explained the world.

speaker: Narrator
text: Case-books of the asylum, with Renfield's more voluminous than most.

text: A modest fire. On the mantel, a stopped carriage-clock and a small stone bust.

text: A heavy glass inkstand with a stopper.

text: I took the decanter. It has revived better men than I.

text: I took the carafe of water.

text: I opened the telegram. It is from Lloyd's.

text: The corridor to the wards, and Renfield's room.

speaker: Narrator
text: The garden door.

speaker: Narrator
text: The stair to the guest rooms, where the Harkers are lodged.

text: Jonathan, hair gone white at the temples, a man who has seen the mountains' other side.

text: Mrs. Harker, small and straight, with a printer's patience about her. Her eyes are very bright.

text: Mina, pale and resolute. Her hands are never still: she folds, unfolds, touches the typescript.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina, with a linen band across her brow. She meets my eye bravely.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina sits in the high-backed chair, like one expecting to be questioned by a dream.

text: Mina, very still. She has understood before any of us that she will not be taken.

text: A broad, keen-eyed Dutchman with a pointed beard. He carries a heavy bag as though it held sleeping children.

text: The Professor, with the Host at his breast and grief behind his eyes.

text: Van Helsing, turning a gold coin over and over: the old hypnotist's trick, made grim.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor with timetables spread before him, already half in Varna.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lord Godalming, calm in a way he did not use to be. Grief has given him a quiet edge.

speaker: Narrator

speaker: Narrator
text: A sturdy desk, with carbon paper in neat stacks.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Remington, borrowed from the village. I feed it papers and it gives back order.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina has pinned notes, cuttings and tickets in order. Threads of cotton link them. A wall of knowledge.

speaker: Narrator
text: A good lamp, trimmed bright.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three copies of everything. 'Never trust one copy,' Jonathan says.

speaker: Narrator
text: Overflowing with spoiled sheets.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the library.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow bed with a grey blanket. The sheets are ripped in strips for some purpose of his own.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sugar spilled in a careful ring. Dead flies lie in rows like soldiers.

speaker: Narrator
text: A jar full of flies, kept for the spiders. 'Life,' Renfield calls it. 'Life, Doctor.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Sugar for the flies. The attendants say he saves it from his tea.

text: I took the notebook. Mina may find the pattern I cannot.

text: The sash opens only an inch, and there is a bar across it. The park beyond is grey with fog.

text: A lamp turned low, the nearest thing to company he allows.

text: My chair. I have sat here more nights than my own bed.

speaker: Narrator
text: The corridor and the library beyond.

text: Renfield, pale and sweating, hands twisting at his waistcoat. For once there is terror in him, not cunning.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield on the floor, back broken, face bruised past knowing. He lives, but only just.

speaker: Narrator
text: He is at peace at last. His hands are open.

speaker: Narrator
text: Simmons, a decent, stolid man who has seen nothing, and would rather not say so.

speaker: Narrator
text: The garden door of the asylum.

text: A heavy oak gate, bolted on the Carfax side. Beyond lie the neglected grounds.

text: A bench the patients use on fine days.

text: I chose a straight billet of ash.

text: I took a strip of clean linen.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lamp on a post, not yet lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cabman with a red nose and a talent for hearing what he shouldn't.

speaker: Narrator
text: The gate we came by.

text: A leaning gatepost, green with moss.

text: A well-head, covered with a plank. It stinks of earth.

text: A cross, so old that no name remains.

text: Moss has eaten the seat. No one has sat here in decades.

speaker: Narrator
text: Harker's lamp, set down on the path, a small yellow world.

text: Jonathan, white and silent, looking at the house as though it were the castle again.

text: The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

text: The third stack: 6 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.

speaker: Narrator
text: The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

speaker: Narrator
text: The fourth stack: 6 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.

speaker: Narrator
text: The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

speaker: Narrator
text: The last stack: 5 great boxes of foul earth, brought from Transylvania. They hum, to my ear, with something evil.

speaker: Narrator
text: The earth is pale and dead now. The Count can never lie here again.

speaker: Narrator
text: The altar-stone is cracked. Dust and earth cover it. The Count has made a jest of the place.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pew, rotten with age. The saints on the wall are scarcely visible.

speaker: Narrator
text: Strokes of chalk on the stone, in fives, crossed through. I count twenty-nine strokes. Someone has been counting what was brought, and not all of it came here.

speaker: Narrator
text: One of Arthur's terriers, a small hard dog with a scarred nose and a conqueror's air.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lamps held high are the best weapon against rats.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door to the park.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hundreds of rats in the nave, a rolling grey tide with eyes like coals.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor, bag at his feet, a pyx of consecrated Host in one gloved hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan holding the lamp, counting under his breath.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cab that brought us up from the asylum.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gilt sign above a smoke-black door: 'CARTER, PATERSON & CO., CARRIERS'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass plate: 'MITCHELL, SONS & CANDY, HOUSE AGENTS AND SURVEYORS'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone-fronted house with a bow window, high steps, and a torn 'To Let' board. I have walked past it this morning.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow alley leads south toward Walworth and its courts.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hansom for hire. 'Mile End New Town, sir? Chicksand Street?'

speaker: Narrator
text: A growler for hire. 'Jamaica Lane, sir? That be Bermondsey.'

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Bartel Street' points one way, 'Piccadilly' the other, and 'Walworth Road' somewhere beyond a hundred chimneys.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gas-lamp, not yet lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: A barrel of winkles, abandoned by a coster.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan in a plain travelling coat, notebook in hand. He has hardened since the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thin boy with quick eyes. He holds out a hand without shame.

speaker: Narrator
text: A scarred oak counter, laden with forms and string.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy ledger, chained to the counter. Mr. Smollet keeps a hand on it. The page for last month is dog-eared.

speaker: Narrator
text: Waybills by the hundredweight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Parcels tied with string and labelled in four different hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: A high stool for an unhappy clerk.

speaker: Narrator
text: A smoky lamp, left lit all day.

speaker: Narrator
text: A notice: 'Carriers are not responsible for boxes of earth, live eels, or the Devil.' A wag has added the last item.

speaker: Narrator
text: The street.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Smollet, foreman of the carriers: a thick man with ink on his cuffs and a cautious eye for strangers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Thomas Snelling, the carter, asleep upright on a sack and smelling of beer.

speaker: Narrator
text: The mouth of the court, back to the alley.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long hand-cart. The planks are dented with the corners of heavy boxes.

speaker: Narrator
text: A rain barrel with a drowned cat's-tail floating.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grey linen on a line across the court.

speaker: Narrator
text: Corcoran's bench, where Bloxam drinks.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lamp, left lit all night by the landlady.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sam Bloxam, carter, in a greasy waistcoat with a clay pipe in his teeth. He eyes my coat for what it might hold.

speaker: Narrator
text: A polished counter with a brass hand-bell.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black safe, bolted to the floor. A discreet agent keeps keys of let property here.

speaker: Narrator
text: Deed boxes labelled with the names of London squares.

speaker: Narrator
text: A framed map of the West End. Piccadilly is underscored in red, with the numbers 341-349 outlined.

speaker: Narrator
text: A potted fir, dusted twice daily.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chair for clients who arrive with money.

speaker: Narrator
text: The street.

speaker: Narrator
text: A young clerk in a high collar, nervous behind his counter, anxious to be discreet.

speaker: Narrator
text: A wide bed, twisted sheets. It faces the window, and Mina has not slept in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thick yellow blind covers the window. On a night of full moon it glows like a lantern.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Bible, a glass of water and Mina's hairpins.

speaker: Narrator
text: The gaslight, turned low.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's trunk: dresses, writing-case, and a locket from Lucy.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chair where Mina sat with her mending, in the first days.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door locks from within. It has a bolt.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan lies face upward in a deathlike lethargy, face flushed, breathing as a drowning man.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall thin man in black, face waxen, eyes red, a bloody scar upon his brow. Beside him, Mina on her knees, her mouth at his open breast.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina in her nightdress, white and bloodied, on her knees at the Count's breast. Her eyes are open and there is no Mina in them.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor with the Host raised in an envelope, face like a judge's.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur with his crucifix thrust forward, trembling.

speaker: Narrator
text: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.

speaker: Narrator
text: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.

speaker: Narrator
text: A neat desk. Bills, receipts, a bundle of letters addressed to 'Count de Ville'. He pays in cash and writes in a very clear hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: House-agent receipts, a cab-hire slip, a receipt for a steam launch's passage... All in cash, all in the one hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dust-sheets over everything. The Count lives here as a ghost lives in a house.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hearth with ash that has no warmth in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hall mirror. Something about it is wrong: it shows the room, and no figure that stands before it but ours.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chair set facing the door, the way a man sets a chair who expects visitors.

speaker: Narrator
text: Candles, burned down to the Count's liking: lit only for show.

speaker: Narrator
text: The front door onto Piccadilly. Its lock is fresh.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan, white as paper, a knife in one hand and the Host's envelope in the other.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor, calm, guiding.

speaker: Narrator
text: At the front door: tall, thin, a pale aquiline face. The Count, in the daylight, in a good coat, with a look of cold fury.

speaker: Narrator
text: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.

speaker: Narrator
text: Steps down to the cellar. The smell comes up them.

speaker: Narrator
text: An empty barrel. Straw within, hollowed into a nest.

speaker: Narrator
text: A broken chair and a gas-bracket with no gas.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dark lantern, lit and shuttered.

speaker: Narrator
text: The tally on the wall: six strokes. Six boxes, all here.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door back to Chicksand Street.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lord Godalming, a lamp in one hand and the Count's keys in the other. He has not smiled since Lucy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Great boxes of foul earth with the Count's mark in chalk. The smell makes my head swim.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dead, pale earth. This house is no longer the Count's.

speaker: Narrator
text: The window is boarded. River-damp comes through the cracks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sacking, the sort used to pack and muffle.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stool left by the carters.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lamp with no oil in it; I refilled it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door to Jamaica Lane.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey, rifle in the crook of his arm. He keeps one eye on the stair and one on the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: The hotel where we wait, day after day, for a ship that does not come. Mina is within.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass plate: 'Agency. Shipping intelligence.' Lord Godalming has been in and out of it all week.

speaker: Narrator
text: A closed cab waits to take us to the railway station. It will not go until every detail of our plan is settled.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grindstone at a ship-chandler's stall, with a flat whetstone left on the rim. The chandler has wandered off to his dinner.

speaker: Narrator
text: I pocketed the whetstone. I shall leave a coin on the barrel for the chandler.

speaker: Narrator
text: A seaman's chest. A good coil of rope is on top, tarred and strong.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took a coil of rope. It may prove a mercy.

speaker: Narrator
text: A crate burst by a dropped hook. One slat is a good length of seasoned ash.

speaker: Narrator
text: I pulled out a length of ash. It will make a stake or a fire.

speaker: Narrator
text: A ship's lamp on a post, burning oil against the fog. The reservoir is full.

speaker: Narrator
text: I drew off a little lamp oil into a flask.

speaker: Narrator
text: HOTEL ODESSUS. LLOYD'S AGENCY. RAILWAY STATION. And in Greek beneath: 'Sailors, mind the fog.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout Bulgarian harbour master in a salt-stained cap. He has been asked about one ship too often.

speaker: Narrator
text: A weathered Greek sailor mending a net. He crosses himself whenever someone mentions the dead of the sea.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door to the quay and the grey harbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A faded sofa where Mina rests. At every sunrise and sunset the Professor puts her in trance here, and she tells us what she hears.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lloyd's slips, the shippers' cards, a map of the Black Sea held down with a coffee-cup. Mina's typewriter sits at one end.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thumbed railway guide, open at the Varna line. Mina has underlined a time in pencil.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took the Bradshaw. Mina will want to consult it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A neat stack of typescript: every diary, every letter, every telegram. 'The facts, in order, are half the battle,' Mina says.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tiled stove-fireplace, hot as a bakery. The Roumanian chambermaid keeps it at roaring.

speaker: Narrator
text: The hotel cook is mystified by Van Helsing's demand for garlic, and has provided it by the basketful.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took two more heads of garlic. They smell worse than any soup.

speaker: Narrator
text: Roumanian novels, a German guide to the Black Sea, and a Greek psalter nobody has opened.

speaker: Narrator
text: A paraffin lamp with a green shade. It burns long into the night while Jonathan sits up.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor sits by Mina's sofa with his watch open, waiting for the sun to touch the horizon.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina, very pale, her red scar showing under her hair. She smiles to reassure us and it breaks my heart.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan sits by the window with the Ghoorka knife and a rag, doing what he can with a dull edge.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey lounges against the wall, as at ease in a hotel as on the prairie, with the Winchester within reach.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur stands over the table with his hands clasped behind him, lines of sleeplessness at his eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: The porter loiters with a salver, hoping for a telegram to deliver and a coin to follow.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the quay and the fog.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall desk with a blotter, a letter-press and a pigeonhole cabinet of telegraph forms.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lloyd's register of arrivals and sailings. Under 'C': Czarina Catherine, Roumanian-flagged, last reported off the Dardanelles on the fourth. No later entry.

speaker: Narrator
text: Slips from every port from Odessa to Alexandria, all ordered, none about our ship.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small iron stove with a kettle forever on the boil.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass lamp, polished to a mirror, on a hook by the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: A neat young clerk with ink on his cuffs. He takes Lord Godalming's money for telegrams with great composure.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy man who speaks four languages, all of them politely, and gives away nothing in any of them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A battered brig with salt-white rigging, her sails furled tight. She came in on the night tide, and no one saw her pilot.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow passage to Burgen-strasse, where the Jew Hildesheim keeps his office.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way back to the hotel where the others sleep.

speaker: Narrator
text: A path leads up to the churchyard on the hill, where something has been found.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sail-maker's bale of canvas, lying by his shop door.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took a length of spare canvas. It may be needed to patch a boat.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shipping marks: 'Mackenzie & Steinkoff, Galatz. Via Varna, per Czarina Catherine.' The office clerk stands next to it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A smoky oil-lamp in the fog. The fog clings to the river like a living thing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A barrel of lamp oil, bung loose. A tin cup hangs on a nail.

speaker: Narrator
text: I filled a flask with lamp oil.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Galatz harbour master, weighing us up as we ask about the Czarina Catherine. He has seen stranger cargoes, but not many.

speaker: Narrator
text: A clerk from Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff, shipping agents, with a ledger under his arm and a nervous cough.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plank gangway down to the quay.

speaker: Narrator
text: The hatch where the long box lay. The boards still smell of old earth, and a few dry crumbs of soil cling to the iron of the clasp.

speaker: Narrator
text: Donelson's log, open at the last pages. The entries speak of fog, a silent man, and a long box. The last line is blotted.

speaker: Narrator
text: A locker of mended canvas. The mate will not miss a yard.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took a yard of sail canvas.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tub of coiled hemp, wet but sound.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took a second coil of rope.

speaker: Narrator
text: The helm. The wheel spokes are dark with sweat. The Captain says no hand but his own turned it for nine days of fog.

speaker: Narrator
text: A square Scot with a grey-flecked ginger beard. He grips a handspike as if the argument were still going.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sailor who will not look at the hatch. He makes the sign against the evil eye when we pass.

speaker: Narrator
text: A young deckhand scrubbing planking that is already clean. He mutters about a tall man at the dead of night.

speaker: Narrator
text: Out to Burgen-strasse and the quay.

speaker: Narrator
text: A desk fitted with a hundred little drawers, each with its own lock. A set of brass scales stands on the corner.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'De Ville, Carpathian earth: 12 boxes, consigned per rail from Bucharest.' The Count used a different alias for each leg of his journey.

speaker: Narrator
text: An iron-bound box with a triple lock. Hildesheim glances at it every time we move.

speaker: Narrator
text: Row on row of leather account books, spines marked in German and Hebrew.

speaker: Narrator
text: A shallow dish of Roumanian silver. A small coin lies next to it, apparently forgotten.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took the forgotten coin. It might serve for a Slovak's hand later.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stove that has not been properly warm for years. Hildesheim does not like to spend.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dark, narrow man in a rusty black coat, who looks at everything first as a price, and then as a risk.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way back down to the harbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Slovak lies under a sheet by the wall. His throat is torn open, clean as by one bite, and nothing else is disturbed. It is not the work of wolves.

speaker: Narrator
text: Roumanian and Greek script, a name worn away. Fresh flowers lie before it.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Maria, wife of a Danubian pilot.' She has been dead seven years.

speaker: Narrator
text: An iron cross with a sprig of garlic wired to the arm. The folk here know of the Un-Dead too.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tin lantern left by the sexton, still lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: A late wild rose, hips red among the thorns. Van Helsing swears by it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I cut a sprig of wild rose.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tired old priest in a black soutane, who says his office over the dead man in a low voice and will not speak ill of wolves.

speaker: Narrator
text: A woman in a black headscarf, wringing her apron. She says she saw a very tall man in the lane.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way down to the quay and the river.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's typewriter, a lamp, a spread of maps and the whole case in order. She works quietly while the men sleep.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's typescripts, tied with a ribbon.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took the typescript; every fact we hold is in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A large-scale map of the Sereth and the Bistritza. Mina has pencilled a thin line from Galatz to the Borgo Pass.

speaker: Narrator
text: I folded the map into my coat.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stove with a copper kettle, still warm.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan lies on the bed in his boots, asleep at last.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor, awake and alert, wearing the face he put on at the grave of Lucy.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fat river-trader summoned by Lord Godalming. Money has already begun to speak.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lord Godalming's launch, named for Mina. She is small, lean and fast, with a boiler that eats wood like a furnace.

speaker: Narrator
text: The little boiler, cold at the grate. It wants wood, and plenty of it, before the gauge will rise.

speaker: Narrator
text: A compact little engine, its bearings dry as bone. A touch of oil will keep it from seizing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A neat stack of split logs on the quay. We shall need all of it before Fundu.

speaker: Narrator
text: I carried an armful of logs aboard.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bare flagstaff at the stern. A flag will give us the look of officials, and fewer questions on the river.

speaker: Narrator
text: An iron bracket at the bow, built for a searchlight.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chart table under a tarpaulin. The sheet is blank, waiting for a map.

speaker: Narrator
text: The wheel. Once all is ready, Lord Godalming will take us upstream at full steam.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan keeps watch at the bow, one hand on the kukri hilt. His eyes never leave the water.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Slovak on a drifting skiff, his lantern held low and his face turned from the light. He looks at us as at a ghost.

speaker: Narrator
text: A raftsman crouched over his poles. He crossed himself twice when the lamp struck him.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Mina lies on a shingle spit with a plank sprung amidships. A seam has opened below the waterline.

speaker: Narrator
text: The broken plank. It wants a timber splint, rope to lash it and canvas to stop the water. Three things, all of which we carry.

speaker: Narrator
text: A good straight spar, washed up by the rapids.

speaker: Narrator
text: I dragged the spar up the bank. It will serve as a splint.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pole with a red rag, planted by raftsmen. Beyond it the river drops three feet at a time.

speaker: Narrator
text: A farmer's cooking-fire, ringed with stones. His wife offers us tea in a tin cup.

speaker: Narrator
text: A farmer with an acre of sheep above the falls, who has watched our launch grind itself on his rocks with something like sympathy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan stands in the shallows with a sodden coat and a stubborn jaw, working the launch off the rocks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur rolls his sleeves, wet to the elbow, with the look of a man who would sooner fix the boat than think.

speaker: Narrator
text: A roadside sign swinging in the wind: a crowned eagle, over the legend 'Fundu'. Behind it, the lights of the little inn.

speaker: Narrator
text: FUNDU. The Sereth bridge. Bistritza. Someone has scored a fresh knife-mark under the last arm: the Szgany boat turned this way.

speaker: Narrator
text: A low sledge on runners, for the road when the snow closes it. 'Russian fashion,' says Quincey.

speaker: Narrator
text: A smoking fire at the roadside. The horses steam beside it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hay bale, with dry grass for the horses.

speaker: Narrator
text: A woolly-bearded innkeeper at his doorstep, wrapped in sheepskin. He has news for those who sit down and pay.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey, mud to his thighs, whittling a stick and watching the clouds. 'Snow by dark, Doc.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A grey wolf at the edge of the pines, watching us with yellow eyes. There are more behind it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The inn yard, where our carriage waits.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great green-tiled stove that warms the whole room. The landlady's cat lives on top of it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A huge covered basket: black bread, smoked sausage, cheese, a flask of plum brandy and a pot of paprika stew in a cloth.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took the basket. It weighs a stone.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sheepskin coats, a bear rug and two travelling-furs, hanging on pegs.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took two heavy furs and a rug. We shall be glad of them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long plait of garlic on the wall. The landlady says it keeps off 'things'.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took a plait of garlic; the Professor will be pleased.

speaker: Narrator
text: A table with a cracked inkwell, and paper. I have a letter to write to Jonathan, which he may never read.

speaker: Narrator
text: A large, kind woman who will not look at my forehead and will not stop packing food into my arms.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor, counting money onto the table, checking horses through the window.

speaker: Narrator
text: The four-in-hand the Professor assembled from the farmers' horses and a farm cart's body. Not elegant, but it has brought us across half the Carpathians.

speaker: Narrator
text: Left, a wide cart-road dropping to a valley. Not the way Jonathan described.

speaker: Narrator
text: Right, a narrow track, climbing between rocks. It looks like a sheep-walk.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grass-grown road under the pines, rising towards a black notch in the mountains: the Borgo Pass, and beyond, the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dog-rose, scarlet with hips against the snow. The Professor says it keeps the Un-Dead in their coffins.

speaker: Narrator
text: I cut a sprig of wild rose.

speaker: Narrator
text: A woodpile at a shrine to the Virgin, left for travellers.

speaker: Narrator
text: I took an armful of dry logs for the night's fire.

speaker: Narrator
text: A wooden crucifix under a small tin roof, hung with ribbons and fresh garlic.

speaker: Narrator
text: A woman with a basket of eggs. She makes the sign of the horns at my forehead and presses garlic into my palm.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor, with a hand always near his satchel, watching me out of the corner of his eye.

speaker: Narrator
text: A large grey wolf on the ridge, motionless. Its pack waits behind the rocks.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black bulk against the stars. Somewhere inside it, three women sleep and wait for dark.

speaker: Narrator
text: A circle of trampled snow, wide enough for a woman to sit in with a fire. Here the Professor will make the holy circle.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hollow in the snow ringed by stones, ready for a fire. It must burn all night.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great bough of pine, dry as paper under the snow.

speaker: Narrator
text: I broke a length of wood from the bough.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dead pine, snapped by the wind. Its resin will burn for hours.

speaker: Narrator
text: I split off more wood. The fire must last till dawn.

speaker: Narrator
text: A crucifix propped in the snow at the edge of the ring. It is not strictly needed, but the Professor says it does no harm.

speaker: Narrator
text: The carriage stands with its horses tethered in the lee. The animals scream if I go near; they have smelt something.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina sits on a fur at the heart of the ring, her shawl drawn tight, her eyes on the black castle and her hands twisting in her lap.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lovely, pale woman in white, her black hair streaming in the wind. She has no footprints in the snow.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dark sister with red lips and a hungry smile.

speaker: Narrator
text: The third sister, the fairest, reaches towards me. I know that face from Jonathan's journal.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white wolf circles the ring at a distance, baring its teeth, but it will not cross the line.

speaker: Narrator
text: A double door, eaten red with rust, the hinges frozen into the stone. It will not move for any hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: The castle's main gate, a gaping arch of black stone. A little of the wafer on its sill will keep him from using it.

speaker: Narrator
