text: Flour and salt-beef.

speaker: Narrator
text: Round, red-faced, a lifelong cook who has never in his life been afraid of a stove and has become afraid of everything else.

speaker: Narrator
text: Up to the deck.

speaker: Narrator
text: A blanket tucked tight, a pipe on the pillow, a St. Nicholas pinned above. He did not come to this bed on the night he was lost.

speaker: Narrator
text: Petrofsky sleeps in the lower berth with his boots on. He says the floor has begun to feel cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tidy as a drawer. A Swedish psalm-book lies open at the 23rd.

speaker: Narrator
text: A big man's bunk, short of a pillow.

speaker: Narrator
text: Chisels, adze, spikes and a heavy iron crowbar, kept sharp by a man who thought he was only a carpenter.

speaker: Narrator
text: The carpenter's crowbar, two feet of black iron. It will lift a lid, or a lid's nails, or a man's courage.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bundle of torches dipped in pitch, for the boat in a calm and the hold in a pinch.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take a torch. A lantern shows what is there; a torch shows what flees.

speaker: Narrator
text: A slate left on the mess table, scrawled with names in three hands, with a fourth line crossed out and written again.

speaker: Narrator
text: Saints nailed over every bunk, St. Nicholas, the Mother of God, St. Elias, with a small iron cross at the foot of each.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sea-bags and oilskins.

speaker: Narrator
text: A seamed, dark, silent hand who has sailed with me nine years. Tonight he is mending a net with hands that do not look at it.

speaker: Narrator
text: My second mate, a quiet, bookish man who steers by compass and prays by habit.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back along the deck.

speaker: Narrator
text: Coiled cable, stiff with salt. A man could lose a hand in it, or find one lost.

speaker: Narrator
text: I cut a length of good manila from the bitter end. A fathom, no more, and it is enough to hold a man to a wheel.

speaker: Narrator
text: The bowsprit points at nothing. The fog begins at its tip.

speaker: Narrator
text: The red and green lights burn dull in the fog. A passing ship would see them. None passes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lying wet against the rail, a blue knitted cap with a name sewn in the band: PETROFSKY.

speaker: Narrator
text: Petrofsky's cap. I fold it in my pocket for the day his mother asks me what became of him.

speaker: Narrator
text: A smear of black earth on the planks.

speaker: Narrator
text: The chain-locker.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tall, thin, white as paper, standing quite still at the stem-head and looking out at the fog. Looking at me, now.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back down the steps.

speaker: Narrator
text: Worn smooth by twenty years of hands. The spokes are the length of a man's reach.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass barometer in a mahogany case. The needle has been drifting down all morning.

speaker: Narrator
text: The compass card, steady as a priest. For now the ship points where I tell her.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chalk-board for the sail-plan. The mate and I argue over it. Today it is mine to settle.

speaker: Narrator
text: Flags, a bell and a lamp. They would be a great help if there were anyone to signal.

speaker: Narrator
text: He has offered to steer and watch, and keep the sail trimmed. Those are not a man's whole duties but he has taken them.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black oak, dragon-headed. It was my father's, and before him another's, and every one of them sat in it as if it were a mistake that could be corrected.

speaker: Narrator
text: A map of the border is pinned under three daggers. The fortress of Severin, burning in red wax, stands where the Turkish ink comes closest.

speaker: Narrator
text: The counsellor's chair, with a cushion upon it for a back that has served three princes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Velvet. Vlaicu will not sit in anything without it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A log the thickness of a man burns on it. Nobody who sits near it is warm.

speaker: Narrator
text: The coiled dragon of the Order, and beneath it, in faded thread: 'Founded by Sigismund, King of Hungary, in the year 1408. Whoso wears the Dragon keeps the gate of Christendom.'

speaker: Narrator
text: The annals of the principality in four hands, none of which agree about anything.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lamp-oil for the beacons, in a barrel with the garrison's mark burned in the lid. Half of it is meant for the tower.

speaker: Narrator
text: I fill a flask from the barrel. The tower will want it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pens, sand and a pot of black ink gone to jelly. A clerk has been working at it since the siege began.

speaker: Narrator
text: A clerk's neat draft: 'To the captains of the levy: assemble at the camp below the Reed ford...' It has no seal and so no force.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the draft order. It wants a seal.

speaker: Narrator
text: A candle, a stick of green wax and a brass press shaped to fit a ring. It waits for the ring.

speaker: Narrator
text: To my father's chamber, and the stair beyond.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow spiral up to the battlements.

speaker: Narrator
text: The great gate and the road to the army. I do not leave until the order is sealed and sent, the beacon is lit, my brother is dealt with and I carry my father's hammer.

speaker: Narrator
text: Counsellor to my father and to his father. A grey beard, a voice like a closing door, and the best advice in the principality delivered with the worst timing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Furs, rings and a smile that arrives a moment after the thought behind it. He commands three hundred spears and mentions it often.

speaker: Narrator
text: My younger brother, back from the Sultan's court with Turkish manners, Turkish silks and an excellent opinion of himself. We have the same eyes. I have never been sure about the rest.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thin rider in a muddy cloak who has been waiting by the door for an order that has not come.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wide as a threshing-floor and cold as one. I have not yet slept in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: An iron-bound chest with a dial of years on the lid. Whatever it holds, my father locked it himself.

speaker: Narrator
text: Vlad Dracul in marble, wearing the Order's collar. On the plinth: 'Invested 1431, at Nuremberg.' It is the year he is proudest of. It is not the year of the Order.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mail, a helm and the heavy iron-headed hammer my father swung on the Danube. It is lighter than it looks, and I am not sure whether I am meant to be flattered.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take my father's hammer. It fits my hand as if it had been waiting.

speaker: Narrator
text: Letters, a wax-stub and a map of the border with the Turkish side left blank, as though no one dared to draw it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Five candles. Four of them are lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: Built for two. Warms one.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hours, a Livy in Latin and three treatises on fortification, all well-thumbed. My father read to be believed.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the hall.

speaker: Narrator
text: Boyar Corvin's daughter. She has a clear grey stare and an unfashionable habit of saying exactly what she means. We were children together in this castle. We are not children now.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cut stone, blackened by seven centuries of other people's fires.

speaker: Narrator
text: An iron brazier on a stone foot, stacked with split logs. The wood is bone dry, and so is the pitch. It would not light for weeks of trying without something to feed it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The logs are dark with oil. A spark would finish the work.

speaker: Narrator
text: It roars. On the far ridge the answering flame has doubled.

speaker: Narrator
text: A resin torch in an iron bracket by the stair door, the only one on the tower that is not burned out.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the torch from its bracket.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shuttered, so as not to be a target.

speaker: Narrator
text: Green water. Even the pine-needles have given it up.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back down to the hall.

speaker: Narrator
text: Thirty years on this tower. He knows every star by the name it has in the barracks, which is not the one in the almanac.

speaker: Narrator
text: The castle gate is behind me, up the hill. The old road has taken the shape of a long habit.

speaker: Narrator
text: One arm points to the camp, the other to a ford with a Turkish name someone has tried to scratch out.

speaker: Narrator
text: Axle cracked, a mattress on top, three children in a heap and a grandmother in front, who has not looked back once.

speaker: Narrator
text: Many hooves, small, wrapped round with felt: the marks are deep and smeared, not the clean crescents of shod horses. Whoever it was came by night, and does not want to be heard.

speaker: Narrator
text: A wooden Christ under a little roof, carved by someone who loved wood more than anatomy. Fresh flowers lie at its foot, from people who have nothing else to give.

speaker: Narrator
text: A candle in a tin, left for travellers by someone who will not know their names.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lightning took it a long time ago. Wolves use it to mark their ground.

speaker: Narrator
text: She sits straight, with a rag-wrapped bundle on her knees. She looks through me rather than at me, which is how a prince is looked at on the road.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three grey shapes at the edge of the lantern-light. They are not afraid of the cart, nor of me. They are weighing something.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pine knots and a kettle. Twenty men sit round it who have all been telling stories, and are all sure the others are lying.

speaker: Narrator
text: A trestle by the commander's tent, with a vellum map held down by four stones.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sheepskins on bracken. A boy sleeps there with his boots on, because he has been told to.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pavilion for the lords, of which only the pole stands in a convincing line.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rations: black bread, onions and salt pork. In a country of mountains, the army marches on onions.

speaker: Narrator
text: Water for the horses, and for the men who would rather it were wine.

speaker: Narrator
text: Forage, tents, the camp-priest's portable altar and a crate marked 'FRAGILE' in a hand nobody will claim.

speaker: Narrator
text: The track runs down through the reeds to the river. It is a mile of mud, and I should know exactly which ford before I walk it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back up to the road and the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: Captain of my father's guard, now of mine. A neck like a bull's and the memory of every battle the principality has lost.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lean, wind-burned, a goatskin cloak over mail. He has just come in from the river, and it shows on his boots.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Turkish light-horseman, tied to a wagon-wheel, with a dignified sulk. He glares at a spot just left of my face.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gaunt man in black who was not here a moment ago. He has the stillness of a thing that has never had to hurry, and shadows lie wrong around his feet.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grey pony with felt tied round its hooves. It fell in the shallows with an arrow in its flank and the river is not yet done with it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Somebody already planted stakes across the shallows. They are not ours.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pitch and tow. They were going to burn the bridge-timbers.

speaker: Narrator
text: A green horse-tail standard on a spear, snapped. A crescent of tin hangs from it by one wire.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the broken standard. I do not know why. A prince should remember what he has fought.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the camp.

speaker: Narrator
text: Light cavalry, felt on their hooves and knives between their teeth. They have not seen me yet.

speaker: Narrator
text: He crouches in the reeds with a short bow, watching the camp-fires across the water.

speaker: Narrator
text: A broad man in a steel cap, with a curved sword he does not draw. He is sure that tonight belongs to him.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black flat boat with a lantern at the bow. It goes out into the mist without a rower and comes back without a mark on it, they say. The ferryman must be paid first.

speaker: Narrator
text: Seven stones, none of them upright. Something older than the school stood here and was not asked.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cairn of lake-stones with an iron cross. In the cairn, pressed in by a careful thumb, a silver coin that no passer-by has dared to take.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the coin. 'He will not need it,' I tell the cairn, and the lake seems to hear.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Scholars only. The tenth pays more.' The last four words have been scratched deeper by a different hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: It burns green and gives no shadows.

speaker: Narrator
text: Standing in the water as it has stood since its roots drowned.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hooded, tall, and so still that a gull has settled on his shoulder. He does not breathe visibly. He holds out his palm without turning his head.

speaker: Narrator
text: A slab of black stone with three hollows in its face: one for a bowl, one for a disc, one for a lamp. What goes in them, and in what order, is for the scholar to know.

speaker: Narrator
text: A single book chained to a slanted board. Nobody opens it for a reason.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench scarred by nine scholars' knives. 'Teodor was here.' Nobody knows which Teodor.

speaker: Narrator
text: The worn hollow where a scholar sat for an entire winter without speaking.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rows of slates. One bears, in chalk: 'Aqua suscitat. Argentum ligat. Ignis signat.' The last word has been underlined, and then, lower, 'But always in this order.'

speaker: Narrator
text: It shows the room correctly, and everyone in it but me. I stand a long time before I realise how little I mind.

speaker: Narrator
text: It burns without smoke or sound. Held near the palm, it gives no heat.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door to the lake and the ferry.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iron, black, banded with the same hollow-and-disc mark as the altar. The lock has a face like a wolf's.

speaker: Narrator
text: A spiral stair that goes further than the mountain. The tithe-chamber is below.

speaker: Narrator
text: Whatever he was, he has not been that for centuries. He teaches in a flat, kind, amused voice, as a cat teaches a mouse the geography of the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: Another scholar, my age, dark and quick, in a student's black. He keeps the library key on a cord round his neck and takes pleasure in showing it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pale boy of seventeen, copying a diagram with trembling hands. He has not been home in three winters.

speaker: Narrator
text: The only woman in the school, silent, with ink on her wrists and a face I would not wish to meet at a crossroads at midnight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Books on chains, as the old libraries did. These chains are to keep the books from the readers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Treatises on storm, hail and thunder, in a flowing hand. 'To raise a tempest, find the storm already in the sky.'

speaker: Narrator
text: 'De Lupis,' 'On the Speech of Beasts' and a leather-bound 'Wolf-Tongue Primer' in a child's hand. The margins are sharp with bite-marks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pages that are cold to touch. I decide not to read them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thin red codex on a reading-stand, open at a diagram of three vessels. The opening line reads: 'Three things wake a rite. Water first, to open the way. Silver next, to bind what has come. Fire last, to seal it.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A black table, scarred round a single circle where something warm once stood.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great scroll on rollers, signed by every scholar who has ever sat below. Ten names stand against each year. Ink is wet on the last line.

speaker: Narrator
text: Candles of black wax, burning with a flame that does not wag.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the lecture hall.

speaker: Narrator
text: The seats are carved from the mountain itself. Ten in a ring, nine worn smooth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Taken in a winter of thin rain. Nobody remembers his name.

speaker: Narrator
text: The tenth seat. It is the only one with a cushion, and the cushion is a hide of something black.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fire that gives a green light and a very faint sound like speech, three rooms off.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grating set in the floor. Beneath, a breath of warm air that smells of wet iron and horse.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way back to the school.

speaker: Narrator
text: He is taller down here, and his shadow now has a shape of its own, which does not agree with his.

speaker: Narrator
text: The lid is nailed and sealed in lead. I am inside. I have been inside long enough that the idea no longer frightens me. Something heavy would break the lid.

speaker: Narrator
text: Torn open, from within. A year ago I would have called that impossible.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Vlad Dracul, Knight of the Dragon.' Beside it, a smaller slab: 'Mircea, his son,' for my elder brother, whom I never knew.

speaker: Narrator
text: The dragon is cut on the lid, but her face is not. She always said the dragon would be enough.

speaker: Narrator
text: They were lit when I was carried in. Each one burned down and was replaced, until someone ceased to replace them.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iron-bound and stoutly barred from the other side. A recess in the lock is shaped to fit the family ring.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the Voivode was blessed, and where the bread of the Mass is blessed. I put my hand near it and feel nothing but cold, which tells me nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: It is only wood and silver. I look at it for a long time. It is only a cross; it does not burn; it does not even disapprove. I should have learned something from that.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the boyars sat on feast-days with their sword-belts loosened.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where I sat as a boy, bored, drawing dragons in the dust of the prayer-book.

speaker: Narrator
text: A new slab, still pale, and a sprig of withered rosemary. 'Ileana Corvin, who waited.' There is a small silver ring on the stone.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down to stubs.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down to the family vault, where I was laid.

speaker: Narrator
text: The castle's old priest, wounded and propped against a pew. A dark stain has crept across his habit. He is looking at me the way men look at the sea before a storm.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two Norman towers, a great west front, and four hundred years of rooks. Mr. Hawkins says it is the only client the firm has never sent a bill.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass plate worn to a shine by thirty years of the housemaid. The door of the office.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tidy gate and a tidy bell. Mina Murray teaches the junior class here and has views on the bell.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bolts of calico in the window and, above, my two rooms with the green blind.

speaker: Narrator
text: A little roofed gate where coffins once waited for the priest. Not today, thank God.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fountain with a tin cup on a chain, and a motto: 'Ye shall draw water with joy.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Warm from the sun. A clerk is asleep upon the Times beside it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Unlit. Lamplighter's ladder leans on the next one, abandoned for his dinner.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Station 1 mile. London 194 miles.' Someone has added, in pencil, 'and back'.

speaker: Narrator
text: Stand No. 4. The cabman has a whip, a pipe, and a very low opinion of the Great Western Railway.

speaker: Narrator
text: Green water and three drowned leaves.

speaker: Narrator
text: A girl with a basket of violets and a very good memory for faces.

speaker: Narrator
text: A big man in a drab coat, who has driven half of Exeter to its weddings and the other half to its funerals.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mahogany, leather-topped, and as orderly as a conscience. A decanter, a blotter, and a calendar open at May.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bundle of heavy cream letters in a small, upright foreign hand. The envelopes bear a Transylvanian stamp and the seal of a wolf's head.

speaker: Narrator
text: I tie the bundle with its pink tape and put it in my breast pocket. Mr. Hawkins has told me to keep it safe.

speaker: Narrator
text: A steel pen, a bottle of Stephens' ink, and a pen-wiper in the shape of a hedgehog.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Hawkins nods as I pocket the pen. 'Take it. I have three.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Our own replies to the Count, copied in damp tissue. A history of the purchase in nine letters.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall desk with a sloping top and a stool, from which Mr. Pell has watched the street for thirty-one years.

speaker: Narrator
text: Every volume of Chancery since the Restoration. Only the dust is complete.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black tin boxes marked with the names of every family in Devon. 'Harker' is not among them; my father never had the money to need a solicitor.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fire kept up from October to May and sometimes in June. Mr. Hawkins says his bones are older than he is.

speaker: Narrator
text: Seven minutes fast. Mr. Hawkins likes his clerks early, and the clock knows it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Deep, hard, and designed to make a man tell the truth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Four umbrellas, none of them mine, and a cricket bat.

speaker: Narrator
text: The street door, with the brass plate behind it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A low oak door with an iron keyhole the size of a florin. The firm's old papers lie behind it.

speaker: Narrator
text: My employer and, since my father died, something nearer to a father: white-haired, spectacled, kind, and never wrong about a deed.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow man in black alpaca with a pen behind each ear. He has the muniment key on a chain across his waistcoat and will tell you so.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way back up to Mr. Hawkins's office.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black japanned box stamped 'PURCHASES - TRANSYLVANIA - PRIVATE'. Mr. Hawkins has the surveys inside, and a lock that wants its own key.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rolls and bundles in red tape. A tabby cat has made its bed in 'Smith v. Smith'.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three-legged, with a cushion that has been sat flat by clerks since the Reform Bill.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hung from a hook by the shelves. There are scorch marks where the clerks tapped their pipes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lumps of broken wax, in every colour. A box of the firm's own old stamps lies on top.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wet-ringed and ink-spattered. On it, a magnifying-glass and a note in Mr. Pell's hand: 'Surveys NOT to leave the room except by Mr. Hawkins.'

speaker: Narrator
text: The schoolroom door, with a coat-peg for each child.

speaker: Narrator
text: A chalk-drawn map of the Exe, and under it a line in neat shorthand. Mina has copied it out in longhand beside: 'Courage, mon ami.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Slates, a ruler, a jar of pens, and a pile of copybooks, marked in red with kind, firm ticks.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Phonographic Teacher.' Mina has been teaching herself shorthand, so as to be useful to a husband. She has not said which one.

speaker: Narrator
text: Europe, with Transylvania a smudge of green by a thumbprint. Mina has underlined it in pencil.

speaker: Narrator
text: Carved with initials, and one confession: 'H.S. loves a ginger cat.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold. The children have drawn a smiling face in the soot.

speaker: Narrator
text: A red geranium on the sill, the only thing in the room not marked for punctuality.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina in her grey school dress, ink on her finger, a pencil in her hair, and the kind of attention that makes one feel the only man in Devon.

speaker: Narrator
text: Seven years old and standing on the bench to see the visitor properly.

speaker: Narrator
text: Eleven steps and the smell of calico.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass-bound sea-trunk with a four-wheel combination lock, taken from my father's room when he died. I have never opened it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow bed made with Mrs. Dunmore's hospital corners.

speaker: Narrator
text: My shorthand notes, a razor-strop, and a half-written letter to Mina, which I keep failing to finish.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout little book bound in black. Mina gave it to me for the journey and said I must keep it in shorthand 'so that nobody can read your nonsense but me'.

speaker: Narrator
text: I put the diary in my coat. Mina is right: a traveller who writes nothing down has seen nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Half packed. Shirts, collars, and a small box of seidlitz powders in case the Count's cooking disagrees with me.

speaker: Narrator
text: Blackstone, Bradshaw's Railway Guide, a dog-eared 'Murray's Handbook for the Continent', and nothing a young man should be ashamed of.

speaker: Narrator
text: It shows the same plain face as every other morning: an honest, tired young man who is going somewhere.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs. Dunmore's best, loaned on condition of no pipe.

speaker: Narrator
text: My landlady: a stout widow with a perfect understanding of the movements of every lodger in the street.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the Close.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'THOMAS HARKER, SURGEON'S ASSISTANT, AND MARGARET HIS WIFE. HE DIED IN THE FEVER OF 1874, SHE FOLLOWED HIM IN THE SPRING. THEIR SON JONATHAN WAS TEN.' Someone has put snowdrops here.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'ALICE ANN, AGED 3 YEARS. SUFFER THE LITTLE CHILDREN.' A dead wreath of pimpernels.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'JOB TREMLETT, 47 YEARS SEXTON OF THIS PARISH, WHO DIGGED GRAVES FOR OTHERS AND NOW LIES IN ONE FOR HIMSELF.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A cross, leaning gently towards the church as if to hear the sermon.

speaker: Narrator
text: Older than the church, and holding up its limbs like a man who has seen much and said little.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench in the sun.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stumpy Saxon tower and a Georgian porch.

speaker: Narrator
text: Old stalks, kept in water by someone who loves them. The verger, perhaps. Or Mina.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bent old man with a billhook and a sharp tongue, who has dug the graves of three generations of Exeter.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way out, and back to the station.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ranks of leather-backed volumes of pasted slips. Under TRANSYLVANIA, one entry is marked with a red ticket: 'Geography and Ethnology of the Carpathians, press-mark K.7'. The other entries are only history.

speaker: Narrator
text: A shallow tray of printed call-slips: Title, Press-mark, Name of Reader.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take a blank slip. The Museum prints them in a shade of green that makes every reader feel guilty.

speaker: Narrator
text: Green baize, brass lamps, and a notice: 'Readers are respectfully requested not to lean on the books.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A sleeping gentleman is using the Peerage as a pillow.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pinned flat on the wall: Buda-Pesth, the Danube, the Carpathians. The Borgo Pass is a pencilled tick. A reader has written beside Transylvania: 'whirlpool of races'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bust of a long-forgotten trustee with a nose broken in 1851.

speaker: Narrator
text: An inkwell chained to the table by order of the Trustees. Even ink cannot be trusted in London.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grave, spectacled man at the high desk, who has never raised his voice and never needed to.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bald, white-bearded, buried in a folio of Hungarian wills. He has the look of a man who has read the whole of Europe and found it wanting.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own window, barred inside by a Count's courtesy. Beneath it, a ledge a foot wide and a drop that does not bear looking at.

speaker: Narrator
text: A rope of ivy thick as my wrist, rooted in the stone. It runs down and to the left. The leaves are torn, as if something heavy had gone down it recently.

speaker: Narrator
text: A rusted iron ring in the wall, once for a banner-pole. The rust on it is rubbed bright on the lower curve, where a hand has taken weight.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone block that has shifted a finger's breadth. Beside it the lime is pale and scraped, as if a boot-heel had caught it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dozen bats under the eave. They are all facing the same window: the one on the east corner.

speaker: Narrator
text: Open to the night. The shutters hang back as though somebody has just gone through, and from within comes the smell of old earth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shut tight; dust on the sill, no scrape, no bat-dropping. Nobody has used this one for a century.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way I came in. The wall below is a thousand feet of moonlit drop.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great heap of gold of every kind: Roman, British, Austrian, Hungarian, Greek and Turkish, covered with a film of dust as if it had lain long in the ground. None of it less than three hundred years old.

speaker: Narrator
text: I fill one pocket with a handful of old coin. The Count has too much to miss it, and I may need to buy a way out.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cup set with jewels, and so old that its enamel has worn to the shape of a thumb.

speaker: Narrator
text: Laid for a meal that was never eaten. Gold plate, a decanter, and no sign of a servant's hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hung with faded velvet. The sheets have not been slept in. I think no one sleeps here.

speaker: Narrator
text: A nail in the wall, high and plain, with a paler square of plaster below it. A mirror hung here once. There is none in the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long wardrobe of black oak, and in the shelves, ledgers in an old Latin hand. The last entry is dated the day I arrived.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy iron poker by a hearth that has not seen a fire in my time.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the poker. It is heavy, and I feel better for it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A ring of keys hanging from a hook, each a different age and size.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door that gives, in the Count's own tower, onto the winding stair and the old chapel below.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back up to the Count's room.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great iron-bound door barred on the inside by a beam, the way the earth-boxes come and go.

speaker: Narrator
text: The bar of the postern: a trunk of oak, shot into iron staples. It will lift if levered.

speaker: Narrator
text: The largest box, its lid thrown back. Within lies the Count, with open eyes like stones, red lips, and a cheek that has no breath in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Earth, fresh from the hills. The smell is unmistakable.

speaker: Narrator
text: Earth heaped to the brim. They are all for England.

speaker: Narrator
text: A single tall candle burning at the Count's head, no taller than a thumb, and with no melted wax.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone altar cracked across. The cross above it has been taken down and put face to the wall.

speaker: Narrator
text: A knight's tomb with the head broken. The inscription is Slavonic; I can read 'unreconciled' only.

speaker: Narrator
text: Old bones, heaped by the wall. Nobody has said a prayer for them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A spade, still stuck in a heap of clay. I could break the Count's skull with it; I have thought of it twice already.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take up the spade. If the thing in the box wakes, I shall at least have an answer.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plank bridge across a deep gully, with the middle plank rotted away. A river roars below.

speaker: Narrator
text: A woodcutter's stack, split and left. There is a stout plank among the logs, long enough to bridge a gap.

speaker: Narrator
text: I drag out a long, stout plank and shoulder it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fire of broken pine, and above it a cook-pot. The smell is of onion and goat. A little caravan stands in the dark beyond.

speaker: Narrator
text: Painted wheels and a tarpaulin tied with rope. It is clean in a way that tells me they have been here a long time.

speaker: Narrator
text: A crude wooden cross with a rag tied on it. Somebody has left a bunch of dried garlic at its foot.

speaker: Narrator
text: A wayside offering. I take none of it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take a head of garlic. The peasants taught me that much, and I was a fool to laugh.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Bistritz - 28 hours. Buda-Pesth - 6 days.' Someone has scratched out 'Buda-Pesth' and written, in a bad hand, 'God knows'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gaunt woman in a red kerchief, who watches me over the cook-pot with a look neither friendly nor threatening.

speaker: Narrator
text: An old man in sheepskin, leaning on a crook with a whistle at his lips.

speaker: Narrator
text: Eyes in the gorse, low and yellow. They have been following me for a hundred yards.

speaker: Narrator
text: Open to the lime trees and a little warm air.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white door with a small brass crucifix.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain iron-framed bed. The sheets have been changed many times; I do not remember any of them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tidy bed. Its occupant has recovered, and left a holy picture on the pillow.

speaker: Narrator
text: An old Magyar peasant sleeps there, with a rosary wound round his fingers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bottles of bromide, a water-jug, and a fever chart pinned to the wall: forty-two days of it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pen and inkwell left on the table after the doctor's rounds.

speaker: Narrator
text: The doctor said I might borrow his pen to write to my fiancee. I do so.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small trunk with my initials, in which the Sisters keep my torn coat, my shirt and my pocket-book.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the lining of my coat, the diary. The leather is torn and stained, but every page is there.

speaker: Narrator
text: A large crucifix in silver. I cannot look at it long without weeping.

speaker: Narrator
text: A little desk where Sister Agatha writes her letters. Paper, a sander, and a half-finished embroidery.

speaker: Narrator
text: A few sheets of hospital paper with the crest of the Sisters.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sister Agatha lets me have a sheet of her paper.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Sister of St. Joseph, small, quick, with gentle grey eyes and a Hungarian-German English all her own.

speaker: Narrator
text: The hospital's physician: a lean man in a frock-coat who makes his rounds like a drill sergeant and has the voice of a country priest.

speaker: Narrator
text: An old drover with a bandaged leg, who has been here nearly as long as I have and keeps count of the days with matchsticks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina. She has come, in her travelling dress, white from the long journey, and she is holding my hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back into the cool of the hospital.

speaker: Narrator
text: Old, wide, humming with bees. The scent of blossom is almost unbearable after the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench with one place worn smoother than the rest.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bush of white roses, in flower. Sister Agatha says they will be wanted for a wedding.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sister Agatha has said I may cut one. I choose the whitest and carry it indoors as if it were glass.

speaker: Narrator
text: A shallow well with a rope and bucket. The water is sweet and ice-cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small grey stone with seven names. Under them: 'They served the sick.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A statue of the Carpenter, with a lily and a moss-grown plane.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gnarled old man with a watering-can and the placid look of one who has seen every sort of patient go by.

speaker: Narrator
text: A girl in a shawl, mending slowly from a fever of her own.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the ward.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white altar-cloth, brass candlesticks and a vase of white roses.

speaker: Narrator
text: Above the altar, a crucifix and the legend 'Ecce Agnus Dei'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A rack of votive candles in red glass. Dripping wax has run down the rack and frozen in long tears.

speaker: Narrator
text: A painted shrine, with fresh flowers and rows of tiny tablets. The hospital's patients leave letters here for those who cannot be reached.

speaker: Narrator
text: Plain oak, with a kneeler worn by a century of knees.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stoup of cold holy water at the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grey, kind clergyman, in Buda-Pesth these thirty years for the sake of British sailors and the odd stranded traveller.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina, in her travelling dress, with white roses in her hand and Jonathan's name already half on her lips.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sister Agatha, dressed in her Sunday veil, standing as witness with a look of fierce delight.

speaker: Narrator
text: White counterpane, blue hangings, and the dent where I read until the candle guttered. It has never once failed to be comfortable.

speaker: Narrator
text: Brushes, ribbons and a hand-glass. Far too many ribbons.

speaker: Narrator
text: A girl in it with a pink face and her hair half up. She looks as though she has been told a secret.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thin cream envelope in Arthur's careful, upright hand, addressed to me and not yet opened.

speaker: Narrator
text: I read it at the window. It is the shortest letter I have ever had from a gentleman, and I read it four times.

speaker: Narrator
text: A candle, a novel, a glass of water and a little pot of forget-me-not seeds from Mina.

speaker: Narrator
text: A squat bottle of black ink. Mamma says I use more ink than the whole of the Admiralty.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the inkwell. If I am to write to Mina this week, I shall want it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Seven white frocks and one blue. I have been told this is unadventurous.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tennyson, a lady's cookery-book that is only a disguise, and Mina's pressed fern in a green frame.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where I sit to be pinned into things.

speaker: Narrator
text: To the stairs and the parlour.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hannah, with an armful of linen and a look of fond despair.

speaker: Narrator
text: Set for six. Mamma's count of the guests increases whenever she looks at it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stand with a green jar on it and the sad stalks of last week's arrangement. A vase is not a flower until someone has taken some trouble over it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mamma's walnut escritoire, with a little brass lock. Mina's letters are kept in the left-hand drawer.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small table by the window, where the light is best for letters.

speaker: Narrator
text: A silver tray for cards. It has been very full this week.

speaker: Narrator
text: A card, slightly bent, left by a tall gentleman who would not wait to be announced.

speaker: Narrator
text: A card in a large, rapid hand. It will not stay in my pocket for long without being read.

speaker: Narrator
text: A square piano with music open on it. I have been playing the same page since February.

speaker: Narrator
text: Chintz roses on a sofa. Real roses in the garden look rather superior.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mamma's. She sits with her back to the draught and her face to the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: The visitors' chair. Occupied this month by a succession of men who all want to be somewhere else.

speaker: Narrator
text: Unlit by day; it is waiting for a better occasion.

speaker: Narrator
text: Up to the first floor and my own room.

speaker: Narrator
text: Open to the lawn.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs. Westenra, in grey silk, with a heart she cannot spare and a talent for seeing exactly what she wants to see.

speaker: Narrator
text: The arbour is thick with roses, and the wild one at its foot has opened first, as it does every year.

speaker: Narrator
text: I pick the wild rose from the foot of the arbour. The thorn takes a drop of blood and I suck my thumb like a child.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tall white lilies, standing in a row like bridesmaids.

speaker: Narrator
text: I cut three white lilies, as tall as my elbow. They will do for the back of any vase.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone sundial with forget-me-nots growing round its foot. The motto reads: 'I count only the sunny hours'. It must be very slow work.

speaker: Narrator
text: A handful of forget-me-nots, small and blue, no taller than my finger.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench in the shade, for reading and for pretending to read.

speaker: Narrator
text: A folded sheet left on the bench. It has my name on it in a hand I have seen on medical charts.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dr. Seward must have left it before he went in to Mamma. I read it, and then I fold it very small.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lace cloth, a pot of Darjeeling and a plate of what Mamma calls seed-cake.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mamma's.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mine.

speaker: Narrator
text: Geraniums in military ranks.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white house with every window open.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the house.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dr. Seward, young, grave, and visibly rehearsing something under his breath. He holds his hat as though it were a patient.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Morris of Texas, lounging against the fence like it was built for him. His boots are covered in Surrey.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur Holmwood, tall and fair and very pale with nerves. He has a rose in his buttonhole, and has forgotten it is there.

speaker: Narrator
text: The narrower bed, nearer the window. Mina took the other, and the key, and the habit of locking the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's bed, made with a neatness that is almost a reproach.

speaker: Narrator
text: Everything I own that is not on the road to Whitby, folded in tissue.

speaker: Narrator
text: A window-seat, cushioned in faded cretonne, with a long view of the harbour and the Abbey.

speaker: Narrator
text: My white slippers, which I left clean by the bed last night. The soles are grey with mud, and the hems of my nightgown are wet.

speaker: Narrator
text: A jug, a bowl and a cracked soap-dish.

speaker: Narrator
text: I look rather pale this week. I think it is the Whitby light.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's books on one shelf and my novels on another, shelved with a sort of silent argument.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina keeps it filled. She says she will not be caught out in the dark.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down to the street, and up to the cliff.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mamma, in a shawl, anxious about draughts and about nothing in particular.

speaker: Narrator
text: Our seat, facing the sea. A brass plate on the back says it was given in loving memory of someone who sat here for forty years. The wind is cold on the back of my neck.

speaker: Narrator
text: The ruins stand over the town like an unfinished sentence.

speaker: Narrator
text: Stone steps cut into the cliff, down to the town and the harbour. Mr. Swales swears there are one hundred and ninety-nine.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Sacred to the memory of a mariner, lost at sea.' I read that on every one of them. The sea has an enormous appetite for stones.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lichen has taken the last of the name.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cross leans seaward, as though it has been listening.

speaker: Narrator
text: Smoothed by generations of people who know exactly what the weather is going to do.

speaker: Narrator
text: A coastguard's lamp, not yet lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'To the Crescent and the town.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina Murray, in a straw hat, with a writing-pad on her knee and anxious eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Old Swales of the East Cliff, nearly ninety, and as hard as the stones he sits among.

speaker: Narrator
text: Our seat. The wood is cold and damp, and I am sitting on it. I do not remember sitting down.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black against a dark blue sky, and one window lit that has no business being lit.

speaker: Narrator
text: There is no bell here. The sound comes from the headland, from the harbour, from inside my own chest, slow, slow, slow.

speaker: Narrator
text: The steps go down into the dark. Down is the way home, if I can stand up.

speaker: Narrator
text: It flutters at the edge of my sight and is gone when I turn.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tall, dark, and pale, with eyes that are very red when they look at me. He has been waiting.

speaker: Narrator
text: Step after step after step, worn into hollows by the feet of sailors' wives. I must go down. I must not lose count.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'In memory of ... who departed this life.' Everyone departs; it is only a matter of whose bell they hear.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cross points downhill, to the harbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lichen, cold and wet, the same dead colour as the sea.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bat, flitting in and out of the moon. I used to think they were charming.

speaker: Narrator
text: A single lamp at the bottom of the steps, swinging in the wind.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina, in her dressing-gown with a shawl over her arm and her hair in a plait. She looks as though she has been running.

speaker: Narrator
text: Blue hangings, white counterpane, and a heap of white flowers on the pillow, which Dr. Van Helsing says is medicine. They smell exactly like a kitchen.

speaker: Narrator
text: A great ugly wreath of garlic blossoms. I am told not to take it off.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pen, paper, ink. A long, steady sheet of paper with nothing yet written on it. The window beyond it is open to a night I am going to remember for a very short time.

speaker: Narrator
text: My father's letter, written to me when I was ten, with forget-me-nots pressed in every fold. I held it in Whitby on the night I would have died, and it held me back. I know what I shall do with it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Someone has sat in it every night this month. I have stopped asking who.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tennyson, and Mina's pressed fern in its green frame. The shelves look as bright as they did in the spring; it is odd that they should.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dr. Seward in the bedside chair, asleep, his hand on my wrist. The best friend any foolish girl ever refused.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mamma, asleep in an armchair with her hands folded over her heart, on Dr. Van Helsing's strict orders.

speaker: Narrator
text: Miss Hallam's desk: a ledger, a bell, and a pen-tray laid out as if for inspection.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shorthand primers, a ruler, and a tin of hairpins I confiscated from the third form.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout steel hairpin, the sort Pitman's disciples use to clean their pens.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take a hairpin. It has got more people out of trouble than any other single invention.

speaker: Narrator
text: Initials cut with a compass-point, and a poem to a boy called Ernest.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tidy to a fault. Edith Marsh sits here and trusts nobody's blotting-paper but her own.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dora Pike's desk, with a page of sums folded very small under the lid.

speaker: Narrator
text: Eleven small hats, eleven small shawls, and one rain-cape that belongs to nobody.

speaker: Narrator
text: Banked for the summer. The kettle on top is the only warm thing in the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: Blind, noble and chalk-dusted. The girls draw spectacles on him in Lent.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow door with a keyhole. Miss Hallam keeps it locked since the winter of the burst pipe.

speaker: Narrator
text: The way out, to my rooms and to the station.

speaker: Narrator
text: The headmistress, upright as a ruler, with spectacles she looks over rather than through.

speaker: Narrator
text: A girl of thirteen with a notebook of her own, in which she records, I suspect, the faults of her elders.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pale, quiet, a good hand at sums. Her sleeve-cuffs have been turned and re-turned until they are thin as paper.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy table with four ink-rings and a place worn pale by two generations of elbows.

speaker: Narrator
text: A little can with a long spout, left by a mechanic who did not return.

speaker: Narrator
text: I take the oil-can's last good drops, decanted into a medicine phial.

speaker: Narrator
text: Foolscap, quills, sealing-wax, and a great many tins that once held something else.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pitman, Gurney, Taylor: three fierce loyalties in one dusty row.

speaker: Narrator
text: Spoiled pages, each wrong in a different and instructive way.

speaker: Narrator
text: Low and wobbly. A girl does not sit in it for pleasure.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to chalk and girls.

speaker: Narrator
text: Retired from shorthand after forty years, she still taps her fingers on every table as if it were one.

speaker: Narrator
text: Forty shorthand exercises, a pot of ink, a cold cup of tea. A pen lies where I put it down to think of Jonathan.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Dear Sir, I beg to acknowledge...' in the fastest hand I have. Somewhere in the pile is a letter to Jonathan I have not dared send.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bradshaw's Guide in four monthly numbers, the Bible, Tennyson, and a Baedeker for places I shall not see.

speaker: Narrator
text: My favourite reading. I could take the 7.15 to Plymouth with my eyes shut and tell you where it stops.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cathedral towers over the chimney-pots. The rooks quarrel about it every evening.

speaker: Narrator
text: Horsehair, and ruthless to the spine. Lucy says it was designed by someone who hated guests.

speaker: Narrator
text: The gas-ring and its kettle. I have boiled a thousand eggs on it and loved none of them.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down the stairs and across the Close.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ten minutes' walk to the station, eight if I do not look at the shop windows.

speaker: Narrator
text: My landlady, who keeps the draper's below and a ledger of every letter that comes to the house.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy, in a travelling dress, with a flush of excitement and a hat-box she has forgotten to unpack.

speaker: Narrator
text: A slanting stand under glass, with a rail for the great books.

speaker: Narrator
text: A standing train: a carriage with a lamp for the dark and hard seats for the honest.

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass grille in a mahogany box. Behind it a young man listens to the whole country ticking.

speaker: Narrator
text: Someone has carved 'Tiverton 14' in the seat, for reasons known to the carver.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lamp that is lit at four every afternoon, even in June.

speaker: Narrator
text: Stamped with the name of a Devon farm and a number I find reassuring.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'To the city and the Close.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A man in a frock-coat who has not been late in nineteen years and does not intend to begin.

speaker: Narrator
text: A young clerk with ink on his cuffs and a faraway look, as if the wires hummed in his teeth.

speaker: Narrator
text: A big man leaning on a barrow, eating a pasty with the concentration of a scholar.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tide-tables, picture post-cards, and a clear space exactly the size of my notebook.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold, with a ship in a bottle on the mantel that Mrs. Westenra thinks is an ornament and the landlord thinks is sacred.

speaker: Narrator
text: Murray's Guide, Mrs. Radcliffe, and a single volume of sermons that has never been opened.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's place. She lies on it and reads the end of novels.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mine, by right of possession.

speaker: Narrator
text: Boats come in by the dozen at four. From here I can count them and make myself no happier.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fourteen steps, of which the ninth complains.

speaker: Narrator
text: Out to the cliff, the churchyard and the sea.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy, rosy from the sea air, with a pencil behind one ear and the post-card of a lighthouse in her hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's mother, in grey silk and a lace cap, enjoying her tea with the air of a woman who has been told not to excite herself.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench of black wood, carved with the initials of four generations and one rude word.

speaker: Narrator
text: It leans toward the sea, as if it wanted to be a sailor too.

speaker: Narrator
text: Broken against the red sky. The sexton says a White Lady is seen in the great window at sunset.

speaker: Narrator
text: A zig-zag path down the cliff toward the pier.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lamp that the harbour-master lights when it pleases him.

speaker: Narrator
text: The road back to our lodgings.

speaker: Narrator
text: An ancient fisherman with a face like a walnut, smoking a pipe nobody has ever seen him light.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two bats out hunting early, turning over my head in tighter and tighter circles. I do not like how they look at me.

speaker: Narrator
text: Charts weighted with a mug, a knife and a sleeping cat.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long brass glass lashed to its stand. It points at nothing at all right now, which is the best sort of target.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stove that is always lit. The tea on it is a legend.

speaker: Narrator
text: Neat coils of spare line, tarred and ready.

speaker: Narrator

text: I take the hammer.

speaker: Narrator
text: The little crucifix I have carried since my ordination to nothing in particular.

speaker: Narrator
text: I put the crucifix in my breast pocket.

speaker: Narrator
text: A globe, worn pale across the Carpathians where my thumb goes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Upstairs to the stove, and my wife.

speaker: Narrator
text: To the Herengracht and the world.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black-edged, it has come while I was in Styria. I know the hand before I turn it over.

speaker: Narrator
text: My wing-chair, with a lamp at its elbow. A man should read bad news sitting down.

speaker: Narrator
text: The bed is turned toward the window so that she can see the canal and the skaters and the boys who do not fall.

speaker: Narrator
text: Blue Delft tiles, a fire of peat and a kettle that has never been allowed to go off the boil.

speaker: Narrator
text: Not a cradle any more; she has put her sewing in it. She will not let the maid move it. I have not asked her to.

speaker: Narrator
text: Half a child's coat, in grey wool, never finished. The needle is still in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Scrubbed pine. A dish of onions, a loaf, a jug of Hollands gin that the doctor does not need to know about.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mine, by the bed, wherever the bed is.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the maid sits when I am at the University.

speaker: Narrator
text: The housekeeper hangs these for the cook-pot and for the winter ague. Mostly for the winter ague.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down the narrow stair to my books.

speaker: Narrator
text: She is thin and very straight against the pillows, and she greets me with the small dry joke she uses instead of complaint.

speaker: Narrator
text: Floured to the elbow. Stout, sixty, and a better judge of the sick than half the Faculty.

speaker: Narrator
text: Number 44, with the brass knocker polished by Mevrouw Bakker.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Faculty's grey arch. 'Veritas', says the keystone, and a hundred and fifty years of pigeons have commented.

speaker: Narrator
text: Under the Latin motto, a smaller notice: 'Silence'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A low door beneath a lantern, and the smell of wax.

speaker: Narrator
text: The coach for the Rhine, the railway and then south, to the Styrian mountains. Arminius's friend, the pastor, has written. I should go, with whatever I can carry.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lit at four in winter, and always a minute late.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bench for watching skaters and not noticing the cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pickled herring, the fuel of the Dutch intellect.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wrapped in three coats, in the way of men who wait out of doors for a living.

speaker: Narrator
text: One of mine. Bright, anxious, and carrying the wrong volume under the right one.

speaker: Narrator
text: In a square hand: 'BELIEVE NOTHING YE CANNOT TEST. DISBELIEVE NOTHING YE HAVE NOT TESTED.' Below, two columns. TESTED: the bite of the rabid dog; the trance under mesmerism in Charcot's wards; blood passed from a sound man to a dying one. UNPROVED: the evil eye; a hanged man's rope as a cure for fever; the ringing of bells to turn the hail.

speaker: Narrator
text: Scarred oak with a brass lamp. A drip of tallow marks the page where I lost my place in 1858 and found a new theory.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plaster skull on a wooden stand, with the sutures painted in. A student has hung a cap on it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Initials carved through two generations, and one drawing I will not describe.

speaker: Narrator
text: The back row. All the best students sit here, and all the worst.

speaker: Narrator
text: The front row, for those who wish to be seen to understand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jars, calipers and a stomach in spirits. I do not say whose.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall iron stove that warms the first row and no one else.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the canal.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall man in a perfect black coat, who has been exactly right in public for thirty years. He holds the key to the rare-book press and the Faculty's good opinion, and I want the first more than the second.

speaker: Narrator
text: A visiting student from London. Earnest, quiet, and clever in the way that frightens his tutors. He has a half-healed scar on the back of his hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: An oak press with a brass lock, kept by the Dean. Inside, behind iron grilles, the books no one wants to be seen reading.

speaker: Narrator
text: Aquinas, Suarez, and a thousand folios of the Fathers. Nobody has taken out Suarez since the Treaty of Utrecht.

speaker: Narrator
text: Boyle, Newton, Leeuwenhoek. A man could be happy here and never need the truth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Voyages to Muscovy, Carpathian tales, Calmet. They are shelved with Natural History, which is about right.

speaker: Narrator
text: A green lamp, an inkstand and a ticket for borrowed books, forty-two of them in the name of one Van Helsing.

speaker: Narrator
text: The constellations in gilded wire, many of them wrongly placed.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three students, asleep, and a fourth pretending to be.

speaker: Narrator
text: Erasmus, who laughed at the Church and loved it all the same.

speaker: Narrator
text: A single steady flame, the only kind a library trusts.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back out into the cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pale as his parchment and twice as dry. He speaks in a whisper, even when the library is empty.

speaker: Narrator
text: Plain stone under a white cloth. A small altar, for a small chapel, kept as though a bishop might arrive.

speaker: Narrator
text: Silver, worn at the arms by generations of lips.

speaker: Narrator
text: Beeswax, honey-sweet, and burning straight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Albs, stoles, corporals and a tin of unleavened bread for the next Mass. Father Pieter has marked the tin: 'Not yet blessed.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Father Pieter nods from the altar. I take the tin of unblessed wafers; they are only flour and water, as yet.

speaker: Narrator
text: A shallow basin with a skin of ice at the edges. Even the holy water is cold in St. Nicholas.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wood worn smooth by the sailors' wives.

speaker: Narrator
text: The sailors' widows' pew. It is always full.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mine, when I come, which is less often than Father Pieter hopes.

speaker: Narrator
text: St. Nicholas and three drowned boys, in lead and blue glass.

speaker: Narrator
text: The canal, and the bells of the Oude Kerk.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty, round, mild. A confessor first, a scholar second, and a very good Latinist whenever there is no one to see.

speaker: Narrator
text: Deaf in the left ear, and fiercely proud of the candle-ends he has saved for forty years.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small church with an onion-spire, whitewashed against the weather and clearly built to be looked at nervously.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Zum Schwarzen Hahn', says the sign: the Black Cock. A lantern burns by the door in daylight.

speaker: Narrator
text: A roofed gate of black timber, hung with dried herbs and a very recent iron nail.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iced over. The women fetch water in pairs and in daylight.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sledge piled with hay and a pitchfork stuck, tines up, in the top of it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Frozen sauerkraut.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Graz, 31 Kilometer.' Somebody has scratched a cross under the 31.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lit well before dusk.

speaker: Narrator
text: The village priest, tall, grey and badly shaved. He has not slept properly in a month, and is ashamed to have written for help.

speaker: Narrator
text: Stooped and strong from forty years of digging. He leans on his spade as though the village might ask him to dig another.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black shawl, black skirt, a white face like a shaved apple. She was eight when the great snow came, and she has not forgotten it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Green tiles, a bench round it, and all the village's feet stretched toward it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Scarred, wine-stained, with a bowl of dumplings going cold because nobody has the heart for them.

speaker: Narrator
text: The wall side. Nobody sits there.

speaker: Narrator
text: Marzen, and a little plum brandy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pewter plates, a Bible, and a very old tarot pack that the landlord claims is for patience.

speaker: Narrator
text: Strings of it over every window. There is more garlic than the soup could ever need.

speaker: Narrator
text: Carved lime-wood, painted, with a fresh sprig of fir behind it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The snow, and the church.

speaker: Narrator
text: A big man with a small voice. He has stopped telling anyone it is late.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sits with his back to the wall and his eyes on the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: Back to the village and the lamps.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'ANNA PFEIFER, WIDOW. DIED 1791, AGED EIGHTY. SHE SLEPT WELL.' The lichen has overgrown the 'well'.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'KATHARINA LINDNER, WIFE AND MOTHER, DIED 1812, AGED NINETEEN, IN THE SPRING AFTER HER WEDDING.' Three iron nails have been driven in a row across the top of the stone. The soil about it is not frozen.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'JOSEF HAUER, 1799. HANGED AT GRAZ FOR SHEEP-STEALING.' Poor wretch. The village has put a cross on him to make him comfortable, and perhaps to keep him down.

speaker: Narrator
text: Worn smooth. Whoever it was is no longer anyone's business.

speaker: Narrator
text: One arm is gone.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small stone with a lamb on it. I look away, then back. Then I look away again.

speaker: Narrator
text: A squat tomb of the Pfeifer family, shut, and clean of snow.

speaker: Narrator
text: A yew older than the church, black and hollow.

speaker: Narrator
text: The sexton's. It will not stay lit beyond the third stone.

speaker: Narrator
text: She wears a wedding-dress gone grey. She has no footprints in the snow, and she has turned her face toward me with great interest.

speaker: Narrator
text: Harker's last stop of civilisation. The landlord's wife presses a crucifix on him.

speaker: Narrator
text: A moonlit mountain road. Wolves howl; blue flames flicker where treasure lies.

speaker: Narrator
text: A vast ruined courtyard under the moon. One great door, no light.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lamp-lit hall where the Count bids him welcome.

speaker: Narrator
text: A comfortable room with a mirror. There is no reflection of the Count in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Books in English on every subject; the Count has studied England thoroughly.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dim chamber on the unexplored side of the castle, where he is forbidden to sleep.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty boxes of earth lie in the old chapel. In one, the Count lies as if dead.

speaker: Narrator
text: Windswept graves above the harbour. Mina's seat overlooks the sea.

speaker: Narrator
text: Our lodgings on the West Cliff: a sitting-room with a view of the sea, and Lucy's mother fussing over her tea-things.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cutaway to Dr. Seward's study at the asylum, where the phonograph waits and Renfield is always near.

speaker: Narrator
text: The churchyard above the harbour. From the seat on the old tomb one sees the whole of Whitby, the Abbey and the grey sea.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fishing boats, nets and the smell of tar. The coastguard hut stands under the cliff, its door padlocked.

speaker: Narrator
text: A snug hut of stove, charts and ropes, smelling of tobacco and paraffin.

speaker: Narrator
text: Broken arches against the sky. The sexton says the White Lady shows herself in the great window at sunset.

speaker: Narrator
text: The whole town stands on the cliff in the howling dark, watching the sea come in.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Russian schooner lies broken on the sand, her sails in rags, her helm still manned by a dead man.

speaker: Narrator
text: Below decks it is dark and stinks of damp earth. Great boxes fill the hold.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two beds side by side, the window looking out on the sea. Lucy sleeps with a faint smile.

speaker: Narrator
text: The fog lamps burn dull orange. Somewhere above, the clock of St. Mary's strikes one.

speaker: Narrator
text: Moonlight on the tombs. On the seat, something white, and something black bending over it.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own room in the asylum: the desk, the phonograph, the case-books. Somewhere below, a patient is counting flies.

speaker: Narrator
text: A whitewashed passage of locked doors. At the end hangs the dispensary cabinet, and at the head of the passage a cell I would rather not open.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bare room with a barred window facing the old house of Carfax. It smells of sugar, dust and something small and dead.

speaker: Narrator
text: Elms, a high wall, and beyond it the ruinous chimneys of Carfax. Sparrows quarrel on the gravel.

speaker: Narrator
text: Keepers' cottages behind the elephant-house. Far off, a wolf is howling in the afternoon.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long, clean ward of white beds and quiet nuns. In the corner bed lies a thin, grey-haired man I cannot recognise, and cannot mistake.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small chapel, candles, a plain altar. Sister Agatha has said it may be done here, at once.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs Westenra's house at Hampstead, quiet as a held breath. A clock ticks too loudly. Upstairs, Lucy sleeps.

speaker: Narrator
text: A girlish room: a white bed, a deep window-seat, curtains stirring where no one has touched them.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lawn, shrubbery, a tool-shed, and the night coming down. Something flaps against the lit windows above.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Westenra vault under the yews. A thin rain. Four men, a Professor, and a very small coffin of silence.

speaker: Narrator
text: Furze, bracken and open sky. The Westminster Gazette speaks of a 'bloofer lady' who walks here after dark and leads small children away.

speaker: Narrator
text: White beds in a long ward. In one of them lies a small child with a bandaged throat.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own study at the asylum: the phonograph, the locked cabinet, and a workbench where I have mended many a lock for the sake of the patients.

speaker: Narrator
text: A modest hotel parlour, a typewriter on a writing-table, a basket of sewing, and two people who have lately been very near to ruin.

speaker: Narrator
text: The house is quiet. White flowers have not yet been cleared from the room where Lucy lay, and the smell of wild garlic still clings to the curtains.

speaker: Narrator
text: A roadside inn on the top of the Heath. A fire, a long table, a landlord who has seen worse doctors than us.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dark lane between hedges. Lamps stand far apart. Somewhere beyond the trees the church of Kingstead keeps its watch.

speaker: Narrator
text: A low stone wall, a lych-gate, a notice board with the plan of the graves, and a sexton's lodge that smells of onions.

speaker: Narrator
text: An avenue of yews, junipers marking the church path, a clump of alders, railed-off tombs ghastly white in the moonlight.

speaker: Narrator
text: A marble vault, damp and sordid. Coffins on shelves, withered flowers, iron gone to rust. Lucy's lead-cased coffin rests at the far end.

speaker: Narrator
text: The doctor's book-lined library at the asylum. The phonograph stands on the desk, and the long table is already set for counsel.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small sunny room off the library. Mina has borrowed a typewriter and pinned the whole sad history to the wall.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bare padded room with one barred window upon the park. Sugar-smears on the sill, a sealed jar of flies on the table.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lawns, a yew-tree and a high stone wall. Beyond the wall, the dark roofs of Carfax.

speaker: Narrator
text: Neglected grounds behind the high wall. The great square house stares with shuttered eyes; the chapel stands apart among the weeds.

speaker: Narrator
text: A damp, ancient chapel. The air is thick with foul earth. Dozens of great boxes lie stacked in the nave.

speaker: Narrator
text: The noise of the City. Hansoms, drays and clerks. Somewhere among these streets the Count has left his trail.

speaker: Narrator
text: A smoky counting-room smelling of horse and ink. A dog-eared ledger lies open on the counter.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cramped court of carts, barrels and washing. The man I seek is said to lodge at Corcoran's.

speaker: Narrator
text: A respectable office with a polished counter and a locked safe. Everything here is discretion and cash.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bedroom behind a thick yellow blind. Gaslight, a locked door, and a cold that does not belong to October.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone-fronted house, high steps, a bow window, a torn 'To Let' board. Within: dust, damp and the smell of old earth.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tumbledown house in a poor street. The windows are boarded; the cellar smells of the grave.

speaker: Narrator
text: A damp, empty house near the river. The last of the boxes lies here.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grey water, tarred hulls and a forest of masts. Somewhere out on the Black Sea a ship called the Czarina Catherine is long overdue.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stuffy private sitting room with a sofa for Mina, a table of telegrams, and a window on the harbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ledgers, brass rails and a clerk who has not yet been told why four Englishmen are so anxious about one ship.

speaker: Narrator
text: A river harbour in the early mist. The Czarina Catherine lies at her moorings, unaccountably arrived.

speaker: Narrator
text: A wet deck, a silent crew and a hold that smells of old earth.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cramped back office, all ledgers and locked boxes. Its owner counts coins with his eyes before his hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: A walled yard in the grey morning. By the wall lies the man who carried the box.

speaker: Narrator
text: The men are asleep. In the sitting room Mina's typewriter clicks softly in the lamplight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Night on the river. The little launch throbs against the current, her electric lamp throwing a white road on the water.

speaker: Narrator
text: Brown water, white spray and a broken keel. The river will carry us no further.

speaker: Narrator
text: A mud road along the right bank, a sky of low snow-cloud, and a long way still to the mountains.

speaker: Narrator
text: A village inn with a fat landlady, a stove, and a great basket being packed with provisions.

speaker: Narrator
text: The road climbs into the pine and the snow. Peasants make the sign against the evil eye as we pass.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fire in the snow, a ring of crumbled Host, and a ruined castle black against the stars.

speaker: Narrator
text: By daylight the castle is only a ruin. The great chapel door has rusted shut.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold, dusty, and silent. Fifty boxes once stood here. Now only the tombs remain.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three tombs. In one lies a woman more radiant than any living, and the room is thick with her will.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two great boulders and a pocket of shelter. From here the whole plain can be seen through the glasses.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white plain, a low red sun, and the leiter-wagon racing the dusk toward the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: The wind has dropped. Where the Count stood, there is nothing but dust.

speaker: Narrator
text: A book-lined room, a boy at play, and a thick bundle of typescript tied with ribbon.

speaker: Narrator
text: The great bed with its faded hangings. The fire is kept high, and the whole room smells of camphor and old paper.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black oak, stag's heads and portraits of Holmwoods who all look as if they had been told bad news.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lawn, limes and the grey flank of the house. The chapel roof shows above the yews, and the Home Wood darkens the hill.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's mother's garden: roses, a lawn that has never seen a weed, and Lucy herself under the arbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A little octagon of white wood and glass at the garden's end. We have taken our tea here for three weeks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ledgers to the ceiling, and a stove which has not been lit since my father last came down these stairs.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cottages of old brick round a pond. The tenants wait outside the Holmwood Arms and do not take off their hats.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black oaks and bracken. Somewhere ahead, a lantern is shuttered, and a wire snare sings in the wind.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold stone, a worn altar and the brasses of my ancestors in the floor. A single bell hangs in the little tower.

speaker: Narrator
text: Steps down into the earth. The air is dry, the lamp-flames lean away from the farther dark.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iron-bound chests of deeds and a desk with a green lamp. The window has been bricked up for a century.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Black Sea port on a bright July morning. Gulls, tar, tarred rope, and a long line of Slovak carriers walking fifty boxes up a gangway as if they were carrying their own coffins.

speaker: Narrator
text: A Russian schooner of no great size, well found and well kept. The boards have been scrubbed white; by the end of the voyage no one will scrub them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bunk, a chart table, a sea-chest and a lamp that swings. Home, for twenty years of voyages, and the only door on board that locks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dark, close and smelling of damp earth and silver sand. Fifty boxes stand lashed in their rows, each the length of a coffin.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black stove, a rack of pans and the cook's whole kingdom in eight square feet. It is the one warm place aboard.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bunks in two tiers, sea-chests, damp oilskins, and holy pictures nailed over every pillow.

speaker: Narrator
text: The foredeck and the bowsprit, wet and narrow, with the anchor cable coiled like a sleeping snake. The fog begins here.

speaker: Narrator
text: The quarterdeck, the binnacle, the barometer in its brass case, and the wheel itself with its worn spokes. A man could stand here forever.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black rafters, a hearth like a cave mouth and a council that has not slept. The banners hang as though the wind outside had tired of them.

speaker: Narrator
text: My father's room, now mine. The bed is too large, the books too many, and the portrait does not like me.

speaker: Narrator
text: Open battlements above the pass. Far off to the east a ridge keeps its own dark, and on it a beacon that should burn does not.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pines, rock and the sound of cartwheels going the wrong way: the hungry are coming up the road as the levy goes down it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hundred fires in a bowl of the hills. Men are cleaning mail, and none of them are talking about home.

speaker: Narrator
text: A broad brown river and reeds as tall as a rider. Water sleeps, the Turks say, and the enemy is sleepless.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black water under a low sky. A ferry-post, a ring of leaning stones and a mountain that seems to have its door open.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stone school under the mountain. The benches are worn, the torches never smoke and nobody here has ever been seen to laugh.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shelves to the vault, chained books and a smell of cold iron and wet paper.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ten seats in a ring, a fire without smoke, and below the floor a sound like a great beast breathing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold stone, old wax, and no light at all but what the eyes themselves seem to give.

speaker: Narrator
text: The little chapel above the crypt. The doors have been left unbarred and the altar candles have burned to stubs.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fine May morning under the cathedral towers. Rooks, cabs, and a flower-seller with the whole of Devon in her basket.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Hawkins's office: deed-boxes to the ceiling, a fire kept up in all weathers, and a quill that has signed more conveyances than the Archbishop.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cool vault under the office where the firm keeps what it cannot bear to throw away.

speaker: Narrator
text: Slates, a globe, a blackboard with a chalk drawing of the Exe, and the faint smell of ink and apples.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two rooms above Mrs. Dunmore's linen-draper's. His father's trunk stands under the window, locked these many years.

speaker: Narrator
text: Where the Harkers lie, in the corner by the yew where the sun comes last.

speaker: Narrator
text: Under the great dome, a hundred readers rustle like a wood in autumn. Somewhere in these catalogues is the whole of Transylvania.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hundreds of feet of sheer stone under the moon, and a window left open on the Count's side. Below, the whole country lies bright and silent.

speaker: Narrator
text: An empty room that is not empty. It smells of old earth, and a heap of gold lies in the corner like rubbish.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down a winding stair, the dead air of an old burial-place. Fifty great boxes of earth stand in the gloom.

speaker: Narrator
text: A goat-track under the stars. Far below, a river; somewhere nearer, wolves and a Szgany fire.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long white ward where the Sisters go about in silence. A bed by the window, and a nun who does not leave it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lime trees, gravel walks and a few patient convalescents in chairs.

speaker: Narrator
text: Small, whitewashed, bright with candles and with a wreath of white roses over the altar.
