speaker: Narrator
text: A white bedroom on the first floor, window open on the lawn. It smells of lavender and of a morning that has not yet decided to be anything but happy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Chintz, a piano nobody plays well, and a vase that is not equal to the occasion. Mamma's workbasket sits where a cat would, if she permitted a cat.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long lawn, a rose arbour and a bench in the shade. Every window of the house is open, and there is a smell of cut grass.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two narrow beds under a sloping ceiling, a window full of sea and a landlady who believes in draughts. We have the best rooms in the Crescent, Mamma says, and the worst stairs.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grass, wind and gulls. The Abbey stands over the town, and below it the old churchyard hangs on to the edge of the cliff by its fingernails.

speaker: Narrator
text: The same cliff, the same seat, and no one else on the whole headland but me and the moon. And a bell somewhere, tolling slowly, that has no business ringing at this hour.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hundred steps down, then a hundred more, between graves and the black water. I do not know how I came to be halfway down.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own room again, with the window open and a smell in it that is not lavender. Someone is always in the chair beside the bed. Tonight it is Dr. Seward, asleep with two fingers on my wrist.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rows of ink-stained desks, a stove, a smell of chalk and wet wool. Somebody has stolen the speech-day prize.

speaker: Narrator
text: A narrow room under the eaves that Miss Hallam lets me use after lessons. One Remington stands under a dust-sheet, and it has not spoken for a year.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two small rooms over a draper's, a gas-ring, a window on the cathedral close and a table piled with shorthand exercises.

speaker: Narrator
text: Steam, porters and the clatter of milk-churns. Everything here runs by the minute, and it is the only place in Exeter where I am entirely at ease.

speaker: Narrator
text: Our lodgings on the West Cliff. Lucy's mother has the best chair and Lucy has the best view; I have the writing table.

speaker: Narrator
text: The seat on the cliff above the harbour, the Abbey black against a red sky, and the gravestones that tell such confident lies.

speaker: Narrator
text: Charts, a brass telescope and a stove that smells of tarred rope.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two beds, one sleeping girl, a curtain that breathes, and the sea saying one long word under the window.

speaker: Narrator
text: Water laps somewhere. Timber creaks. I know this place and I have never been here.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dawn on the home corral. The rail is cut clean through, the remuda is gone, and an old hand sits on an upturned bucket holding his head.

speaker: Narrator
text: Warm, dim and smelling of hay and saddle-soap. One stall stands empty, with a name painted on a board above it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grass to the sky in every direction, a water-hole, and a trail that wants reading before it rains.

speaker: Narrator
text: Slow brown water under leaning trees. Somewhere in the reeds, something is breathing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fire in a hollow, horses on a picket-line, and one white-socked paint mare pulling at her rope.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grass to the horizon, one supply-wagon, and a fire of dung and thistle-stalk. Arthur is cleaning his gun, Seward is writing, and the gaucho is looking at the sky.

speaker: Narrator
text: A moon without a cloud, tall silent grass, and the picketed horses stamping uneasily at nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: The wind has dropped. The grass is bright, and everything wrong lies in it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Padded in grey ticking where the plaster has been mended. A barred window, a cot, a tin tray. Home, of a kind.

speaker: Narrator
text: Seven iron beds, three barred windows, nine lamps and a clock that is wrong in the hour. Everything here is counted by somebody.

speaker: Narrator
text: Carbolic, cigar smoke and a phonograph under a cloth. Somewhere in these case-books I am a column of figures.

speaker: Narrator
text: A black range, a stone sink and the good smell of a kitchen that has no idea what is kept upstairs.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wet gravel under a thin moon, the high old wall and a water-butt. Beyond the wall, the dark mass of Carfax.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold stone, a broken window and the smell of old earth. Someone has been bringing boxes into a holy place.

speaker: Narrator
text: Carbolic, cigar smoke and the faint sweetness of chloral. The phonograph waits on the desk, and the house is quiet in the particular way of a house full of the sleepless.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long day-room with iron beds along the wall, a stopped clock, and the soft, continual sounds of people who talk to themselves.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield's room. Sugar on the table, a jar on the window-sill, and a stillness that is never quite restful.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jars, scales and a locked poison-cupboard. Everything here can cure or kill, depending on a grain.

speaker: Narrator
text: Case-books in rows, copying-presses and a bundle of foreign letters tied with tape.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gravel, a water-butt and a high old wall. Beyond it, the dark mass of Carfax.

speaker: Narrator
text: Books to the ceiling, a skull on the globe, and a lamp that has burned late every night for twenty years.

speaker: Narrator
text: Upstairs, where the stove is kept high and the voices are lowered. The kitchen smells of cloves and onions.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gabled houses lean over the black canal. Skaters on the ice, a barrel-organ, and the bells of the Oude Kerk.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tiered benches, a long blackboard and the smell of chalk and wet wool. The students are early. The Dean is earlier.

speaker: Narrator
text: Alcoves of calf and vellum under green lamps. At the end of the hall, a press of oak with a brass lock: the rare books.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold stone and thin candlelight. Father Pieter keeps the altar plain and the sacristy tidy.

speaker: Narrator
text: A mountain village under snow: low roofs, one inn, a church with an onion-spire. The peasants stop talking as the stranger passes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black beams, a tiled stove, and a long table where nobody wants to sit with their back to the door.

speaker: Narrator
text: Leaning crosses in the snow. The moon shows three old stones at the north wall, and a fourth shadow that is not a stone.

speaker: Narrator
text: The old woman's gift. 'For your mother's sake.' I did not like it, but I took it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Garlic. The peasants ward off evil with it. They must know something.

speaker: Narrator
text: My shorthand journal. The only thing in this place I can still call my own.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small shaving mirror. I saw no reflection of the Count behind me.

speaker: Narrator
text: A key from the Count's own coat. It is heavier than it looks.

speaker: Narrator
text: A good lamp. The castle is dark in places even by day.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sharpened oak. A thing I should not know the use of.

speaker: Narrator
text: A mason's hammer from the chapel.

speaker: Narrator
text: Taken from the Count's own belt. I can hardly believe he did not wake.

speaker: Narrator
text: Golden Tokay. 'Excellent wine', I wrote in my journal.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small brass key. It belongs to some inner door.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's account of the three proposals: a girl in bliss and despair.

speaker: Narrator
text: A large safety-pin. It will fasten a shawl at a throat.

speaker: Narrator
text: The warmest shawl we own. Lucy will need it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The key to the door of the room Lucy and I share.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small iron key on tarred twine.

speaker: Narrator
text: A short iron crowbar.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout lantern that will not blow out.

speaker: Narrator
text: A key of dull brass, from the captain's pocket.

speaker: Narrator
text: First leaf of the log, dated from 6 July to 16 July. Varna, the Bosphorus, the Dardanelles.

speaker: Narrator
text: A leaf dated from 17 July to 28 July. A stranger on deck, the search, the Bay of Biscay.

speaker: Narrator
text: A leaf dated from 29 July to 3 August. Men missing, the mate, the box.

speaker: Narrator
text: The last entry, 4 August, from a bottle in the captain's pocket.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty boxes of earth for Mr. S. F. Billington of 7 The Crescent, forwarded by Hawkins's agents.

speaker: Narrator
text: A string of beads and a small cross, still stiff from the cords that held them to the wheel.

speaker: Narrator
text: From the Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth: 'Mr. Harker has had a sharp attack of brain fever...'

speaker: Narrator
text: A small brass key marked D. It opens the poison cabinet in the ward. Only I, and Hennessey, carry one.

speaker: Narrator
text: Chloral hydrate, in clean white crystal. Dissolved in water it sends a man to sleep. In the wrong dose it sends him a good deal further.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sugar lumps, hidden in a patient's pillow. Sugar attracts flies. Flies are his stock-in-trade.

speaker: Narrator
text: A jam-jar with a muslin lid and forty bluebottles. He counts them aloud every evening.

speaker: Narrator
text: A matchbox in which large spiders have been kept like cattle. He feeds them flies and they grow fat.

speaker: Narrator
text: Columns of figures: so many flies, so many spiders, so many sparrows, in a small, neat, terrible hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Lucy is not well. Come to Hillingham at once. - Arthur.' It was written, I think, by someone who had not slept.

speaker: Narrator
text: A blank post-office telegram form. Every word costs a halfpenny, and an hour may cost a great deal more.

speaker: Narrator
text: My black bag: silver tubing, lancets, a small syringe, carbolic. Everything a transfusion needs but the blood.

speaker: Narrator
text: The housekeeper's key to Lucy's room. A locked door is the one ward that cannot be argued with.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout iron pin from the potting-shed. Dropped through the sash-staples it holds a window against anything but a saw.

speaker: Narrator
text: The shorthand journal from the Castle. Jonathan will not look at it and will not part from it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stick of red wax from Sister Agatha's desk.

speaker: Narrator
text: A length of black ribbon from the sisters' sewing basket.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plain gold ring, found in Jonathan's waistcoat pocket among a few coins. I think it was meant for this.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'He has had a brain fever. He wishes you to know he loves you, and that he is afraid.' - Agatha, Sister of St Joseph.

speaker: Narrator
text: A crumpled paper found against her heart. Her handwriting is neat to the last line, and then it is not.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'An Escaped Wolf': the keeper's tale, cut from the Pall Mall Gazette. A tall, thin man with a beaky nose was admiring the wolf before it escaped.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs Westenra's own salts. They will bring round a faint, but not a drugged girl.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'A Hampstead Mystery': children lured by a beautiful lady, found with small wounds on the throat.

speaker: Narrator
text: My notes on the child's throat: two punctures, a finger-breadth apart, edges white and ragged.

speaker: Narrator
text: Harker's Transylvanian journal in Pitman's shorthand. Few can read it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A new ribbon, still in its blue paper.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan's journal and Mina's own, typed in clean black letters.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bill from Messrs. Chubb for 'one four-lever falling-bolt lock for the Westenra vault, with two keys'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A note in Lucy's hand about sleep-walking and a sore throat.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pawnbroker's ticket: 'One small gold crucifix, 5 shillings'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A blank key of good brass, uncut.

speaker: Narrator
text: A four-lever key cut to the vault's falling lock.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy turnscrew for coffin screws, and for punching into lead.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tiny fret-saw with a blade fine enough for lead.

speaker: Narrator
text: A short candle-end of sperm wax.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucifer matches in a tin box.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lantern with a slide for hiding or showing the light.

speaker: Narrator
text: A ball of grey putty, soft as clay.

speaker: Narrator
text: Putty kneaded with the crumbled Host: a seal against the Un-Dead.

speaker: Narrator
text: A plumber's iron, black with use.

speaker: Narrator
text: The soldering iron, heated cherry-red in the blue flame.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stick of dull grey plumber's solder.

speaker: Narrator
text: My case of surgical knives. The Professor asked for them.

speaker: Narrator
text: Van Helsing's missal, with the prayers for the dead.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dr. Seward's spoken diary, wax cylinders in a stained box. Mina begs to hear them.

speaker: Narrator
text: My husband's shorthand journal from Transylvania, held together by a strap.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own diary and the Dailygraph cuttings about the wreck of the Demeter.

speaker: Narrator
text: Van Helsing's closely written notes on Lucy's death and on the Un-Dead.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rows of tiny figures, pages of flies, spiders and sparrows tallied day by day.

speaker: Narrator
text: Every paper copied in order, in triplicate. The whole case in one pile.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small key, the sort a doctor hides from his own patients.

speaker: Narrator
text: Heavy keys to the gate, the house and the chapel of Carfax, from Mr. Hawkins' papers.

speaker: Narrator
text: A rusty iron key. The chapel lock is old and stubborn.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bright sovereign. In London, a sovereign opens more mouths than a magistrate.

speaker: Narrator
text: A letter over Jonathan's hand and Lord Godalming's seal, pleading our authority.

speaker: Narrator
text: A copy of the carriers' ledger: six boxes to Mile End, six to Bermondsey, nine to Piccadilly.

speaker: Narrator
text: The keys of the Piccadilly house, handed over by the agents with a good deal of reluctance.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bunch of keys dropped as the Count tore through us. Each is labelled in a neat hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gold and Bank of England notes, dropped from his torn coat. He paid in cash for everything.

speaker: Narrator
text: A telegram from Lloyd's: the Czarina Catherine cleared the Thames this morning for Varna.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's notes, in the Professor's hand: darkness, water lapping, creaking wood. A ship. Varna.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur's purse. Money, he says, is the only language every port understands.

speaker: Narrator
text: Van Helsing's field glasses, brass and leather, good for a mile of open ground.

speaker: Narrator
text: A flat grey whetstone from a chandler's stall. Jonathan's kukri has not seen one in a week.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan's Ghoorka knife, edged till it takes a hair from the air.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Czarina Catherine reported entering Galatz at one o'clock to-day.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A thumbed railway guide. Mina has marked the Varna line in pencil.

speaker: Narrator
text: A paper from the Varna shippers to the Captain and the Galatz agent: they may look in the box.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty pounds' worth of earth, consigned to one Immanuel Hildesheim, Burgen-strasse 16, Galatz.

speaker: Narrator
text: A note from Messrs. Mackenzie & Steinkoff asking Hildesheim to be helpful. It carries weight.

speaker: Narrator
text: The box was handed over to one Petrof Skinsky, a Slovak. Signed, with a thumbprint.

speaker: Narrator
text: A slip of rough paper found by Skinsky's wall: a boat, a crew of Slovaks, 'up the river by night'.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's map, pencilled with the Count's likely road through Fundu to the Borgo Pass.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's fair copy of every diary and letter. A thick bundle, still smelling of ink.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small flag. Fly it at Fundu and the villagers will take us for officials.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bright electric lamp for the launch. The boatmen fall to their knees when it shines on them.

speaker: Narrator
text: A basket of bread, cold meat and a flask of soup, packed by a landlady who says nothing about why.

speaker: Narrator
text: Heavy furs. It is a long way to the pass and the snow is coming.

speaker: Narrator
text: Gold-rimmed, folded in the dying Lord's own hand-writing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Foul, steadying, and prescribed.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Do not stay away for fear of us.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Brass, small, worn by a thumb. It opens the writing-desk.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small old ring with a pale stone, in a velvet box.

speaker: Narrator
text: A letter of introduction in my father's handwriting.

speaker: Narrator
text: Blue silk, still faintly smelling of lavender.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arrears, interest, and the name Crowle & Aske.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three wards, heavy as a hymn-book.

speaker: Narrator
text: Heavy, worn smooth. Three rings on a field of grey: the Holmwood arms.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three red seals. The whole estate, pledged.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Do not lie as I did.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A neat sheet: sell the Wood, sell the Green, and say nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Thirty names, some of them only crosses.

speaker: Narrator
text: '50 boxes of earth and silver sand, Varna to Whitby, consigned to Mr. S. F. Billington.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A stamped clearance for the Demeter. The stamp is crooked, which is the best a bribe can do.

speaker: Narrator
text: A beeswax candle from the widow on the quay.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two feet of black iron.

speaker: Narrator
text: The big brass key to the main hatch.

speaker: Narrator
text: The key to my cabin. The only lock on the ship that has never been picked.

speaker: Narrator
text: A string of black beads, worn smooth by a lifetime of prayer.

speaker: Narrator
text: A strong bottle with a stout cork.

speaker: Narrator
text: The last pages of the log of the Demeter, sealed in wax.

speaker: Narrator
text: The men's petition for a double watch, signed in a ring so that no one signs first.

speaker: Narrator
text: A blue knitted cap, wet.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small silver crucifix and a string of worn black beads, carried by the Captain of the Demeter to the last.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dragon coiled round a cross, worn smooth by three generations of princes.

speaker: Narrator
text: My father's medal, silver-gilt. 'O quam misericors est Deus', and on the reverse the dragon biting its own tail.

speaker: Narrator
text: A grey wolf's fang, set in iron and hung on a thong. It does not keep wolves off. It tells them who you are.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iron-headed, ash-hafted, notched on the left. It has killed men on the Danube and it can break a lead seal.

speaker: Narrator
text: The captains of the levy are to assemble at the camp. Unsealed, it is only a clerk's handwriting.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dragon stands up in green wax. The order is the Voivode's now.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'The ford at the new moon. The boyars are divided. The Voivode is young.' Signed with a Turkish cipher and, below, in a hand I know, an R.

speaker: Narrator
text: A length of grey silk, still faintly perfumed with rosemary.

speaker: Narrator
text: A disc of black iron stamped with a wolf's mouth. Open to those who carry it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Black iron, shaped like a wolf's head. The lock it opens is shaped like a mouth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ink that dries at once and looks a year old.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lessons in the speech of beasts and the calling of weather, in a hand like barbed wire.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small silver ring, cut for a hand that never wore it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A green horse-tail on a snapped spear, with a tin crescent.

speaker: Narrator
text: Nine letters in a small upright hand: a large, old, secluded house, with a chapel and a high wall, no neighbours who can overlook it. The Count would also like a pond or well.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Pell's own key to the firm's basement vault.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small japanned key for the black deed-box.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hampstead: a villa among a dozen others, a bandstand in the road. Whitby: a villa on the cliff, overlooked from the church. Purfleet (Carfax): old, walled, with a chapel, a pond like a well, and the lunatic asylum as sole neighbour.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Hawkins's letter of introduction to the Count's agents, with the draft of the deed.

speaker: Narrator
text: A green Museum call-slip, blank.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pen and a small bottle of ink from Mr. Hawkins's desk.

speaker: Narrator
text: Notes on the Carpathians: Saxon, Wallach, Magyar and Szekely; the Szgany; the Evil Eye; the name Dracula.

speaker: Narrator
text: A thin gold ring, worn at the back. My mother's. She wore it for nineteen years.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Jonathan, if you read this I will have been gone a long while. Be a decent man. Be kind to your mother's memory. Write things down.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A ribbon from Mina's hair, red, slightly crumpled, still smelling of her soap.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small black diary bound for the journey; the shorthand pages are still blank.

speaker: Narrator
text: Old coin of five reigns, from the Count's heap.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy iron key on a ring, worn at the bow.

speaker: Narrator
text: A heavy iron poker.

speaker: Narrator
text: A gravedigger's spade, with a splintered haft.

speaker: Narrator
text: A yellowed tooth, picked from the ground where the wolves fell back.

speaker: Narrator
text: A pen lent by the hospital physician.

speaker: Narrator
text: A sheet of the Sisters' writing-paper, thin and cream.

speaker: Narrator
text: My journal, salvaged from the lining of my coat. I do not wish to read it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The torn diary, tied with Mina's ribbon and sealed with the chapel's wax.

speaker: Narrator
text: A single sheet, folded small, addressed 'To my Father and Mother'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A torn black diary bound with a red ribbon and sealed in wax: the account of his captivity, which he vowed never to open 'unless some solemn duty come upon me'.

speaker: Narrator
text: A squat bottle of black ink. Mamma says it is the Admiralty's, borrowed.

speaker: Narrator
text: Good cream paper from Mamma's escritoire. Rather too good for my writing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tiny brass key. It opens the walnut escritoire in the parlour.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Begin with what you see out of the window; then the people in the house; then what you cannot tell anyone else; and last, your love.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Three tall white lilies. The back of the vase.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fistful of small blue flowers. The front of the vase.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lilies behind, the rose between, and a fringe of forget-me-nots in front. It is exactly right.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'I am no hand at speeches. I only want to know whether I might hope, and I shall not mind a plain answer.'

speaker: Narrator
text: 'If I am to be refused, let it be plainly done. I could not bear to be managed, or kept dangling, or laughed at kindly.'

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Say it short, Miss Lucy, and say it to my face. I won't mind either, but I'd mind being talked round.'

speaker: Narrator
text: His mother's ring: a small old band with a pale stone, a little too loose.

speaker: Narrator
text: My father's last letter, written when I was ten, with forget-me-nots pressed in every fold. It still smells faintly of summer.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mina's shorthand notebook: tides, timetables, dreams, and the unanswered questions about Jonathan.

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout steel hairpin that frees jammed type-bars.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fresh, glossy black ribbon for the Remington.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Speech Day Tennyson in green morocco, gilt-edged and recovered.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small iron key from Miss Hallam's chatelaine.

speaker: Narrator
text: A beautifully typed letter, eleven lines with no errors.

speaker: Narrator
text: A typed note from Mr. Hawkins's office: a registered letter for Miss Murray has gone astray on the Bristol line.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan's letter from Bistritz, twelve days late, soft at the corners.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dog-eared almanac. The margin notes: 'Tides run fifty minutes later each day.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A brass plumb-bob on a knotted cord, from the coastguard's lead-line.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall white candle for the bedside table.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Remington's ribbon wound round Mina's Whitby notebook: the two instruments of her gift.

speaker: Narrator
text: A lump of sugar from Maria's tin. Santa Fe would follow me to Mexico for one.

speaker: Narrator
text: A horn of black powder, kept dry.

speaker: Narrator
text: Spent slugs dug out of Wash's target post and tapped into a lump. Good for ten cartridges.

speaker: Narrator
text: A big Mexican spur engraved with a P, lost at the ford by one of Dunning's men.

speaker: Narrator
text: A rustler's brand-changing iron, taken from Dunning's loot chest.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her worn saddle-blanket, soft with years, smelling of her.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Dear Quincey, Seward and I are sailing for Buenos Aires in the spring to hunt on the Pampas. We shall want a man who can shoot. Come, and bring the mare. Your friend, Art.'

speaker: Narrator
text: A stout lantern, dry as a bone. It needs oil.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ten bullet-slugs, freshly cast, still smelling of hot lead.

speaker: Narrator
text: A broad leathery wing, cut from the creature at the lines. Proof for Seward.

speaker: Narrator
text: Tooled Texas leather, bitten once by a spiteful mare on the Brazos. It has carried the great bowie knife through the whole of this story.

speaker: Narrator
text: A bent tin spoon that has seen better dinners. A lever for a loose board.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield's ledger: every fly, spider and sparrow, in a clerk's hand. A sane document about an insane account.

speaker: Narrator
text: A white lump, blue-papered. The bait for the smallest and most numerous of lives.

speaker: Narrator
text: An empty glass jar with a ring of old jam at the lip.

speaker: Narrator
text: A jar of eleven small furious lives, held in a palm.

speaker: Narrator
text: An iron key on a loop of tape marked 'GARDEN'. The spider's, or Hodge's.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small brown bird with a hurt wing, warm in the hand. It weighs nothing, and it weighs everything.

speaker: Narrator
text: A note in Seward's hand: 'Move R. to the quiet wing on Monday. Be gentle.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Dr. Seward's pencil stub. It was meant for case-notes and will do for confessions.

speaker: Narrator
text: A cloth-bound notebook with a faded crest. The last entry is a sparrow, crossed out.

speaker: Narrator
text: The small iron key to the patients' ward.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Pym's winding key. He wants it back.

speaker: Narrator
text: Kept by Hennessey in the one place nobody would look.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hennessey's spare, hidden where a patient would not look.

speaker: Narrator
text: A smooth cylinder of wax for the phonograph.

speaker: Narrator
text: A wax cylinder: the doctor's voice on the night that Purfleet went wrong.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dry grey wool.

speaker: Narrator
text: Soaked, heavy, ready to smother a fire.

speaker: Narrator
text: Twenty grains of chloral in a glass of water. Neither too weak nor too strong.

speaker: Narrator
text: A slip for sixty grains of morphia, in a forged hand, in violet ink.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two columns on every page: what I saw, and what I was told.

speaker: Narrator
text: A small brass key, for the cabinet where Arminius's letters are kept.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three Hungarian letters on the Voivode, the Scholomance and a Styrian village.

speaker: Narrator
text: Cold brass, warm only where the Dean's thumb has held it. Opens the rare-book press.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Before the bread is blessed the hands must be washed; before the hands are washed the priest must be shriven; the Collect is said over the bread, and the pyx is sealed last.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Flour and water, cut thin. Not yet a sacrament.

speaker: Narrator
text: Small, bright and made for a christening. It was not made to be put away.

speaker: Narrator
text: A linen square holding a consecrated Wafer, a child's silver cross and a braid of garlic, bound in red thread.

speaker: Narrator
text: Scarred black leather, brass clasps. Lancets, a stethoscope, a bottle of brandy, and in the lid a pyx of consecrated wafers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Left Munich at 8:35 P.M. The impression I had was that we were leaving the West and entering the East. At the Golden Krone the landlord's wife begged me not to go: it is the eve of St. George's Day. She gave me a crucifix.

speaker: Narrator
text: Four black horses stood where there had been none. A tall driver with a long brown beard and eyes that seemed red in the lamplight. Wolves howled all about us.

speaker: Narrator
text: A tall old man, clean shaven save for a long white moustache, clad in black from head to foot. His hand was as cold as ice. 'Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!' I am not to sleep in any other part of the castle.

speaker: Narrator
text: I was shaving when I felt a hand on my shoulder. I had seen no one come in, and in the glass there was no reflection of him at all. I cut myself. The Count seized my throat - then drew back at the crucifix.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the forbidden part of the castle, in the moonlight, three young women whispered by my couch: 'He is young and strong; there are kisses for us all.' The Count's fury dispersed them. I am a prisoner.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the old chapel I found fifty great boxes of earth. In one of them lay the Count - eyes open, stony, without colour. Not dead and not alive. I took the keys from his belt.

speaker: Narrator
text: With the Count's keys I tried the low iron door beside his box. A stair, worn hollow by feet long turned to dust, led down into the earth. The air was cold and stale, and somewhere far below water dripped. If this castle has a heart, it lies under here.

speaker: Narrator
text: The iron door gave at last under the hammer. Beyond lay a ledge of rock, the wind, and a drop into the black gorge. Across the gap rose the castle's south wall, and in it one window. I knew that window. It was mine. There is no road out this way - only the road I already know.

speaker: Narrator
text: In a vaulted chamber lay a great heap of gold - Roman, British, Austrian, Hungarian, Greek and Turkish coin - under a film of dust. None of it, I noticed, was less than three hundred years old. A man with such a hoard has no need to keep a guest, unless he wants something more.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Szgany are loading the boxes onto wagons. The Count means to go to England. If I can escape, I may warn them. Good-bye, all! Mina!

speaker: Narrator
text: A stair behind the founder's slab goes down beneath the abbey: an undercroft of old monks' graves, cold as a cellar and reeking of something sharp and animal. Someone has been here, and not a monk. The dust is scuffed, and a rag of white lawn hangs from a nail. I think of Lucy's sleeping feet, and how far they have wandered.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy met me at the station and drove me to the Crescent, which looks out over the harbour and the East Cliff and the sea. I have had no letter from Jonathan since the 29th of June. Lucy's mother is sweet, and Lucy is lovelier than ever.

speaker: Narrator
text: Dr. Seward, Mr. Quincey P. Morris and Arthur Holmwood all asked for my hand on the same day. I refused two and accepted one. Why can't a girl marry three men? I am so happy and so wretched at once.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy has refused me, as I feared. I must turn to work. My most interesting case is R. M. Renfield: sanguine, strong, excitable, with a fixed idea that he must eat living things to gain their life.

speaker: Narrator
text: Patient Renfield collects flies, spiders and now a sparrow. 'The blood is the life,' he says. A homicidal maniac of a peculiar kind, perhaps. I will watch him closely, and write down what he wants.

speaker: Narrator
text: The churchyard is the nicest spot in Whitby, with seats to sit on and the sea laid out below. Lucy loves the seat on the suicide's tomb. Old men sit on the benches and talk all day, and the oldest is Mr. Swales.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'It be all lies,' said Mr. Swales of the stones. I think he is the most honest man in Whitby. He tells me the Barguest, the Abbey ghost and the dead are no worse than the living. He is ninety-five.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Swales says one stone, the widow's, for the only son George Canon who fell at Kettleness, is a bigger lie than most, and a clever man would hide something there. Is that the coastguard's spare key?

speaker: Narrator
text: The harbour is full of boats, the quay is full of gossip, and the sky is full of gulls. The coastguard keeps a hut under the cliff with a heavy padlock. The fishermen talk of mares'-tails and bad weather.

speaker: Narrator
text: Officer Dunn keeps his hut in good order: a stove, charts, a tool-chest, a storm lantern and a notice-board. He tells me he has never seen the glass drop like this. There is a desk where I may set out papers.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Spare key kept with the stone of the widow's only son.' That is George Canon's stone in the East Cliff churchyard, whose epitaph Mr. Swales so detests. The coastguard hides his key in a lie.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Abbey is the loveliest ruin in the land. The sexton says the White Lady shows in the great window at sunset. I picked wild roses and found a clean ash bough and a font brimming with rain.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sunset blood-red, mares'-tails across the sky, and a hush on the sea. Then the wind rose, and the waves came over the piers. All the town stands on the cliff in the fog, and the searchlight sweeps the water.

speaker: Narrator
text: A schooner ran between the piers with every sail set and a dead man lashed to the wheel. When the keel struck sand an immense dog sprang from below, bounded up the cliff and was lost in the fog. It made for the churchyard.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Demeter of Varna lies on Tate Hill Pier, her sails in rags. A constable keeps the crowd back. Mr. Billington, to whom she is consigned, is greatly distressed. All the town speaks of the dog and the dead steersman.

speaker: Narrator
text: The constable let me through. A word from Mr. Swales, or from the consignee, is as good as a warrant in Whitby. I shall see the dead captain and the ship.

speaker: Narrator
text: The deck is wet and bare. The wheel is lashed with cords and the dead man's hands are bound over a crucifix. His eyes are shut; his face is quite calm. Whatever he saw, he met it as a man.

speaker: Narrator
text: He fastened the knots with his teeth. In his pocket, a corked bottle and a cabin key; in his hands, a crucifix and a rosary. He wished it known that he was captain, and a Christian, and he did his duty.

speaker: Narrator
text: The hold is full of great boxes of mould, marked for Mr. Billington. One is open, and the earth in it has been lain in. Another has its nails bent out from within. They came from Varna with the ballast.

speaker: Narrator
text: Crew uneasy off Cape Matapan; a tall thin stranger seen; men vanish one by one in fog and storm; the mate stabs the figure and the knife passes through; he opens a box, screams, leaps into the sea. The captain, alone, lashes himself to the wheel.

speaker: Narrator
text: The fifty boxes were consigned to a house called Carfax at Purfleet, bought through Mr. Hawkins. Jonathan's firm! I cannot rid myself of the feeling that Jonathan's long silence and this ship are connected.

speaker: Narrator
text: The captain was buried today, with a hundred boats at the funeral. When we came to Lucy's seat, Mr. Swales was lying there, his neck broken, his face frozen in horror. 'He had been dreading it,' someone said. And the dog...

speaker: Narrator
text: I woke at one in the morning and found Lucy's bed empty. The door was still locked, the key under my pillow, but the window stood open. I took the shawl, a pin and the key, and went out.

speaker: Narrator
text: The fog lamps burn like dull coals. Bare footprints in the wet, a strip of her nightgown on a railing, a watchman who saw her go up the steps toward the churchyard. I must be quick.

speaker: Narrator
text: The moon is full. The clock of St. Mary's has stopped. On the seat I can see something white, and something dark that bends over it.

speaker: Narrator
text: A long, black form leaned over Lucy, and when I called it raised a white face with red, gleaming eyes. Then it was gone, and a great bat wheeled over the churchyard. Lucy sat quite still, breathing hard.

speaker: Narrator
text: I wrapped her in the shawl and fastened it at her throat with a pin, so she should not catch cold. I must have pricked her, for she cried out. Two tiny red spots lay on her skin beneath it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy sleeps all night and wakes weary. Her cheeks are white and her lips colourless. Mrs. Westenra says it is the sea air; I fear it is something else. Those marks on her throat do not heal.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two small punctures with white edges and red rims, a quarter-inch apart. Lucy blames my pin. A pin never made such a mark, and I never pinned her twice. She is growing paler by the day.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Mr. Harker is with us and has had a sharp attack of brain fever. He has been raving of wolves, poison and ghosts, and of things I dare not name. Come to him, if you can; he asks for you.' - Sister Agatha.

speaker: Narrator
text: I faced the great dog under the pier, and it fled up the cliff toward the churchyard. A mastiff was found dead there the next morning, torn open, they say, by some savage thing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Under my own asylum lies the old cellar where my predecessors kept the violent cases: padded stalls, iron staples, a dripping tap. Renfield has no business knowing of it, and yet he spoke of 'the cold dark under the house' only last week. I find I do not like the coincidence.

speaker: Narrator
text: Margin notes in my predecessor's hand: 'Zoophagy - the madman eats lives to gain life. Seen once before, and he spoke of a Master then also.' I read it twice, and wish I had not. Whatever Renfield serves, it has served itself of other minds before his.

speaker: Narrator
text: My patient Renfield is the interest of my days: a life-eater, a zoophagous maniac who collects flies, then spiders, then sparrows. I keep this diary on the phonograph; it records my voice and my doubts alike. Lucy's name keeps surfacing, and Arthur's letters worry me.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own pencilled rule: chloral hydrate, ten grains for a man of nine stone, fifteen for twelve, thirty for a bull. Renfield is nine stone and wasted. Ten grains, then, in water, and no more.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ten grains in clean water, a quiet word, and Renfield went down like a lamb. I do not like how easily he took it. A man who eats lives should resist the needle more.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sugar for flies, flies for spiders, spiders for sparrows, and in time, he asked me, a kitten. Renfield believes that to swallow many lives is to gain life. He calls it 'the blood is the life'. He says 'the Master' is coming.

speaker: Narrator
text: A slat in the wall by the elms was hanging by one nail, and a path through the long grass leads straight to Carfax. I have nailed it fast. Pocock swears it is not the first time.

speaker: Narrator
text: The boy came at four. Arthur's father is dying and Arthur dare not leave him; Lucy is ill, and he trusts me to see her. I go to Hillingham tonight. Renfield is quiet; for that I am grateful and, I admit, a little uneasy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy is bloodless, breathing heavily, and sleeps with her window open. Mrs Westenra says she is much better. I find no disease I can name, and that frightens me more than any I can.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two small punctures on her throat, white-edged and torn, and no fever. Her gums are pale as paper. Whatever drains her is drawing it from outside the body. I cannot do this alone: I will write to the one man who might know, my old teacher Van Helsing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bradshaw: the night boat leaves the Hook of Holland for Harwich and the boat-train reaches Liverpool Street at five minutes past six in the morning. The telegraph closes at eight tonight. A wire sent before then, and Van Helsing can be at Hillingham by breakfast.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sent, before the office shut: 'Come by the night boat from the Hook; boat-train reaches Liverpool Street 6.05; urgent, a matter of life.' The boy ran off through the dusk. I cannot do more tonight.

speaker: Narrator
text: Sister Agatha's letter said he was alive, and weak, and calling for me. I found him in the corner bed, white-haired and looking through me as if I were a window. When at last he knew me, he wept. I will not leave him again.

speaker: Narrator
text: He has given me his journal of the Castle, and begged me never to read it unless some solemn duty demands it. I sealed it with black ribbon and red wax before witnesses, so that neither of us shall be tempted. It is the first thing we have decided together.

speaker: Narrator
text: We were married in the chapel of St Joseph, with Sister Agatha for a witness and an English priest for a voice. I am Mina Harker now. Jonathan does not remember his terror at the altar, but I do: he held my hand as if I were a rope over a pit.

speaker: Narrator
text: He came as the clock struck seven, small, deliberate, with a leather case and a hundredweight of questions. One look at Lucy and he sent for blood. 'Let us not waste time on words, friend John. She needs blood, or she will die this night.'

speaker: Narrator
text: He examined her throat with a lens, her eyes with a candle, and her wrist with his watch. He asked what no physician asks: did she sleep with her window open, did she walk at night, did anything fly at the pane? Then he said: 'Arthur is her lover. His blood first.'

speaker: Narrator
text: He gave me flowers of garlic from Haarlem with the gravity of a priest giving the Host. 'The window. The door. The chimney. And a wreath for her neck, friend John. Do not laugh. It is medicine.' I did not laugh. I was, rather, afraid.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur's blood passed into Lucy and the colour came back to her face as dawn comes to a window. Van Helsing's hands never trembled. He told us afterward: 'Arthur must never know that any hand but his own gave her life. A husband has jealousies even for gifts.'

speaker: Narrator
text: At dawn the wreath lay on the floor, the garlic had been swept from the window-sill, the window itself was ajar. Lucy was white again and could say nothing. She had not rung. She had not stirred, and she does not remember.

speaker: Narrator
text: Garlic petals on the carpet from the bed to the window-seat; her slippers by the sill, wet with dew. Lucy herself undid the wards, asleep, and does not know it. Van Helsing is quite sure it is not her will but another's. We lock the door, pin the window, and watch.

speaker: Narrator
text: I gave my own blood this time. 'You are strong, friend John, and the secret is the more safe in a doctor's arm than a lover's.' The bed swam a little; brandy set it right. Arthur does not know. Lucy sleeps, and for an hour, so did I.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mrs Westenra, whose kindness has done more harm than any wolf, found the flowers 'stuffy' and flung them out, and opened the windows to the dawn. We came back to a room cold as a cellar and a girl whom the night had emptied again. Van Helsing wept, and I saw him do it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Van Helsing gave his own blood, saying only: 'Devils or no devils, we fight him all the same.' He will not say who 'him' is. Lucy's cheek has a little rose in it; Mrs Westenra has promised on her honour to touch nothing in the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: A box of garlic arrives each morning from Haarlem. Lucy eats a little, laughs a little, reads Arthur's letters aloud. Van Helsing sleeps in a chair with a hand on the door. Something flaps at the window each night. He says it is a bat. He does not say it with a smile.

speaker: Narrator
text: At midnight the glass burst inwards, and a great grey wolf was on the bed. We drove it back, and it fled, howling, into the garden. Mrs Westenra rose to see, and her heart stopped at the sight. She fell across her daughter and lay still. Lucy lay under her in a swoon.

speaker: Narrator
text: She is dead. She had not slept since the shutters failed. A woman who had borne so much so lightly was killed by an animal's face at the window. The garlic that might have kept it out she herself had cleared away.

speaker: Narrator
text: The maids lay insensible round the kitchen table, smelling of laudanum, and the decanter on the sideboard was left half-full. Van Helsing sniffed it and said nothing. This was not a drunkard's sleep. Someone wished to be undisturbed in that house.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey Morris came in, rumpled and weather-worn, and held out his arm before we could ask. 'A brave man's blood is the best thing on this earth when a woman is in trouble.' Four men have now given Lucy their blood. She sleeps; I do not.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her breath is slow and snoring; her teeth look longer, the gums have drawn back. Arthur kissed her forehead at Van Helsing's word, and that was all. Between one breath and the next she was dead, and for a moment, lovelier than ever she had been.

speaker: Narrator
text: Van Helsing drew her lip back with a finger. The canine teeth are longer and sharper than any I have seen in a living mouth. 'You have eyes, friend John. Remember this; remember it well.' He would say no more.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's last memorandum was found against her heart: a scrap of a night's fear, 'Arthur, forgive me', in a hand that fails by the end of the page. Van Helsing read it twice and pocketed it. I asked him what it meant, and he answered: 'Another day.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Bilder, keeper of the wolves, says Berserker is the gentlest great beast in the gardens, and that on the night of the storm he went mad, tore at the bars, and was gone by morning. A tall thin man had been watching him that evening, he says, with a hooked nose.

speaker: Narrator
text: The coffin went down an hour ago. The clergyman has gone; the mourners have gone to the carriages; and the Professor has not moved from the vault door. I have never seen a man look so little like a mourner and so much like a sentry.

speaker: Narrator
text: We laid her in the Westenra vault. Arthur wept like a boy; Quincey wept like a man; I did neither, and shall, I think, hereafter. Van Helsing stood at the door and said, 'It is not finished.' I did not ask him what he meant.

speaker: Narrator
text: Beneath Kingstead lie older vaults than the Westenra tomb: lead coffins in niches, a gallery of the long dead. Lucy is not the first this churchyard has held. I look in each niche for the signs: a lid forced, earth fresh, a face too red. Most are only dead. That is not the same as being at peace.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the lower gallery one coffin lid has been prised from within; the splinters point outward. Others hunted here before us, and lost. Their stake lies in the dust, its point stained to the grain. We are not the first to learn what that kind of sleep means, and we need not be the last to pay.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Gazette tells of children lured on the Heath by a 'bloofer lady', found with small throat wounds. Van Helsing went white when he read it, and has said only that I must see for myself. I do not like the look in his face.

speaker: Narrator
text: A HAMPSTEAD MYSTERY. Children have been missing on the Heath and found, after an interval, with small wounds on the throat. They say a 'bloofer lady' enticed them. It is a pretty name for a horrid thing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A nursemaid and a ragged child both speak of a kind lady in white who kisses children on the neck. Children do not invent such tales. I begin to wonder what walks the Heath at night.

speaker: Narrator
text: A red shoe, a thread of fine lawn, a woman's bare footprints, all pointing north to Kingstead. The Professor says the trail is as clear as the Gazette. I see it, and I do not wish to.

speaker: Narrator
text: I saw the child's throat at the North Hospital. Two punctures, a finger apart, white-edged and ragged. I have seen the same on Lucy's neck. There is a doctor in me who says it cannot be, and an observer who says it is.

speaker: Narrator
text: I told Van Helsing it was madness; he did not rebuke me. He asked for belief in things unseen, and said there is a woman in Paddington whose typewriter will do what his words cannot. I am too weary to quarrel.

speaker: Narrator
text: She has the courage of a soldier and the hands of a clerk. She reads her husband's journal and does not weep. If the world is saved, it will be by such women. I ask her only for what she can give.

speaker: Narrator
text: The ribbon was fresh, the keys clean, the shorthand surrendered. By evening the whole of Jonathan's foreign journal lay typed, clear as print. I pray it will convince the doctors, since it has convinced me.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan wept when the Professor told him the journal was true. He has been a different man since: pale but whole. He saw the Count in Piccadilly, and fainted; but now he says he will help to the end.

speaker: Narrator
text: I have read Mina Harker's pages and seen the child's wound. I cannot call it madness any longer. Van Helsing says we shall look into the Westenra tomb. If it is empty, I shall have no more reasons to disbelieve him.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy's papers are in order, Mr. Marquand's work. Among them the undertaker's bill, which gives the make of the vault lock, and a note in her own hand about walking in her sleep. The Professor smiled sadly: 'it is all here.'

speaker: Narrator
text: The little gold cross was stolen by the maid, who is poor and frightened. I redeemed it, and forgave her. A wretch in need is not to be punished; a wretch in power is.

speaker: Narrator
text: I cut a key for a four-lever falling lock by the undertaker's description. An hour of filing at the bench; it fits as if made by Chubb. I feel like a criminal and a physician at once.

speaker: Narrator
text: We dined at Jack Straw's, I with little appetite. The Professor explained his plan and chose the dark path by Hampstead Lane to avoid the patrol. Then, with turnscrew, saw, candle and cross, we set out for Kingstead.

speaker: Narrator
text: We opened the vault by night. The Professor unscrewed the lid, cut through the lead with a tiny saw, and held the candle over the satin. The coffin was empty. I felt as though the ground gave way.

speaker: Narrator
text: We watched from under the yew. A white figure came with a child in her arms. The Professor opened the lantern, and I saw Lucy's face, her mouth wet with blood. She dropped the child and fled into the tomb.

speaker: Narrator
text: We laid the child on a bench under the lamp and hid behind the hedge. The constable found it within minutes, and we slipped home across the Heath. The Professor said nothing, and neither did I.

speaker: Narrator
text: By day we opened the coffin again. Lucy lay sleeping, redder and more beautiful than in death, with fresh blood on her lips and her teeth sharper. The Professor said: 'Now do you believe?' I did.

speaker: Narrator
text: She lay as in sleep, but not at rest. The Professor says she is Un-Dead and that we must fetch Arthur: it is his right, and his burden, to see her released.

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur agreed to come. He was white as paper, but he said that if there was any chance of releasing her, he would take it. Quincey Morris stood beside him, silent and unshakeable.

speaker: Narrator
text: We watched under the alders. The Bloofer Lady came with a child on her arm and called Arthur by name. The Professor held up the golden crucifix, and she fell back, hissing, as if burned.

speaker: Narrator
text: At sunset she rose, with a smile that was not hers. We drove her back with the cross and our hands until she lay helpless. The Professor said, 'Now, friend Arthur, strike.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Arthur set the point above her heart and drove the stake home with three blows. The body arched, screamed, and was still. The Professor read the prayers while the tomb breathed out.

speaker: Narrator
text: We did what remained: the head, the garlic, the lead case soldered shut. The face wore the sweetness of the girl I had loved. Arthur said, 'She smiled at me.' I think she did.

speaker: Narrator
text: We swore on the vault door to hunt down the creature that did this. The Professor asked me for the use of my asylum, and for all the help I could give. It is a hard road, but I shall walk it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Under Carfax chapel lies a cellar of damp dressed stone, older than the house. The boxes above were carried up from here; the drag-marks on the flags are plain. Fifty boxes came to Carfax and only twenty-nine stand in the nave. The rest went out by cart, and carters keep ledgers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Among the straw, half-torn labels in a clerk's hand: 'Carter, Paterson and Co.' - 'Jamaica L...' - 'Piccad...' - 'to be called for'. The twenty-one missing boxes did not vanish. They were ordered, and what is ordered is written down.

speaker: Narrator
text: Below the cellar, a second vault of brick where the damp stands in puddles and the air tastes of copper. If the Count made a bed in England, he made it where no church bell could reach. The cold that rises here is not the cold of stone.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan Harker and his wife arrive at the asylum. He is grey at the temples, and she is brave beyond words. Van Helsing greets them as old friends. At last, one house holds all of those who know.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan has handed Dr. Seward every page of his Transylvanian journal. I am to copy it and everything else. I know of no better use for a typewriter.

speaker: Narrator
text: I unlocked the cabinet with the little key and gave Mrs. Harker the cylinders of my phonograph diary. She wept at Lucy's death, but said she must hear it all.

speaker: Narrator
text: Seward's cylinders typed. Renfield's fits, Lucy's wasting, the night at Hillingham. And a note: Renfield's wildest days fall when the Count is near the house.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan's journal typed. The castle, the Count's boxes of earth, fifty of them in the chapel. And the shipping to Whitby, to London, to Carfax.

speaker: Narrator
text: My Whitby diary typed with the cuttings. A great dog leapt ashore from the Demeter, and Lucy's sleep-walking began the same week.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor's memorandum typed: the Un-Dead cannot rest save in earth sanctified to them. They lie in their boxes by day and walk by night.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield's notebook typed. His columns of flies and sparrows lie in a pattern. They climb and fall with the nights the Count visits.

speaker: Narrator
text: Jonathan's fifty boxes and Mr. Hawkins' deeds for Carfax. The Count sleeps among them in the old chapel next door to the asylum.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield's moods and the Count's visits keep step. He is the Count's pawn, and perhaps the only one who can tell us when the Count is near.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Demeter's cargo of fifty boxes consigned to Billington of Whitby, then by rail to London, then by carrier to Carfax. A road can be followed.

speaker: Narrator
text: The papers are in order. Fifty boxes; the Count must rest in each of them. Destroy their holy sanctuary, and he has nowhere to hide. I told the Professor what I had found.

speaker: Narrator
text: We sat round the long table. Van Helsing told us all that science does not teach, and we, who laughed at it, listened. I never felt so small, nor so resolved.

speaker: Narrator
text: He is strong as twenty. He casts no shadow, no reflection. He cannot enter unless invited. He is powerless at noon, and cannot cross running water save at slack or flood tide. Crucifix, garlic, the Host: these he shuns.

speaker: Narrator
text: They have admitted me to counsel. The Professor says: no more secrets. I felt a great weight lift, and a greater one settle upon my heart.

speaker: Narrator
text: We went through the wall at dusk with the keys in Harker's hand. The house breathed damp. The chapel door took two of us to open. The smell of the earth was ripe.

speaker: Narrator
text: Thousands of rats, eyes like coals, poured from the crypt. Arthur's terriers went in like furies. When the lamps were held high, the swarm broke.

speaker: Narrator
text: We counted twenty-nine boxes, sterilised each with a crumb of the Host. Fifty came from the castle. Twenty-one are elsewhere in London, and the Count knows we are hunting.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mr. Smollet's ledger: six boxes to 197 Chicksand Street, Mile End New Town; six to Jamaica Lane, Bermondsey; the rest nine boxes to a man called Bloxam. A sovereign opens a ledger.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bloxam carried the nine boxes to a stone-fronted house in Piccadilly, bow window, high steps, a white church nearby. An old man with a white moustache lifted a box himself.

speaker: Narrator
text: The house agents confirm: 347 Piccadilly sold for cash to Count de Ville. A word of Lord Godalming's, a letter and a clerk's nerves, and I have the keys.

speaker: Narrator
text: Renfield begged to be released: 'Do not let Him find me.' Not mad then, or not entirely. He feels the Count's attention. I have told Van Helsing.

speaker: Narrator
text: We found Renfield with a broken back and a smashed skull. 'I tried to stop Him. He promised me life, and I was weak.' We are all weak. We are sworn nevertheless.

speaker: Narrator
text: The door burst. Moonlight, mist, and Mina on her knees at the Count's chest, drinking. Jonathan in a stupor. Van Helsing held out the Host. The Count cowered back, and went.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Unclean! Unclean!' The Host burned my forehead like a hot iron. The Professor says the scar will fade when the Count is dead, and not before. I shall wear it as a sign.

speaker: Narrator
text: Eight boxes in the Piccadilly hall, sterilised. Then the front door, and the Count on the threshold. He leapt through us like a cat through rats. His keys and his money fell in the hall.

speaker: Narrator
text: Notes and gold, and the bunch of keys with labels in a neat hand: Mile End, Bermondsey. He is not omnipotent. He bleeds money like any man, and he is afraid of us.

speaker: Narrator
text: Six boxes in a boarded cellar. Arthur's keys turned in the Count's locks. A crumb of the Host on the earth, and the hideous smell was gone.

speaker: Narrator
text: Six more at Jamaica Lane. Forty-nine boxes destroyed. One remains in the Count's hands, and he knows it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I feel him, like a cold wind with a taste. When the sun is rising or setting I seem able to follow him a little way. The Professor says this may be our only road to him.

speaker: Narrator
text: Under the Professor's hand I heard lapping water, creaking wood, a rope taut, the hollow tramp of feet above. Darkness, and cold. I am afraid for what I said.

speaker: Narrator
text: At sunset again: dull ringing of a bell, hawsers, a cry from the deck. 'We are going, we are going.' I could not say where. The Count was close, and aware.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lloyd's reports: the Czarina Catherine cleared the Thames for Varna. A ship, water and wood, an eastbound hawser. He is returning to his own land. We must race him.

speaker: Narrator
text: By rail to Paris and the Orient Express, then Varna. The Count's ship is slow, ours fast. We shall be there first and wait for the box. All of us, save one.

speaker: Narrator
text: They have decided to go and I am not in the plan. 'It is for your safety.' I watched the cab out of sight with Jonathan's face still in my eyes. I do not mean to stay behind.

speaker: Narrator
text: By day the Count's stronghold is only a ruin: fallen merlons, a gate that no longer closes, and a keep rotted open to the snow. But a fire was lit here not two days past, and the cold ashes lead toward the gate. He has not left his house empty. He has left it waiting.

speaker: Narrator
text: Before we left London Mina asked each of us to swear that, if she turned, we would do for her what we did for Lucy. Quincey swore first. Jonathan was to read the Burial Service. We are in God's hands, and we must be steady.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three days by the Orient Express. Mina slept almost the whole way. Now we are at Varna, and the Czarina Catherine has not arrived. Lord Godalming wires Lloyd's daily. We have nothing to do but wait.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor put me in trance. I heard lapping water, rushing by. I heard creaking, as of masts and cordage, and the tramp of feet overhead. I felt a motion under me. The ship is moving, and the ship is not here.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Czarina Catherine was reported passing the Dardanelles on 4 October. Nothing since. A fast steamer would be here already; she is not. Either the sea has her, or she is making for some other port.

speaker: Narrator
text: Van Helsing says the Count knows we are at Varna: he learned it through Mina's mind, and has cut her off. The ship will not come where we wait. We must watch the wires and be ready to run.

speaker: Narrator
text: A telegram from Lloyd's: the Czarina Catherine has entered Galatz at one o'clock. We have been tricked, and by a margin of a day. Mina, the 'train fiend,' says the only train leaves at 6.30 in the morning.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Continental Bradshaw gives one train a day from Varna to Galatz: leaving at half-past six, arriving in the afternoon. Jonathan laughs at me for my 'train fiend' ways, but he is glad of them now.

speaker: Narrator
text: The ship lies in the river harbour, and the box is gone. Captain Donelson says the box was taken ashore at dawn by men acting for a Hildesheim. Our one hope now is to follow the trail before it is cold.

speaker: Narrator
text: A fog went with the ship from the Bay of Biscay to Galatz, and the crew would not touch the long box. The Captain swung a handspike at the mutiny. 'If the Deil did have any luggage aboord the ship, it was nane ither than that.'

speaker: Narrator
text: Immanuel Hildesheim was bought at a fair price and delivered a receipt. The box was handed to a Slovak named Petrof Skinsky. The price was paid by an English note cashed at the bank. Hildesheim hopes we shall not trouble him again.

speaker: Narrator
text: Skinsky was found in St. Peter's churchyard, his throat torn. The priest says wolves; the neighbours say a very tall man. But in his coat was a slip for a boat and a crew of Slovaks, to go up the river by night.

speaker: Narrator
text: By exclusion: not by road, since horses fear him; not by rail, since he must be seen at stations; therefore by water, on the Sereth, then the Bistritza, which is the water that runs by the Borgo Pass. It must be so.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lord Godalming and Jonathan go by steam launch. Quincey and I ride the bank. Van Helsing takes Mina by train and carriage to the Borgo Pass and the castle. Jonathan protested; Mina quieted him. Money brought us a launch, horses and maps in three hours.

speaker: Narrator
text: We steam day and night, overhauling every boat. The Slovaks fall on their knees when our electric lamp strikes them. They say a boat with a great box passed before us, bound up the Bistritza with Szgany at the oars.

speaker: Narrator
text: The launch struck a rock below the rapids and lost her keel plank. We mended her with a spar, a coil of rope and canvas, and lost half a day. Lord Godalming bought horses at a farm above the falls.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey and I have ridden three days along the right bank. At Fundu we heard that the launch went up the Bistritza. Snow threatens; if the road closes we shall take a sledge and go on, Russian fashion. Wolves howl behind us.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor bought a carriage, horses and furs. The landlady packed a great basket and wept. We are truly in the hands of God. I write this to Jonathan, who may never see it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I knew the road at the Pass. Have not my Jonathan travelled it, and written of his travel? I am strangely sleepy all day and wakeful at dusk. The peasants cross themselves at my scar. The Professor watches me and says nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Professor crumbled the Host into a ring around me and the fire. I cannot step out of it, though I long to. The horses scream and cower in the snow. Mist forms in the dark, and three white women are calling me sister.

speaker: Narrator
text: They begged, and laughed, and wept, and held out their arms. 'Come, sister. Come to us.' The Professor held the Host toward them and they could not cross. At dawn they thinned into the snow, and we found the horses dead.

speaker: Narrator
text: By day the castle is only stone. I broke the rusted chapel door with a blacksmith's hammer, and my heart was a stone also. I must not look at the faces in the tombs too long.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the first tomb lay a woman so lovely that I felt the madness of her call. I heard Mina's wail, and the spell broke. Stake, then knife; the dust fell and she was at peace. So with the others. Three souls made free.

speaker: Narrator
text: I laid a piece of Host in the Count's own tomb, which was empty, and made it unclean for him forever. The doors I sealed with the Wafer also. He cannot come home to rest, whatever else he may do.

speaker: Narrator
text: We rested in a hollow between two great stones. The Professor drew a circle around the rock and looked out through the glasses. 'They are racing for the sunset. We may be too late. God's will be done!'

speaker: Narrator
text: We rode to death of some one. The Szgany closed around the wagon. I cut through to the box; Quincey beside me. I swung the kukri at the Count's throat while Quincey's knife went to his heart. Before our eyes he crumbled into dust.

speaker: Narrator
text: Quincey was stabbed in the side and bleeding fast. The setting sun fell on my forehead, and he cried, 'See! The snow is not more stainless than her forehead! The curse has passed away!' He died with a smile. A gallant gentleman.

speaker: Narrator
text: My father has been dying since Candlemas. We have a nurse, a physician and a rug over his knees. He would prefer his spectacles, his cordial, and news from Hillingham, in that order. I have not slept a whole night in a fortnight.

speaker: Narrator
text: He read Mrs. Westenra's telegram with trembling hands and told me to go to Lucy. There is a ring in his desk, a letter, and a key hidden somewhere in the hall. He looked ashamed when he spoke of the key. I did not ask why.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucy in the garden, Mrs. Westenra under her parasol, and Quincey Morris making an elegant exit with the air of a man who has lost a bet and enjoyed it. I had come to propose and my hands were damp.

speaker: Narrator
text: She asked whether the Ring was in good heart. I answered as I did. Whatever I said, she watched my face while I said it, and I knew I would remember her look when I was older.

speaker: Narrator
text: She said yes. I said many foolish things first. She gave me a blue ribbon from her hair, and I have worn it against my watch since, and I think I am the happiest man in England.

speaker: Narrator
text: Three weeks of tea, croquet and Tennyson. I had not known that life could be so light. Lucy cheats at croquet. Mrs. Westenra pretends not to see. Quincey, to his credit, loses at it with great ceremony.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'LORD GODALMING SINKING.' I left Hillingham in the dusk with Lucy's hand in mine until the carriage moved. I did not reach the Ring in time. He had died at four, with Bates beside him, and a window open that he had asked for.

speaker: Narrator
text: I am Lord Godalming. The title sits on my shoulders like a coat cut for a larger man. Bates has wept, Dr. Lenox has not, and Mr. Pennefather has the face of a man bringing me a bill. He is, I think, bringing me a bill.

speaker: Narrator
text: Wilkes keeps the ledgers as another man keeps a conscience: carefully and out of sight. There was a book on his desk with a strap round it. The red ink in it looked less like arithmetic than like a wound.

speaker: Narrator
text: Thirty years' service, and he held the secret for my father for four of them. I could not be angry for more than a minute. He gave me the key to the muniment room, and the knowledge that I would need my father's signet to use it.

speaker: Narrator
text: The tenants did not take off their hats. I did not blame them. Marsh spoke for them, with Mrs. Marsh listening and the miller scowling. They want to see whether the new Lord will do more than inherit.

speaker: Narrator
text: A hind with her throat torn. Three shapes in the dark, and something growling that was not entirely a dog. I will not be afraid in my own wood. I will merely be careful.

speaker: Narrator
text: The bell rang once, though the rope was still, and there was a woman kneeling at the far pew. She was Nan, my nurse. I have decided that the bell was the wind, and that I am not afraid of it.

speaker: Narrator
text: 'Here he rests.' Not the year Sir Hugh fell, but the year his son carried him home. A house which marks its burials as homecomings is a house I do not wish to disgrace.

speaker: Narrator
text: The vault is dry and ordered. My mother is here. He is by her. I stood a long time. The signet was on his hands, as custom says. I took it and I will wear it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I told Marsh the truth: the estate is mortgaged to its roof, and not a cottage will be sold if I can help it. He took off his hat. They have given me thirty names and their promise to stand by me.

speaker: Narrator
text: I broke the seal of silence. My father left a deed and a letter, side by side on the blotter, as though he were waiting for me. He is, in a manner of speaking. I read them standing.

speaker: Narrator
text: A very reasonable man. Sell the Wood, say nothing, be rid of it all by Michaelmas. It is the most comfortable thing anyone has offered me in a month, and I know that is exactly what is wrong with it.

speaker: Narrator
text: I signed. The Wood is gone, the debt is small, and no one spoke of it again. I am a very good Lord Godalming by every measure but one, and that one I do not take out to look at often.

speaker: Narrator
text: I stood on the green and said it all. The village did not cheer; it did something better and went home to count what it could give. I know now that a name can bear a debt but not a lie. I wear the signet in good conscience.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two poachers and a starved wolf, driven out of my grandfather's oaks by a man with a club and a worse temper than he knew he had. Hobbs wept. The tenants will want to hear it from me.

speaker: Narrator
text: 6 July. The quay is loud and the cargo is quiet. Fifty boxes of earth and sand, for a gentleman in Whitby whom no one has met. The freight is paid in full and I am asked no question. I have been twenty years at sea and I do not like a cargo that nobody wants to talk about.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty boxes of earth, silver sand, consigned to Mr. S. F. Billington of Whitby. The papers are clean. The man who ordered it did not come himself, and the Slovaks who loaded it would not look at it. I put the bill in my coat and I say nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: The customs officer found the boxes 'irregular' until I found a silver coin. Then they were perfectly regular. I have been in business long enough to know that this is how the world works, and long enough to hope that it will not always be so.

speaker: Narrator
text: Father Nikolai blessed the ship and gave me a small flask of holy water. 'A cross is better than a pilot,' he said. I do not argue with priests, and on this voyage I am not sure I argue with anyone.

speaker: Narrator
text: At noon we cast off. East wind, fresh. The men sing at the capstan, a little too loudly. Five hands, two mates, the cook, and myself; a good crew who have sailed with me before. I expected nothing, and I am already uneasy.

speaker: Narrator
text: My own cabin, my own lamp, my own cross in the sea-chest. I have kept the log here for twenty years. I shall keep it as long as I can hold a pen.

speaker: Narrator
text: Fifty boxes in five rows. The ship sits lower than clay would make her. I count them twice. It is the same number, and it should be a comfort.

speaker: Narrator
text: The cook is the most superstitious man aboard, and the only one I would trust with the ship. Garlic over the stove, salt on the step. He laughs at me, then crosses himself.

speaker: Narrator
text: The men have nailed more holy pictures over their bunks than a church has walls. I say nothing. A man who prays is a man who has not given up.

speaker: Narrator
text: Glass falling, mares'-tails in the north-west, gulls inland, porpoises running west. The cook, the sky and the needle agree. We reef down before the blow; the men are quicker than I ever saw them. It is good to give orders that make sense.

speaker: Narrator
text: 11 July at dawn entered Bosphorus. Boarded by Turkish Customs officers. Backsheesh. All correct. Under way at 4 p.m. 12 July, through the Dardanelles. More Customs officers. Want us off soon. At dark passed into the Archipelago. I write it exactly, so that it can be checked.

speaker: Narrator
text: 16 July. Petrofsky is missing. He took the larboard watch at eight bells and was relieved by Abramoff, but he never went to his bunk. The men say they expected it. They will say no more than that there is something aboard.

speaker: Narrator
text: 17 July. Olgaren tells me that behind the deck-house, in the rain, he saw a tall, thin man, not like any of the crew, come up the companion-way and go along the deck, and disappear. He followed and found no one, and every hatch closed. I fear that panic may spread.

speaker: Narrator
text: Searched stem to stern with lanterns, all keeping abreast. No man found; only earth spilled from box thirteen to the bows, and Petrofsky's cap. The men are relieved. The mate scowled and said nothing. I did not say what I thought.

speaker: Narrator
text: 24 July. Dmitri is gone. A second man off his watch, and not seen again. The crew have sent me a round robin asking for a double watch. They fear to be alone. The mate is angry. I fear that either he or the men will do some violence.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two men lost since Varna: Petrofsky and Dmitri. Both off watch, neither seen again. I write it exactly. A log does not weep, and neither will I, until I am ashore.

speaker: Narrator
text: I chalk up the watches: Ivan and Bolotin for the first, the mate and myself for the middle, Olgaren and Abramoff for the morning. No man alone. If anything can be done by arithmetic, I have done it.

speaker: Narrator
text: 28 July. Four days in a maelstrom; no sleep for anyone. 29 July: the second mate gone, and only the steersman on deck. 30 July: both watch and helmsman gone. Without second mate, crew in a panic. The mate and I agree to go armed henceforth and wait for any sign of the cause.

speaker: Narrator
text: With the crowbar I opened the box with the bright nails. Black earth, and in it the shape of a man. I have done what I can: it will not be a bed again. But there are forty-nine more, and I am one man.

speaker: Narrator
text: 2 August, midnight. A cry outside my port. The mate heard it too, and ran. No sign of the man on watch. One more gone. I take lantern and club to the hold, where the boxes are moving.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the hold, with a lantern and a cross, I held off the dark until dawn. Whether it was bats, or rats, or the thing that walks on deck, I cannot swear. Something with a white face. Olgaren is gone. God, help me.

speaker: Narrator
text: I have written the last entry, sealed it in a bottle, and kept the cabin key in my pocket. If we are wrecked, mayhap this bottle may be found, and those who find it may understand.

speaker: Narrator
text: 3 August. The mate came on deck as if shot from a gun, his eyes rolling. 'You had better come too, Captain, before it is too late. The sea will save me from Him.' And he leapt overboard. I suppose I know the secret now.

speaker: Narrator
text: The bow is where Olgaren saw It, and where the mate saw It. It is where the fog begins. I stand on the foredeck and I am sure that if I turn my back, it will be behind me.

speaker: Narrator
text: The wheel is the only thing aboard that still obeys. I put my hands where a hundred captains have put theirs, and I decide, quietly, that mine are the last that will.

speaker: Narrator
text: 4 August. I shall tie my hands to the wheel, and along with them I shall tie that which He dare not touch; and then, come good wind or foul, I shall save my soul, and my honour as a captain. God and the Blessed Virgin and the saints help a poor ignorant soul trying to do his duty.

speaker: Narrator
text: My father is two years dead and I am nineteen. The council meets in his hall, in his chair, with his crest on the wall, and not one man here believes I will keep it. Severin burns on the border. They look at me as at a candle, wondering how long before the draught.

speaker: Narrator
text: I sleep here now, or fail to. There is a chest with a dial, a stand of armour, a portrait of a man I could not please, and Ileana by the window. I was a boy in this room. It has since decided I am not.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Order of the Dragon was founded in 1408; my father was invested in 1431. The Order is older than the man. I have been inclined to forget that the men who wear a thing are less than the thing. The chest opened with the older date, the right date. It is a lesson.

speaker: Narrator
text: A dragon in green wax. The levy has been a clerk's wish for a week. In one moment, with my father's ring, it becomes an army. I hope no man ever learns how easily paper becomes blood.

speaker: Narrator
text: Two hundred villagers fed from the army's store. Vlaicu stormed and Stanciu bowed. The men will march on thinner rations, and the village will remember who fed it. I do not know whether I have done wisely. I know it is what I would want done to me.

speaker: Narrator
